title: 快樂王子及其他故事
author: Oscar Wilde 奧斯卡·王爾德
description: 《The Happy Prince and Other Tales》(1888)。王爾德的五篇童話:〈快樂王子〉〈夜鶯與玫瑰〉〈自私的巨人〉〈忠實的朋友〉〈了不起的火箭〉,以詩意而諷刺的筆法寫愛、犧牲與虛榮。英文原文對照廣東話/普通話翻譯。

chapters.title: The Happy Prince 快樂王子

passages.original: HIGH above the city, on a tall column, stood the statue of the Happy Prince. He was gilded all over with thin leaves of fine gold, for eyes he had two bright sapphires, and a large red ruby glowed on his sword-hilt.
passages.vernacular: 高高喺城市上方,一根高柱上,矗立住快樂王子嘅雕像。佢全身貼滿薄薄嘅純金葉子,眼睛係兩顆明亮嘅藍寶石,劍柄上閃耀住一顆巨大嘅紅寶石。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 高高在城市上方,一根高柱上,矗立著快樂王子的雕像。他全身貼滿薄薄的純金葉子,眼睛是兩顆明亮的藍寶石,劍柄上閃耀著一顆巨大的紅寶石。

passages.original: He was very much admired indeed. “He is as beautiful as a weathercock,” remarked one of the Town Councillors who wished to gain a reputation for having artistic tastes; “only not quite so useful,” he added, fearing lest people should think him unpractical, which he really was not.
passages.vernacular: 佢確實好受人欣賞。「佢像風標一樣美麗,」一位想博取懂藝術嘅名聲嘅市議員講;「只係冇咁有用,」佢補充講,怕人家認為佢不切實際,其實佢並唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他確實很受人欣賞。「他像風標一樣美麗,」一位想博取懂藝術的名聲的市議員說;「只是沒那麼有用,」他補充說,怕人家認為他不切實際,其實他並不是。

passages.original: “Why can’t you be like the Happy Prince?” asked a sensible mother of her little boy who was crying for the moon. “The Happy Prince never dreams of crying for anything.”
passages.vernacular: 「你點解唔能夠像快樂王子一樣?」一位明理嘅母親問佢哭住要月亮嘅小男孩。「快樂王子從來唔會夢想為任何事哭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你為什麼不能像快樂王子一樣?」一位明理的母親問她哭著要月亮的小男孩。「快樂王子從來不會夢想為任何事哭。」

passages.original: “I am glad there is some one in the world who is quite happy,” muttered a disappointed man as he gazed at the wonderful statue.
passages.vernacular: 「我好高興世上有一個人係完全快樂嘅,」一個失意嘅人凝視住呢座奇妙嘅雕像時喃喃講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很高興世上有一個人是完全快樂的,」一個失意的人凝視著這座奇妙的雕像時喃喃說。

passages.original: “He looks just like an angel,” said the Charity Children as they came out of the cathedral in their bright scarlet cloaks and their clean white pinafores.
passages.vernacular: 「佢睇起嚟簡直像天使,」慈善學校嘅細路哋穿住鮮豔嘅猩紅色斗篷同乾淨嘅白圍裙從大教堂出嚟時講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他看起來簡直像天使,」慈善學校的孩子們穿著鮮豔的猩紅色斗篷和乾淨的白圍裙從大教堂出來時說。

passages.original: “How do you know?” said the Mathematical Master, “you have never seen one.”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋點知道?」數學老師講,「你哋從冇見過天使。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們怎麼知道?」數學老師說,「你們從沒見過天使。」

passages.original: “Ah! but we have, in our dreams,” answered the children; and the Mathematical Master frowned and looked very severe, for he did not approve of children dreaming.
passages.vernacular: 「啊!但我哋見過,喺夢裡,」細路哋回答;數學老師皺起眉頭,顯得好嚴厲,因為佢不贊成細路做夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!但我們見過,在夢裡,」孩子們回答;數學老師皺起眉頭,顯得很嚴厲,因為他不贊成孩子做夢。

passages.original: One night there flew over the city a little Swallow. His friends had gone away to Egypt six weeks before, but he had stayed behind, for he was in love with the most beautiful Reed. He had met her early in the spring as he was flying down the river after a big yellow moth, and had been so attracted by her slender waist that he had stopped to talk to her.
passages.vernacular: 一天夜裡,一隻小燕子飛過呢座城市。佢嘅朋友哋六個星期前就去咗埃及,但佢留咗下嚟,因為佢愛上咗最美麗嘅蘆葦。佢係早春時節認識佢嘅,當時佢正沿住河追一隻大黃蛾,被佢纖細嘅腰身吸引,就停下嚟同佢講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天夜裡,一隻小燕子飛過這座城市。他的朋友們六個星期前就去了埃及,但他留了下來,因為他愛上了最美麗的蘆葦。他是早春時節認識她的,當時他正沿著河追一隻大黃蛾,被她纖細的腰身吸引,就停下來同她說話。

passages.original: “Shall I love you?” said the Swallow, who liked to come to the point at once, and the Reed made him a low bow. So he flew round and round her, touching the water with his wings, and making silver ripples. This was his courtship, and it lasted all through the summer.
passages.vernacular: 「我可以愛你嗎?」燕子講,佢鍾意一開始就直奔主題,蘆葦向佢深深鞠躬。於是佢繞住佢一圈一圈地飛,翅膀碰到水面,激起銀色嘅漣漪。呢個就係佢嘅求愛,持續咗整個夏天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我可以愛你嗎?」燕子說,他喜歡一開始就直奔主題,蘆葦向他深深鞠躬。於是他繞著她一圈一圈地飛,翅膀碰到水面,激起銀色的漣漪。這就是他的求愛,持續了整個夏天。

passages.original: “It is a ridiculous attachment,” twittered the other Swallows; “she has no money, and far too many relations”; and indeed the river was quite full of Reeds. Then, when the autumn came they all flew away.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係一段荒謬嘅戀情,」其他燕子嘰嘰喳喳地講;「佢冇錢,而且親戚太多」;確實,河裡滿係蘆葦。然後,秋天嚟喇,佢哋都飛走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是一段荒謬的戀情,」其他燕子嘰嘰喳喳地說;「她沒有錢,而且親戚太多」;確實,河裡滿是蘆葦。然後,秋天來了,他們都飛走了。

passages.original: After they had gone he felt lonely, and began to tire of his lady-love. “She has no conversation,” he said, “and I am afraid that she is a coquette, for she is always flirting with the wind.” And certainly, whenever the wind blew, the Reed made the most graceful curtseys. “I admit that she is domestic,” he continued, “but I love travelling, and my wife, consequently, should love travelling also.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋走後,佢感到孤獨,開始厭倦佢嘅情人。「佢唔會講話,」佢講,「我怕佢係個賣弄風情嘅人,因為佢總是同風調情。」確實,每當風吹過,蘆葦就行最優雅嘅屈膝禮。「我承認佢愛家,」佢繼續講,「但我愛旅行,所以我嘅妻子都應該愛旅行。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們走後,他感到孤獨,開始厭倦他的情人。「她不會說話,」他說,「我怕她是個賣弄風情的人,因為她總是同風調情。」確實,每當風吹過,蘆葦就行最優雅的屈膝禮。「我承認她愛家,」他繼續說,「但我愛旅行,所以我的妻子也應該愛旅行。」

passages.original: “Will you come away with me?” he said finally to her; but the Reed shook her head, she was so attached to her home.
passages.vernacular: 「你願意同我走嗎?」佢終於對佢講;但蘆葦搖咗搖頭,佢太依戀佢嘅家喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你願意同我走嗎?」他終於對她說;但蘆葦搖了搖頭,她太依戀她的家了。

passages.original: “You have been trifling with me,” he cried. “I am off to the Pyramids. Good-bye!” and he flew away.
passages.vernacular: 「你一直喺玩弄我,」佢喊道。「我要去金字塔喇。再見!」佢飛走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你一直在玩弄我,」他喊道。「我要去金字塔了。再見!」他飛走了。

passages.original: All day long he flew, and at night-time he arrived at the city. “Where shall I put up?” he said; “I hope the town has made preparations.”
passages.vernacular: 佢飛咗一整天,晚上佢到咗呢座城市。「我喺邊度落腳?」佢講;「我希望呢座城市作咗準備。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他飛了一整天,晚上他到了這座城市。「我在哪裡落腳?」他說;「我希望這座城市作了準備。」

passages.original: Then he saw the statue on the tall column.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢睇到高柱上嘅雕像。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他看到高柱上的雕像。

passages.original: “I will put up there,” he cried; “it is a fine position, with plenty of fresh air.” So he alighted just between the feet of the Happy Prince.
passages.vernacular: 「我就喺嗰度落腳,」佢喊道;「呢個位置好好,空氣新鮮。」於是佢落喺快樂王子嘅雙腳之間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就在那裡落腳,」他喊道;「這個位置很好,空氣新鮮。」於是他落在快樂王子的雙腳之間。

passages.original: “I have a golden bedroom,” he said softly to himself as he looked round, and he prepared to go to sleep; but just as he was putting his head under his wing a large drop of water fell on him. “What a curious thing!” he cried; “there is not a single cloud in the sky, the stars are quite clear and bright, and yet it is raining. The climate in the north of Europe is really dreadful. The Reed used to like the rain, but that was merely her selfishness.”
passages.vernacular: 「我有一間金色嘅臥室,」佢環顧四周,輕輕對自己講,準備瞓覺;但就喺佢把頭藏到翅膀下時,一大滴水落喺佢身上。「真奇怪!」佢喊道;「天上一片雲都冇,星星清晰明亮,不過卻喺下雨。歐洲北部嘅氣候真係可怕。蘆葦以前鍾意雨,但嗰只係佢自私。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有一間金色的臥室,」他環顧四周,輕輕對自己說,準備睡覺;但就在他把頭藏到翅膀下時,一大滴水落在他身上。「真奇怪!」他喊道;「天上一片雲也沒有,星星清晰明亮,可是卻在下雨。歐洲北部的氣候真是可怕。蘆葦以前喜歡雨,但那只是她自私。」

passages.original: Then another drop fell.
passages.vernacular: 然後又掉下一滴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後又掉下一滴。

passages.original: “What is the use of a statue if it cannot keep the rain off?” he said; “I must look for a good chimney-pot,” and he determined to fly away.
passages.vernacular: 「如果雕像唔能夠擋雨,有乜嘢用?」佢講;「我必須找一個好嘅煙囪帽,」佢決定飛走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果雕像不能擋雨,有什麼用?」他說;「我必須找一個好的煙囪帽,」他決定飛走。

passages.original: But before he had opened his wings, a third drop fell, and he looked up, and saw—Ah! what did he see?
passages.vernacular: 但喺佢展開翅膀之前,第三滴落下,佢抬頭一睇,睇到——啊!佢睇到咗乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在他展開翅膀之前,第三滴落下,他抬頭一看,看到——啊!他看到了什麼?

passages.original: The eyes of the Happy Prince were filled with tears, and tears were running down his golden cheeks. His face was so beautiful in the moonlight that the little Swallow was filled with pity.
passages.vernacular: 快樂王子嘅眼睛裡充滿咗淚水,淚水沿住佢嘅金色臉頰流淌。佢嘅臉喺月光下係咁美,小燕子充滿咗憐憫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快樂王子的眼睛裡充滿了淚水,淚水沿著他的金色臉頰流淌。他的臉在月光下是那麼美,小燕子充滿了憐憫。

passages.original: “Who are you?” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「你係邊個?」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是誰?」他說。

passages.original: “I am the Happy Prince.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係快樂王子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是快樂王子。」

passages.original: “Why are you weeping then?” asked the Swallow; “you have quite drenched me.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你點解哭?」燕子問;「你把我淋得全濕喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你為什麼哭?」燕子問;「你把我淋得全濕了。」

passages.original: “When I was alive and had a human heart,” answered the statue, “I did not know what tears were, for I lived in the Palace of Sans-Souci, where sorrow is not allowed to enter. In the daytime I played with my companions in the garden, and in the evening I led the dance in the Great Hall. Round the garden ran a very lofty wall, but I never cared to ask what lay beyond it, everything about me was so beautiful. My courtiers called me the Happy Prince, and happy indeed I was, if pleasure be happiness. So I lived, and so I died. And now that I am dead they have set me up here so high that I can see all the ugliness and all the misery of my city, and though my heart is made of lead yet I cannot chose but weep.”
passages.vernacular: 「我活住、有一顆人類嘅心時,」雕像回答,「我唔知道眼淚係乜嘢,因為我住喺無憂宮,悲傷不許進入嗰度。白天我同我嘅伙伴哋喺花園裡玩,晚上我喺大廳裡領舞。花園周圍有一堵好高嘅圍牆,但我從唔想問牆外係乜嘢,我周圍嘅一切都咁美。我嘅朝臣哋叫我快樂王子,如果快樂就係幸福,我確實係快樂嘅。我就咁樣活住,都咁樣死去。而家我死喇,佢哋把我放喺咁高嘅地方,我可以睇到我嘅城市所有嘅醜陋同所有嘅苦難,雖然我嘅心係鉛做嘅,我都不禁要哭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我活著、有一顆人類的心時,」雕像回答,「我不知道眼淚是什麼,因為我住在無憂宮,悲傷不許進入那裡。白天我同我的伙伴們在花園裡玩,晚上我在大廳裡領舞。花園周圍有一堵很高的圍牆,但我從不想問牆外是什麼,我周圍的一切都那麼美。我的朝臣們叫我快樂王子,如果快樂就是幸福,我確實是快樂的。我就這樣活著,也這樣死去。現在我死了,他們把我放在這麼高的地方,我可以看到我的城市所有的醜陋和所有的苦難,雖然我的心是鉛做的,我也不禁要哭。」

passages.original: “What! is he not solid gold?” said the Swallow to himself. He was too polite to make any personal remarks out loud.
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢!佢唔係純金嘅嗎?」燕子對自己講。佢太有禮貌喇,唔會大聲發表任何針對個人嘅評論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼!他不是純金的嗎?」燕子對自己說。他太有禮貌了,不會大聲發表任何針對個人的評論。

passages.original: “Far away,” continued the statue in a low musical voice, “far away in a little street there is a poor house. One of the windows is open, and through it I can see a woman seated at a table. Her face is thin and worn, and she has coarse, red hands, all pricked by the needle, for she is a seamstress. She is embroidering passion-flowers on a satin gown for the loveliest of the Queen’s maids-of-honour to wear at the next Court-ball. In a bed in the corner of the room her little boy is lying ill. He has a fever, and is asking for oranges. His mother has nothing to give him but river water, so he is crying. Swallow, Swallow, little Swallow, will you not bring her the ruby out of my sword-hilt? My feet are fastened to this pedestal and I cannot move.”
passages.vernacular: 「好遠好遠,」雕像用低沉悅耳嘅聲音繼續講,「好遠嘅一條小街上,有一間窮人嘅房子。其中一扇窗係開住嘅,透過佢我可以睇到一個女人坐喺桌旁。佢嘅臉消瘦憔悴,雙手粗糙發紅,被針扎滿喇,因為佢係個女裁縫。佢喺一件緞子長袍上繡西番蓮,畀王后最可愛嘅宮女喺下次宮廷舞會上穿。房間角落嘅床上躺住佢生病嘅小男孩。佢發燒喇,要橙子食。佢母親只有河水畀佢,所以佢喺哭。燕子,燕子,小燕子,你能唔能夠把我劍柄上嘅紅寶石帶畀佢?我嘅腳被固定喺呢個基座上,我唔能夠動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很遠很遠,」雕像用低沉悅耳的聲音繼續說,「很遠的一條小街上,有一間窮人的房子。其中一扇窗是開著的,透過它我可以看到一個女人坐在桌旁。她的臉消瘦憔悴,雙手粗糙發紅,被針扎滿了,因為她是個女裁縫。她在一件緞子長袍上繡西番蓮,給王后最可愛的宮女在下次宮廷舞會上穿。房間角落的床上躺著她生病的小男孩。他發燒了,要橙子吃。他母親只有河水給他,所以他在哭。燕子,燕子,小燕子,你能不能把我劍柄上的紅寶石帶給她?我的腳被固定在這個基座上,我不能動。」

passages.original: “I am waited for in Egypt,” said the Swallow. “My friends are flying up and down the Nile, and talking to the large lotus-flowers. Soon they will go to sleep in the tomb of the great King. The King is there himself in his painted coffin. He is wrapped in yellow linen, and embalmed with spices. Round his neck is a chain of pale green jade, and his hands are like withered leaves.”
passages.vernacular: 「埃及喺等我,」燕子講。「我嘅朋友哋正在尼羅河上下飛翔,同大蓮花講話。不久佢哋就要喺大王嘅墓裡瞓覺。國王自己就喺嗰度,喺佢彩繪嘅棺材裡。佢裹住黃色嘅亞麻布,用香料防腐。佢脖子上有一條淡綠色嘅玉鏈,佢嘅手像枯葉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「埃及在等我,」燕子說。「我的朋友們正在尼羅河上下飛翔,同大蓮花說話。不久他們就要在大王的墓裡睡覺。國王自己就在那裡,在他彩繪的棺材裡。他裹著黃色的亞麻布,用香料防腐。他脖子上有一條淡綠色的玉鏈,他的手像枯葉。」

passages.original: “Swallow, Swallow, little Swallow,” said the Prince, “will you not stay with me for one night, and be my messenger? The boy is so thirsty, and the mother so sad.”
passages.vernacular: 「燕子,燕子,小燕子,」王子講,「你能唔能夠同我待一晚,做我嘅信使?男孩咁口渴,母親咁悲傷。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「燕子,燕子,小燕子,」王子說,「你能不能和我待一晚,做我的信使?男孩那麼口渴,母親那麼悲傷。」

passages.original: “I don’t think I like boys,” answered the Swallow. “Last summer, when I was staying on the river, there were two rude boys, the miller’s sons, who were always throwing stones at me. They never hit me, of course; we swallows fly far too well for that, and besides, I come of a family famous for its agility; but still, it was a mark of disrespect.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想我不鍾意男孩,」燕子回答。「去年夏天,我住喺河上時,有兩個粗魯嘅男孩,磨坊主嘅兒子,總是向我扔石頭。當然佢哋從冇打中我;我哋燕子飛得太好喇;而且我出身一個以敏捷著稱嘅家族;但無論如何,嗰個係不尊重嘅表示。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我不喜歡男孩,」燕子回答。「去年夏天,我住在河上時,有兩個粗魯的男孩,磨坊主的兒子,總是向我扔石頭。當然他們從沒打中我;我們燕子飛得太好了;而且我出身一個以敏捷著稱的家族;但無論如何,那是不尊重的表示。」

passages.original: But the Happy Prince looked so sad that the little Swallow was sorry. “It is very cold here,” he said; “but I will stay with you for one night, and be your messenger.”
passages.vernacular: 但快樂王子睇起嚟咁悲傷,小燕子覺得抱歉。「呢度好冷,」佢講;「但我會同你待一晚,做你嘅信使。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但快樂王子看起來那麼悲傷,小燕子覺得抱歉。「這裡很冷,」他說;「但我會同你待一晚,做你的信使。」

passages.original: “Thank you, little Swallow,” said the Prince.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你,小燕子,」王子講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你,小燕子,」王子說。

passages.original: So the Swallow picked out the great ruby from the Prince’s sword, and flew away with it in his beak over the roofs of the town.
passages.vernacular: 於是燕子從王子嘅劍上取下大紅寶石,叼喺嘴裡,飛越城市嘅屋頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是燕子從王子的劍上取下大紅寶石,叼在嘴裡,飛越城市的屋頂。

passages.original: He passed by the cathedral tower, where the white marble angels were sculptured. He passed by the palace and heard the sound of dancing. A beautiful girl came out on the balcony with her lover. “How wonderful the stars are,” he said to her, “and how wonderful is the power of love!”
passages.vernacular: 佢經過大教堂塔樓,嗰度雕刻住白色大理石天使。佢經過王宮,聽到舞蹈嘅聲音。一位美麗嘅女孩同佢嘅情人走上陽台。「星星幾咁奇妙,」佢對佢講,「愛嘅力量幾咁奇妙!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他經過大教堂塔樓,那裡雕刻著白色大理石天使。他經過王宮,聽到舞蹈的聲音。一位美麗的女孩同她的情人走上陽台。「星星多麼奇妙,」他對她說,「愛的力量多麼奇妙!」

passages.original: “I hope my dress will be ready in time for the State-ball,” she answered; “I have ordered passion-flowers to be embroidered on it; but the seamstresses are so lazy.”
passages.vernacular: 「我希望我嘅衣服能及時做好參加國宴舞會,」佢回答;「我已經訂咗喺上面繡西番蓮;但女裁縫哋太懶喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望我的衣服能及時做好參加國宴舞會,」她回答;「我已經訂了在上面繡西番蓮;但女裁縫們太懶了。」

passages.original: He passed over the river, and saw the lanterns hanging to the masts of the ships. He passed over the Ghetto, and saw the old Jews bargaining with each other, and weighing out money in copper scales. At last he came to the poor house and looked in. The boy was tossing feverishly on his bed, and the mother had fallen asleep, she was so tired. In he hopped, and laid the great ruby on the table beside the woman’s thimble. Then he flew gently round the bed, fanning the boy’s forehead with his wings. “How cool I feel,” said the boy, “I must be getting better”; and he sank into a delicious slumber.
passages.vernacular: 佢飛過河,睇到船桅上掛住嘅燈籠。佢飛過猶太區,睇到老猶太人互相討價仲價,用銅天平稱錢。最後佢到咗窮人嘅房子,往裡睇。男孩喺床上發燒地翻嚟覆去,母親瞓住喇,佢太累喇。佢跳進去,把大紅寶石放喺桌上女人嘅頂針旁邊。然後佢輕輕繞住床飛,用翅膀為男孩嘅額頭扇風。「我覺得多涼快,」男孩講,「我一定喺好起嚟;」佢沉入咗甜美嘅瞓眠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他飛過河,看到船桅上掛著的燈籠。他飛過猶太區,看到老猶太人互相討價還價,用銅天平稱錢。最後他到了窮人的房子,往裡看。男孩在床上發燒地翻來覆去,母親睡著了,她太累了。他跳進去,把大紅寶石放在桌上女人的頂針旁邊。然後他輕輕繞著床飛,用翅膀為男孩的額頭扇風。「我覺得多涼快,」男孩說,「我一定在好起來;」他沉入了甜美的睡眠。

passages.original: Then the Swallow flew back to the Happy Prince, and told him what he had done. “It is curious,” he remarked, “but I feel quite warm now, although it is so cold.”
passages.vernacular: 然後燕子飛回快樂王子嗰度,告訴佢自己做咗乜嘢。「真奇怪,」佢講,「雖然咁冷,我卻覺得好暖同。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後燕子飛回快樂王子那裡,告訴他自己做了什麼。「真奇怪,」他說,「雖然這麼冷,我卻覺得很暖和。」

passages.original: “That is because you have done a good action,” said the Prince. And the little Swallow began to think, and then he fell asleep. Thinking always made him sleepy.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係因為你做咗一件好事,」王子講。小燕子開始思考,然後瞓住喇。思考總是讓佢想瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是因為你做了一件好事,」王子說。小燕子開始思考,然後睡著了。思考總是讓他想睡覺。

passages.original: When day broke he flew down to the river and had a bath. “What a remarkable phenomenon,” said the Professor of Ornithology as he was passing over the bridge. “A swallow in winter!” And he wrote a long letter about it to the local newspaper. Every one quoted it, it was full of so many words that they could not understand.
passages.vernacular: 天亮時佢飛到河邊洗咗個澡。「幾咁了不起嘅現象,」鳥類學教授經過橋上時講。「冬天裡有一隻燕子!」佢畀當地嘅報紙寫咗一封關於呢個嘅長信。每個人都引用佢,佢充滿咗咁多佢哋睇不懂嘅詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天亮時他飛到河邊洗了個澡。「多麼了不起的現象,」鳥類學教授經過橋上時說。「冬天裡有一隻燕子!」他給當地的報紙寫了一封關於這個的長信。每個人都引用它,它充滿了那麼多他們看不懂的詞。

passages.original: “To-night I go to Egypt,” said the Swallow, and he was in high spirits at the prospect. He visited all the public monuments, and sat a long time on top of the church steeple. Wherever he went the Sparrows chirruped, and said to each other, “What a distinguished stranger!” so he enjoyed himself very much.
passages.vernacular: 「今晚我去埃及,」燕子講,想到呢個前景,佢興高采烈。佢參觀咗所有嘅公共紀念碑,喺教堂尖塔頂上坐咗好久。佢到邊度,麻雀哋都吱吱喳喳,互相講:「幾咁傑出嘅陌生人!」所以佢玩得好開心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今晚我去埃及,」燕子說,想到這個前景,他興高采烈。他參觀了所有的公共紀念碑,在教堂尖塔頂上坐了很久。他到哪裡,麻雀們都吱吱喳喳,互相說:「多麼傑出的陌生人!」所以他玩得很開心。

passages.original: When the moon rose he flew back to the Happy Prince. “Have you any commissions for Egypt?” he cried; “I am just starting.”
passages.vernacular: 月亮升起時佢飛回快樂王子嗰度。「你有乜嘢嘢要我帶去埃及嗎?」佢喊道;「我正要出發。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 月亮升起時他飛回快樂王子那裡。「你有什麼東西要我帶去埃及嗎?」他喊道;「我正要出發。」

passages.original: “Swallow, Swallow, little Swallow,” said the Prince, “will you not stay with me one night longer?”
passages.vernacular: 「燕子,燕子,小燕子,」王子講,「你能唔能夠再同我多待一晚?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「燕子,燕子,小燕子,」王子說,「你能不能再同我多待一晚?」

passages.original: “I am waited for in Egypt,” answered the Swallow. “To-morrow my friends will fly up to the Second Cataract. The river-horse couches there among the bulrushes, and on a great granite throne sits the God Memnon. All night long he watches the stars, and when the morning star shines he utters one cry of joy, and then he is silent. At noon the yellow lions come down to the water’s edge to drink. They have eyes like green beryls, and their roar is louder than the roar of the cataract.”
passages.vernacular: 「埃及喺等我,」燕子回答。「聽日我嘅朋友哋會飛到第二瀑布。河馬躺喺嗰度嘅蒲草叢中,一個巨大嘅花崗岩寶座上坐住門農神。佢整夜睇住星星,晨星閃耀時,佢發出一聲歡呼,然後沉默。中午黃色嘅獅子哋下嚟到水邊飲水。牠哋嘅眼睛像綠色嘅綠柱石,牠哋嘅吼聲比瀑布嘅轟鳴更響。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「埃及在等我,」燕子回答。「明天我的朋友們會飛到第二瀑布。河馬躺在那裡的蒲草叢中,一個巨大的花崗岩寶座上坐著門農神。他整夜看著星星,晨星閃耀時,他發出一聲歡呼,然後沉默。中午黃色的獅子們下來到水邊喝水。牠們的眼睛像綠色的綠柱石,牠們的吼聲比瀑布的轟鳴更響。」

passages.original: “Swallow, Swallow, little Swallow,” said the Prince, “far away across the city I see a young man in a garret. He is leaning over a desk covered with papers, and in a tumbler by his side there is a bunch of withered violets. His hair is brown and crisp, and his lips are red as a pomegranate, and he has large and dreamy eyes. He is trying to finish a play for the Director of the Theatre, but he is too cold to write any more. There is no fire in the grate, and hunger has made him faint.”
passages.vernacular: 「燕子,燕子,小燕子,」王子講,「遠喺城市對面,我睇到一個年輕人喺閣樓裡。佢俯喺一張堆滿紙嘅書桌上,身邊嘅玻璃杯裡有一束枯萎嘅紫羅蘭。佢嘅頭髮係棕色捲曲嘅,嘴唇紅得像石榴,有一雙大而夢幻嘅眼睛。佢正努力為劇院經理寫完一個劇本,但佢冷得再都寫不下去。爐子裡冇火,飢餓讓佢虛弱。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「燕子,燕子,小燕子,」王子說,「遠在城市對面,我看到一個年輕人在閣樓裡。他俯在一張堆滿紙的書桌上,身邊的玻璃杯裡有一束枯萎的紫羅蘭。他的頭髮是棕色捲曲的,嘴唇紅得像石榴,有一雙大而夢幻的眼睛。他正努力為劇院經理寫完一個劇本,但他冷得再也寫不下去。爐子裡沒有火,飢餓讓他虛弱。」

passages.original: “I will wait with you one night longer,” said the Swallow, who really had a good heart. “Shall I take him another ruby?”
passages.vernacular: 「我再同你待一晚,」燕子講,佢真嘅有一顆善良嘅心。「我再帶一顆紅寶石畀佢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我再同你待一晚,」燕子說,他真的有一顆善良的心。「我再帶一顆紅寶石給他嗎?」

passages.original: “Alas! I have no ruby now,” said the Prince; “my eyes are all that I have left. They are made of rare sapphires, which were brought out of India a thousand years ago. Pluck out one of them and take it to him. He will sell it to the jeweller, and buy food and firewood, and finish his play.”
passages.vernacular: 「唉!我而家冇紅寶石喇,」王子講;「我嘅眼睛係我僅剩嘅。佢哋係稀有嘅藍寶石做嘅,係一千年前從印度帶嚟嘅。拔出其中一顆,帶畀佢。佢會賣畀珠寶商,買食物同柴火,完成佢嘅劇本。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「唉!我現在沒有紅寶石了,」王子說;「我的眼睛是我僅剩的。它們是稀有的藍寶石做的,是一千年前從印度帶來的。拔出其中一顆,帶給他。他會賣給珠寶商,買食物和柴火,完成他的劇本。」

passages.original: “Dear Prince,” said the Swallow, “I cannot do that”; and he began to weep.
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅王子,」燕子講,「我唔能夠嗰樣做;」佢開始哭泣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的王子,」燕子說,「我不能那樣做;」他開始哭泣。

passages.original: “Swallow, Swallow, little Swallow,” said the Prince, “do as I command you.”
passages.vernacular: 「燕子,燕子,小燕子,」王子講,「照我嘅命令做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「燕子,燕子,小燕子,」王子說,「照我的命令做。」

passages.original: So the Swallow plucked out the Prince’s eye, and flew away to the student’s garret. It was easy enough to get in, as there was a hole in the roof. Through this he darted, and came into the room. The young man had his head buried in his hands, so he did not hear the flutter of the bird’s wings, and when he looked up he found the beautiful sapphire lying on the withered violets.
passages.vernacular: 於是燕子拔出王子嘅一隻眼睛,飛往學生嘅閣樓。進去好容易,因為屋頂有個洞。佢從呢度飛進,進咗房間。年輕人把頭埋喺手裡,所以冇聽到鳥嘅翅膀拍動聲,佢抬頭時,發現美麗嘅藍寶石躺喺枯萎嘅紫羅蘭上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是燕子拔出王子的一隻眼睛,飛往學生的閣樓。進去很容易,因為屋頂有個洞。他從這裡飛進,進了房間。年輕人把頭埋在手裡,所以沒聽到鳥的翅膀拍動聲,他抬頭時,發現美麗的藍寶石躺在枯萎的紫羅蘭上。

passages.original: “I am beginning to be appreciated,” he cried; “this is from some great admirer. Now I can finish my play,” and he looked quite happy.
passages.vernacular: 「我開始被人賞識喇,」佢喊道;「呢個係某位大仰慕者送嘅。而家我可以完成我嘅劇本喇,」佢睇起嚟好快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我開始被人賞識了,」他喊道;「這是某位大仰慕者送的。現在我可以完成我的劇本了,」他看起來非常快樂。

passages.original: The next day the Swallow flew down to the harbour. He sat on the mast of a large vessel and watched the sailors hauling big chests out of the hold with ropes. “Heave a-hoy!” they shouted as each chest came up. “I am going to Egypt”! cried the Swallow, but nobody minded, and when the moon rose he flew back to the Happy Prince.
passages.vernacular: 第二天燕子飛到港口。佢坐喺一艘大船嘅桅杆上,睇水手哋用繩子把大箱子從船艙拉出嚟。「嗨喲!」每個箱子出嚟時佢哋都喊道。「我要去埃及喇」!燕子喊道,但冇人理會,月亮升起時佢飛回快樂王子嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天燕子飛到港口。他坐在一艘大船的桅杆上,看水手們用繩子把大箱子從船艙拉出來。「嗨喲!」每個箱子出來時他們都喊道。「我要去埃及了」!燕子喊道,但沒有人理會,月亮升起時他飛回快樂王子那裡。

passages.original: “I am come to bid you good-bye,” he cried.
passages.vernacular: 「我嚟向你道別,」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我來向你道別,」他喊道。

passages.original: “Swallow, Swallow, little Swallow,” said the Prince, “will you not stay with me one night longer?”
passages.vernacular: 「燕子,燕子,小燕子,」王子講,「你能唔能夠再同我多待一晚?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「燕子,燕子,小燕子,」王子說,「你能不能再同我多待一晚?」

passages.original: “It is winter,” answered the Swallow, “and the chill snow will soon be here. In Egypt the sun is warm on the green palm-trees, and the crocodiles lie in the mud and look lazily about them. My companions are building a nest in the Temple of Baalbec, and the pink and white doves are watching them, and cooing to each other. Dear Prince, I must leave you, but I will never forget you, and next spring I will bring you back two beautiful jewels in place of those you have given away. The ruby shall be redder than a red rose, and the sapphire shall be as blue as the great sea.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家係冬天,」燕子回答,「寒冷嘅雪好快就要嚟喇。喺埃及,陽光暖暖地照喺綠色嘅棕櫚樹上,鱷魚躺喺泥裡,懶洋洋地四處張望。我嘅同伴哋正在巴勒貝克神廟裡築巢,粉紅色同白色嘅鴿子睇住佢哋,互相咕咕叫。親愛嘅王子,我必須離開你,但我永遠唔會忘記你,明年春天我會畀你帶回兩顆美麗嘅寶石,代替你送出去嘅嗰兩顆。紅寶石會比紅玫瑰更紅,藍寶石會像大海一樣藍。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在是冬天,」燕子回答,「寒冷的雪很快就要來了。在埃及,陽光暖暖地照在綠色的棕櫚樹上,鱷魚躺在泥裡,懶洋洋地四處張望。我的同伴們正在巴勒貝克神廟裡築巢,粉紅色和白色的鴿子看著他們,互相咕咕叫。親愛的王子,我必須離開你,但我永遠不會忘記你,明年春天我會給你帶回兩顆美麗的寶石,代替你送出去的那兩顆。紅寶石會比紅玫瑰更紅,藍寶石會像大海一樣藍。」

passages.original: “In the square below,” said the Happy Prince, “there stands a little match-girl. She has let her matches fall in the gutter, and they are all spoiled. Her father will beat her if she does not bring home some money, and she is crying. She has no shoes or stockings, and her little head is bare. Pluck out my other eye, and give it to her, and her father will not beat her.”
passages.vernacular: 「下面嘅廣場上,」快樂王子講,「站住一個賣火柴嘅小女孩。佢把火柴掉喺水溝裡,全都壞喇。如果佢不帶些錢回家,佢爸爸會打佢,佢喺哭。佢冇鞋子同襪子,小小嘅頭都光住。拔出我嘅另一隻眼睛,畀佢,佢爸爸就唔會打佢喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「下面的廣場上,」快樂王子說,「站著一個賣火柴的小女孩。她把火柴掉在水溝裡,全都壞了。如果她不帶些錢回家,她爸爸會打她,她在哭。她沒有鞋子和襪子,小小的頭也光著。拔出我的另一隻眼睛,給她,她爸爸就不會打她了。」

passages.original: “I will stay with you one night longer,” said the Swallow, “but I cannot pluck out your eye. You would be quite blind then.”
passages.vernacular: 「我再同你待一晚,」燕子講,「但我唔能夠拔你嘅眼睛。嗰樣你就完全瞎喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我再同你待一晚,」燕子說,「但我不能拔你的眼睛。那樣你就完全瞎了。」

passages.original: “Swallow, Swallow, little Swallow,” said the Prince, “do as I command you.”
passages.vernacular: 「燕子,燕子,小燕子,」王子講,「照我嘅命令做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「燕子,燕子,小燕子,」王子說,「照我的命令做。」

passages.original: So he plucked out the Prince’s other eye, and darted down with it. He swooped past the match-girl, and slipped the jewel into the palm of her hand. “What a lovely bit of glass,” cried the little girl; and she ran home, laughing.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢拔出王子嘅另一隻眼睛,帶住佢俯衝下去。佢掠過賣火柴嘅女孩,把寶石塞進佢嘅手掌心。「多可愛嘅一小塊玻璃,」小女孩喊道;佢笑住跑回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他拔出王子的另一隻眼睛,帶著它俯衝下去。他掠過賣火柴的女孩,把寶石塞進她的手掌心。「多可愛的一小塊玻璃,」小女孩喊道;她笑著跑回家。

passages.original: Then the Swallow came back to the Prince. “You are blind now,” he said, “so I will stay with you always.”
passages.vernacular: 然後燕子回到王子嗰度。「你而家瞎喇,」佢講,「所以我要永遠留喺你身邊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後燕子回到王子那裡。「你現在瞎了,」他說,「所以我要永遠留在你身邊。」

passages.original: “No, little Swallow,” said the poor Prince, “you must go away to Egypt.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,小燕子,」可憐嘅王子講,「你必須去埃及。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,小燕子,」可憐的王子說,「你必須去埃及。」

passages.original: “I will stay with you always,” said the Swallow, and he slept at the Prince’s feet.
passages.vernacular: 「我要永遠同你喺一起,」燕子講,佢瞓喺王子嘅腳邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要永遠同你在一起,」燕子說,他睡在王子的腳邊。

passages.original: All the next day he sat on the Prince’s shoulder, and told him stories of what he had seen in strange lands. He told him of the red ibises, who stand in long rows on the banks of the Nile, and catch gold-fish in their beaks; of the Sphinx, who is as old as the world itself, and lives in the desert, and knows everything; of the merchants, who walk slowly by the side of their camels, and carry amber beads in their hands; of the King of the Mountains of the Moon, who is as black as ebony, and worships a large crystal; of the great green snake that sleeps in a palm-tree, and has twenty priests to feed it with honey-cakes; and of the pygmies who sail over a big lake on large flat leaves, and are always at war with the butterflies.
passages.vernacular: 第二天一整天,佢坐喺王子嘅肩膀上,畀佢講佢喺陌生地方見到嘅事。佢畀佢講紅色嘅朱鷺,牠哋排成長隊站喺尼羅河岸邊,用嘴捉金魚;講斯芬克斯,同世界一樣古老,住喺沙漠裡,乜嘢都知道;講商人哋,慢慢走喺佢哋嘅駱駝旁邊,手裡攞住琥珀珠子;講月亮山嘅國王,像烏木一樣黑,崇拜一塊大水晶;講瞓喺棕櫚樹上嘅大綠蛇,有二十個祭司用蜜餅餵牠;講侏儒哋,乘住大片扁平嘅樹葉越過大湖,總是同蝴蝶打仗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天一整天,他坐在王子的肩膀上,給他講他在陌生地方見到的事。他給他講紅色的朱鷺,牠們排成長隊站在尼羅河岸邊,用嘴捉金魚;講斯芬克斯,與世界一樣古老,住在沙漠裡,什麼都知道;講商人們,慢慢走在他們的駱駝旁邊,手裡拿著琥珀珠子;講月亮山的國王,像烏木一樣黑,崇拜一塊大水晶;講睡在棕櫚樹上的大綠蛇,有二十個祭司用蜜餅餵牠;講侏儒們,乘著大片扁平的樹葉越過大湖,總是同蝴蝶打仗。

passages.original: “Dear little Swallow,” said the Prince, “you tell me of marvellous things, but more marvellous than anything is the suffering of men and of women. There is no Mystery so great as Misery. Fly over my city, little Swallow, and tell me what you see there.”
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅小燕子,」王子講,「你畀我講嘅都係奇妙嘅事,但比任何事更奇妙嘅係男人同女人嘅苦難。冇邊個奧祕比苦難更大。飛過我嘅城市,小燕子,告訴我你喺嗰度睇到乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的小燕子,」王子說,「你給我講的都是奇妙的事,但比任何事更奇妙的是男人和女人的苦難。沒有哪個奧祕比苦難更大。飛過我的城市,小燕子,告訴我你在那裡看到什麼。」

passages.original: So the Swallow flew over the great city, and saw the rich making merry in their beautiful houses, while the beggars were sitting at the gates. He flew into dark lanes, and saw the white faces of starving children looking out listlessly at the black streets. Under the archway of a bridge two little boys were lying in one another’s arms to try and keep themselves warm. “How hungry we are!” they said. “You must not lie here,” shouted the Watchman, and they wandered out into the rain.
passages.vernacular: 於是燕子飛過大城市,睇到富人喺佢哋美麗嘅房子裡尋歡作樂,而乞丐坐喺門口。佢飛進黑暗嘅小巷,睇到飢餓嘅細路哋蒼白嘅臉無精打采地望住黑色嘅街道。喺橋拱下,兩個小男孩互相抱住躺住,試圖保暖。「我哋多餓啊!」佢哋講。「你哋不許躺喺呢度,」警衛喊道,佢哋走進咗雨中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是燕子飛過大城市,看到富人在他們美麗的房子裡尋歡作樂,而乞丐坐在門口。他飛進黑暗的小巷,看到飢餓的孩子們蒼白的臉無精打采地望著黑色的街道。在橋拱下,兩個小男孩互相抱著躺著,試圖保暖。「我們多餓啊!」他們說。「你們不許躺在這裡,」警衛喊道,他們走進了雨中。

passages.original: Then he flew back and told the Prince what he had seen.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢飛回去,告訴王子佢睇到嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他飛回去,告訴王子他看到的。

passages.original: “I am covered with fine gold,” said the Prince, “you must take it off, leaf by leaf, and give it to my poor; the living always think that gold can make them happy.”
passages.vernacular: 「我身上蓋住純金,」王子講,「你必須一片一片把佢取下嚟,畀我嘅窮人;活住嘅人總以為黃金能使佢哋快樂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我身上蓋著純金,」王子說,「你必須一片一片把它取下來,給我的窮人;活著的人總以為黃金能使他們快樂。」

passages.original: Leaf after leaf of the fine gold the Swallow picked off, till the Happy Prince looked quite dull and grey. Leaf after leaf of the fine gold he brought to the poor, and the children’s faces grew rosier, and they laughed and played games in the street. “We have bread now!” they cried.
passages.vernacular: 燕子一片又一片地啄下純金葉子,直到快樂王子睇起嚟暗淡灰色。佢一片又一片地把純金帶畀窮人,細路哋嘅臉變得紅潤,佢哋喺街上笑住玩遊戲。「我哋有麵包喇!」佢哋喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 燕子一片又一片地啄下純金葉子,直到快樂王子看起來暗淡灰色。他一片又一片地把純金帶給窮人,孩子們的臉變得紅潤,他們在街上笑著玩遊戲。「我們有麵包了!」他們喊道。

passages.original: Then the snow came, and after the snow came the frost. The streets looked as if they were made of silver, they were so bright and glistening; long icicles like crystal daggers hung down from the eaves of the houses, everybody went about in furs, and the little boys wore scarlet caps and skated on the ice.
passages.vernacular: 然後雪嚟喇,雪後霜嚟喇。街道睇起嚟像銀子做嘅,咁明亮閃爍;長長嘅冰柱像水晶匕首從房子嘅屋簷垂下,每個人都穿住毛皮外出,小男孩哋戴住猩紅色帽子喺冰上滑冰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後雪來了,雪後霜來了。街道看起來像銀子做的,那麼明亮閃爍;長長的冰柱像水晶匕首從房子的屋簷垂下,每個人都穿著毛皮外出,小男孩們戴著猩紅色帽子在冰上滑冰。

passages.original: The poor little Swallow grew colder and colder, but he would not leave the Prince, he loved him too well. He picked up crumbs outside the baker’s door when the baker was not looking and tried to keep himself warm by flapping his wings.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅小燕子越嚟越冷,但佢唔肯離開王子,佢太愛佢喇。佢趁麵包師不注意時喺麵包店門外撿麵包屑,試圖拍動翅膀保持溫暖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的小燕子越來越冷,但他不肯離開王子,他太愛他了。他趁麵包師不注意時在麵包店門外撿麵包屑,試圖拍動翅膀保持溫暖。

passages.original: But at last he knew that he was going to die. He had just strength to fly up to the Prince’s shoulder once more. “Good-bye, dear Prince!” he murmured, “will you let me kiss your hand?”
passages.vernacular: 但最後佢知道自己要死喇。佢剛好有力氣再飛到王子嘅肩膀上。「再見,親愛嘅王子!」佢喃喃講,「你讓我吻你嘅手好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但最後他知道自己要死了。他剛好有力氣再飛到王子的肩膀上。「再見,親愛的王子!」他喃喃說,「你讓我吻你的手好嗎?」

passages.original: “I am glad that you are going to Egypt at last, little Swallow,” said the Prince, “you have stayed too long here; but you must kiss me on the lips, for I love you.”
passages.vernacular: 「我好高興你終於要去埃及喇,小燕子,」王子講,「你喺呢度待得太久喇;但你必須吻我嘅嘴唇,因為我愛你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很高興你終於要去埃及了,小燕子,」王子說,「你在這裡待得太久了;但你必須吻我的嘴唇,因為我愛你。」

passages.original: “It is not to Egypt that I am going,” said the Swallow. “I am going to the House of Death. Death is the brother of Sleep, is he not?”
passages.vernacular: 「我要去嘅唔係埃及,」燕子講。「我要去死亡之家。死亡係瞓眠嘅兄弟,唔係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要去的不是埃及,」燕子說。「我要去死亡之家。死亡是睡眠的兄弟,不是嗎?」

passages.original: And he kissed the Happy Prince on the lips, and fell down dead at his feet.
passages.vernacular: 佢吻咗快樂王子嘅嘴唇,倒喺佢腳下死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他吻了快樂王子的嘴唇,倒在他腳下死了。

passages.original: At that moment a curious crack sounded inside the statue, as if something had broken. The fact is that the leaden heart had snapped right in two. It certainly was a dreadfully hard frost.
passages.vernacular: 就喺嗰一刻,雕像裡面響起一聲奇怪嘅斷裂聲,好像乜嘢嘢破喇。事實係鉛做嘅心完全斷成咗兩半。嗰確實係可怕嘅嚴寒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在那一刻,雕像裡面響起一聲奇怪的斷裂聲,好像什麼東西破了。事實是鉛做的心完全斷成了兩半。那確實是可怕的嚴寒。

passages.original: Early the next morning the Mayor was walking in the square below in company with the Town Councillors. As they passed the column he looked up at the statue: “Dear me! how shabby the Happy Prince looks!” he said.
passages.vernacular: 第二天一早,市長同市議員哋喺下面嘅廣場上散步。佢哋經過柱子時,佢抬頭睇雕像:「天呀!快樂王子睇起嚟幾咁破舊!」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天一早,市長同市議員們在下面的廣場上散步。他們經過柱子時,他抬頭看雕像:「天哪!快樂王子看起來多麼破舊!」他說。

passages.original: “How shabby indeed!” cried the Town Councillors, who always agreed with the Mayor; and they went up to look at it.
passages.vernacular: 「確實幾咁破舊!」市議員哋喊道,佢哋總是同意市長;佢哋走上去睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「確實多麼破舊!」市議員們喊道,他們總是同意市長;他們走上去看。

passages.original: “The ruby has fallen out of his sword, his eyes are gone, and he is golden no longer,” said the Mayor in fact, “he is little better than a beggar!”
passages.vernacular: 「紅寶石從佢嘅劍上掉喇,佢嘅眼睛冇喇,佢唔再係金色嘅,」市長其實係講,「佢比乞丐好不咗多少!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「紅寶石從他的劍上掉了,他的眼睛沒了,他不再是金色的,」市長其實是說,「他比乞丐好不了多少!」

passages.original: “Little better than a beggar,” said the Town Councillors.
passages.vernacular: 「比乞丐好不咗多少,」市議員哋講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「比乞丐好不了多少,」市議員們說。

passages.original: “And here is actually a dead bird at his feet!” continued the Mayor. “We must really issue a proclamation that birds are not to be allowed to die here.” And the Town Clerk made a note of the suggestion.
passages.vernacular: 「呢度佢腳下居然有一隻死鳥!」市長繼續講。「我哋真嘅必須發布一道公告,不許鳥喺呢度死去。」市政書記記下咗呢個建議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這裡他腳下居然有一隻死鳥!」市長繼續說。「我們真的必須發布一道公告,不許鳥在這裡死去。」市政書記記下了這個建議。

passages.original: So they pulled down the statue of the Happy Prince. “As he is no longer beautiful he is no longer useful,” said the Art Professor at the University.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋拆掉咗快樂王子嘅雕像。「既然佢唔再美麗,佢就唔再有用,」大學嘅藝術教授講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們拆掉了快樂王子的雕像。「既然他不再美麗,他就不再有用,」大學的藝術教授說。

passages.original: Then they melted the statue in a furnace, and the Mayor held a meeting of the Corporation to decide what was to be done with the metal. “We must have another statue, of course,” he said, “and it shall be a statue of myself.”
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋把雕像放進熔爐融化喇,市長召開市政會議,決定點樣處理呢啲金屬。「我哋當然必須有另一座雕像,」佢講,「嗰會係我自己嘅雕像。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們把雕像放進熔爐融化了,市長召開市政會議,決定怎樣處理這些金屬。「我們當然必須有另一座雕像,」他說,「那會是我自己的雕像。」

passages.original: “Of myself,” said each of the Town Councillors, and they quarrelled. When I last heard of them they were quarrelling still.
passages.vernacular: 「我自己嘅,」每個市議員都講,佢哋吵咗起嚟。我最後聽到佢哋嘅消息時,佢哋仲喺吵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我自己的,」每個市議員都說,他們吵了起來。我最後聽到他們的消息時,他們還在吵。

passages.original: “What a strange thing!” said the overseer of the workmen at the foundry. “This broken lead heart will not melt in the furnace. We must throw it away.” So they threw it on a dust-heap where the dead Swallow was also lying.
passages.vernacular: 「真奇怪!」鑄造廠嘅工頭講。「呢顆破裂嘅鉛心喺熔爐裡唔會融化。我哋必須把佢扔掉。」於是佢哋把佢扔喺垃圾堆上,死燕子都躺喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真奇怪!」鑄造廠的工頭說。「這顆破裂的鉛心在熔爐裡不會融化。我們必須把它扔掉。」於是他們把它扔在垃圾堆上,死燕子也躺在那裡。

passages.original: “Bring me the two most precious things in the city,” said God to one of His Angels; and the Angel brought Him the leaden heart and the dead bird.
passages.vernacular: 「畀我帶嚟城市裡兩件最珍貴嘅嘢,」上帝對祂嘅一位天使講;天使畀祂帶嚟咗鉛心同死鳥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「給我帶來城市裡兩件最珍貴的東西,」上帝對祂的一位天使說;天使給祂帶來了鉛心和死鳥。

passages.original: “You have rightly chosen,” said God, “for in my garden of Paradise this little bird shall sing for evermore, and in my city of gold the Happy Prince shall praise me.”
passages.vernacular: 「你選得對,」上帝講,「因為喺我天堂嘅花園裡,呢隻小鳥將永遠歌唱,喺我嘅黃金之城裡,快樂王子將讚美我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你選得對,」上帝說,「因為在我天堂的花園裡,這隻小鳥將永遠歌唱,在我的黃金之城裡,快樂王子將讚美我。」

chapters.title: The Nightingale and the Rose 夜鶯與玫瑰

passages.original: “SHE said that she would dance with me if I brought her red roses,” cried the young Student; “but in all my garden there is no red rose.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢講如果我畀佢帶紅玫瑰,佢就同我跳舞,」年輕嘅學生喊道;「但我整個花園裡冇一朵紅玫瑰。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她說如果我給她帶紅玫瑰,她就同我跳舞,」年輕的學生喊道;「但我整個花園裡沒有一朵紅玫瑰。」

passages.original: From her nest in the holm-oak tree the Nightingale heard him, and she looked out through the leaves, and wondered.
passages.vernacular: 夜鶯喺佢嘅冬青櫟樹巢裡聽到咗佢,佢透過葉子向外睇,感到奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夜鶯在她的冬青櫟樹巢裡聽到了他,她透過葉子向外看,感到奇怪。

passages.original: “No red rose in all my garden!” he cried, and his beautiful eyes filled with tears. “Ah, on what little things does happiness depend! I have read all that the wise men have written, and all the secrets of philosophy are mine, yet for want of a red rose is my life made wretched.”
passages.vernacular: 「我整個花園裡冇紅玫瑰!」佢喊道,美麗嘅眼睛裡充滿淚水。「啊,幸福幾咁依賴小事!智者寫下嘅一切我都讀過,哲學嘅所有秘密都屬於我,然而因為缺一朵紅玫瑰,我嘅生命卻變得悲慘。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我整個花園裡沒有紅玫瑰!」他喊道,美麗的眼睛裡充滿淚水。「啊,幸福多麼依賴小事!智者寫下的一切我都讀過,哲學的所有秘密都屬於我,然而因為缺一朵紅玫瑰,我的生命卻變得悲慘。」

passages.original: “Here at last is a true lover,” said the Nightingale. “Night after night have I sung of him, though I knew him not: night after night have I told his story to the stars, and now I see him. His hair is dark as the hyacinth-blossom, and his lips are red as the rose of his desire; but passion has made his face like pale ivory, and sorrow has set her seal upon his brow.”
passages.vernacular: 「終於有一個真正嘅情人喇,」夜鶯講。「夜復一夜我為佢歌唱,雖然我不認識佢:夜復一夜我把佢嘅故事講畀星星聽,而家我睇到佢喇。佢嘅頭髮黑如風信子花,嘴唇紅如佢渴望嘅玫瑰;但激情使佢嘅臉像淡淡嘅象牙,悲傷喺佢眉頭蓋上咗印。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「終於有一個真正的情人了,」夜鶯說。「夜復一夜我為他歌唱,雖然我不認識他:夜復一夜我把他的故事講給星星聽,現在我看到他了。他的頭髮黑如風信子花,嘴唇紅如他渴望的玫瑰;但激情使他的臉像淡淡的象牙,悲傷在他眉頭蓋上了印。」

passages.original: “The Prince gives a ball to-morrow night,” murmured the young Student, “and my love will be of the company. If I bring her a red rose she will dance with me till dawn. If I bring her a red rose, I shall hold her in my arms, and she will lean her head upon my shoulder, and her hand will be clasped in mine. But there is no red rose in my garden, so I shall sit lonely, and she will pass me by. She will have no heed of me, and my heart will break.”
passages.vernacular: 「王子明晚舉行舞會,」年輕嘅學生喃喃講,「我嘅愛人會喺賓客之中。如果我畀佢帶一朵紅玫瑰,佢會同我跳舞到天亮。如果我畀佢帶一朵紅玫瑰,我會把佢擁喺懷裡,佢會把頭靠喺我肩上,佢嘅手會握喺我嘅手裡。但我嘅花園裡冇紅玫瑰,所以我會孤獨地坐住,佢會從我身邊經過。佢唔會理會我,我嘅心會碎。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「王子明晚舉行舞會,」年輕的學生喃喃說,「我的愛人會在賓客之中。如果我給她帶一朵紅玫瑰,她會同我跳舞到天亮。如果我給她帶一朵紅玫瑰,我會把她擁在懷裡,她會把頭靠在我肩上,她的手會握在我的手裡。但我的花園裡沒有紅玫瑰,所以我會孤獨地坐著,她會從我身邊經過。她不會理會我,我的心會碎。」

passages.original: “Here indeed is the true lover,” said the Nightingale. “What I sing of, he suffers—what is joy to me, to him is pain. Surely Love is a wonderful thing. It is more precious than emeralds, and dearer than fine opals. Pearls and pomegranates cannot buy it, nor is it set forth in the marketplace. It may not be purchased of the merchants, nor can it be weighed out in the balance for gold.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢確實係一個真正嘅情人,」夜鶯講。「我歌唱嘅,佢喺受苦——對我係歡樂嘅,對佢係痛苦。愛確實係奇妙嘅嘢。佢比翡翠更珍貴,比上等蛋白石更可貴。珍珠同石榴買唔到佢,佢都不喺市場上陳列。商人嗰度買唔到佢,都唔能夠喺天平上用黃金稱量。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這確實是一個真正的情人,」夜鶯說。「我歌唱的,他在受苦——對我是歡樂的,對他是痛苦。愛確實是奇妙的東西。它比翡翠更珍貴,比上等蛋白石更可貴。珍珠和石榴買不到它,它也不在市場上陳列。商人那裡買不到它,也不能在天平上用黃金稱量。」

passages.original: “The musicians will sit in their gallery,” said the young Student, “and play upon their stringed instruments, and my love will dance to the sound of the harp and the violin. She will dance so lightly that her feet will not touch the floor, and the courtiers in their gay dresses will throng round her. But with me she will not dance, for I have no red rose to give her”; and he flung himself down on the grass, and buried his face in his hands, and wept.
passages.vernacular: 「樂師哋會坐喺佢哋嘅樓座裡,」年輕嘅學生講,「彈奏佢哋嘅弦樂器,我嘅愛人會隨住豎琴同小提琴嘅聲音跳舞。佢會跳得咁輕盈,腳唔會碰到地板,穿住鮮豔衣服嘅朝臣哋會圍住佢。但佢唔會同我跳舞,因為我冇紅玫瑰畀佢」;佢撲倒喺草地上,把臉埋喺手裡,哭咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「樂師們會坐在他們的樓座裡,」年輕的學生說,「彈奏他們的弦樂器,我的愛人會隨著豎琴和小提琴的聲音跳舞。她會跳得那麼輕盈,腳不會碰到地板,穿著鮮豔衣服的朝臣們會圍著她。但她不會同我跳舞,因為我沒有紅玫瑰給她」;他撲倒在草地上,把臉埋在手裡,哭了起來。

passages.original: “Why is he weeping?” asked a little Green Lizard, as he ran past him with his tail in the air.
passages.vernacular: 「佢點解哭?」一隻小綠蜥蜴問,佢翹住尾巴從佢旁邊跑過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他為什麼哭?」一隻小綠蜥蜴問,他翹著尾巴從他旁邊跑過。

passages.original: “Why, indeed?” said a Butterfly, who was fluttering about after a sunbeam.
passages.vernacular: 「點解呢?」一隻追住陽光飛舞嘅蝴蝶講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼呢?」一隻追著陽光飛舞的蝴蝶說。

passages.original: “Why, indeed?” whispered a Daisy to his neighbour, in a soft, low voice.
passages.vernacular: 「點解呢?」一朵雛菊用柔和低沉嘅聲音對鄰居低語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼呢?」一朵雛菊用柔和低沉的聲音對鄰居低語。

passages.original: “He is weeping for a red rose,” said the Nightingale.
passages.vernacular: 「佢喺為一朵紅玫瑰哭,」夜鶯講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他在為一朵紅玫瑰哭,」夜鶯說。

passages.original: “For a red rose?” they cried; “how very ridiculous!” and the little Lizard, who was something of a cynic, laughed outright.
passages.vernacular: 「為一朵紅玫瑰?」佢哋喊道;「幾咁荒謬!」嗰隻有點憤世嫉俗嘅小蜥蜴放聲大笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為一朵紅玫瑰?」他們喊道;「多麼荒謬!」那隻有點憤世嫉俗的小蜥蜴放聲大笑。

passages.original: But the Nightingale understood the secret of the Student’s sorrow, and she sat silent in the oak-tree, and thought about the mystery of Love.
passages.vernacular: 但夜鶯理解學生悲傷嘅祕密,佢默默地坐喺橡樹上,思考住愛嘅奧祕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但夜鶯理解學生悲傷的祕密,她默默地坐在橡樹上,思考著愛的奧祕。

passages.original: Suddenly she spread her brown wings for flight, and soared into the air. She passed through the grove like a shadow, and like a shadow she sailed across the garden.
passages.vernacular: 突然佢展開棕色嘅翅膀飛起,升入空中。佢像影子一樣穿過樹林,像影子一樣掠過花園。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 突然她展開棕色的翅膀飛起,升入空中。她像影子一樣穿過樹林,像影子一樣掠過花園。

passages.original: In the centre of the grass-plot was standing a beautiful Rose-tree, and when she saw it she flew over to it, and lit upon a spray.
passages.vernacular: 草坪中央站住一棵美麗嘅玫瑰樹,佢睇到佢,飛過去,落喺一根嫩枝上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 草坪中央站著一棵美麗的玫瑰樹,她看到它,飛過去,落在一根嫩枝上。

passages.original: “Give me a red rose,” she cried, “and I will sing you my sweetest song.”
passages.vernacular: 「畀我一朵紅玫瑰,」佢喊道,「我就為你唱我最甜美嘅歌。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「給我一朵紅玫瑰,」她喊道,「我就為你唱我最甜美的歌。」

passages.original: But the Tree shook its head.
passages.vernacular: 但樹搖咗搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但樹搖了搖頭。

passages.original: “My roses are white,” it answered; “as white as the foam of the sea, and whiter than the snow upon the mountain. But go to my brother who grows round the old sun-dial, and perhaps he will give you what you want.”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅玫瑰係白嘅,」佢回答;「像海浪嘅泡沫一樣白,比山上嘅雪仲白。但去找我哥哥,佢長喺老日晷周圍,或者佢會畀你想要嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的玫瑰是白的,」它回答;「像海浪的泡沫一樣白,比山上的雪還白。但去找我哥哥,他長在老日晷周圍,也許他會給你想要的。」

passages.original: So the Nightingale flew over to the Rose-tree that was growing round the old sun-dial.
passages.vernacular: 於是夜鶯飛向長喺老日晷周圍嘅玫瑰樹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是夜鶯飛向長在老日晷周圍的玫瑰樹。

passages.original: “Give me a red rose,” she cried, “and I will sing you my sweetest song.”
passages.vernacular: 「畀我一朵紅玫瑰,」佢喊道,「我就為你唱我最甜美嘅歌。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「給我一朵紅玫瑰,」她喊道,「我就為你唱我最甜美的歌。」

passages.original: But the Tree shook its head.
passages.vernacular: 但樹搖咗搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但樹搖了搖頭。

passages.original: “My roses are yellow,” it answered; “as yellow as the hair of the mermaiden who sits upon an amber throne, and yellower than the daffodil that blooms in the meadow before the mower comes with his scythe. But go to my brother who grows beneath the Student’s window, and perhaps he will give you what you want.”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅玫瑰係黃嘅,」佢回答;「像坐喺琥珀寶座上嘅美人魚嘅頭髮一樣黃,比割草人攞住鐮刀嚟之前草地上開嘅水仙仲黃。但去找我哥哥,佢長喺學生嘅窗下,或者佢會畀你想要嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的玫瑰是黃的,」它回答;「像坐在琥珀寶座上的美人魚的頭髮一樣黃,比割草人拿著鐮刀來之前草地上開的水仙還黃。但去找我哥哥,他長在學生的窗下,也許他會給你想要的。」

passages.original: So the Nightingale flew over to the Rose-tree that was growing beneath the Student’s window.
passages.vernacular: 於是夜鶯飛向長喺學生窗下嘅玫瑰樹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是夜鶯飛向長在學生窗下的玫瑰樹。

passages.original: “Give me a red rose,” she cried, “and I will sing you my sweetest song.”
passages.vernacular: 「畀我一朵紅玫瑰,」佢喊道,「我就為你唱我最甜美嘅歌。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「給我一朵紅玫瑰,」她喊道,「我就為你唱我最甜美的歌。」

passages.original: But the Tree shook its head.
passages.vernacular: 但樹搖咗搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但樹搖了搖頭。

passages.original: “My roses are red,” it answered, “as red as the feet of the dove, and redder than the great fans of coral that wave and wave in the ocean-cavern. But the winter has chilled my veins, and the frost has nipped my buds, and the storm has broken my branches, and I shall have no roses at all this year.”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅玫瑰係紅嘅,」佢回答,「像鴿子嘅腳一樣紅,比喺海洋洞穴中搖擺不停嘅大珊瑚扇仲紅。但冬天凍壞咗我嘅血管,霜凍傷咗我嘅花蕾,暴風雨折斷咗我嘅枝條,今年我根本唔會有玫瑰。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的玫瑰是紅的,」它回答,「像鴿子的腳一樣紅,比在海洋洞穴中搖擺不停的大珊瑚扇還紅。但冬天凍壞了我的血管,霜凍傷了我的花蕾,暴風雨折斷了我的枝條,今年我根本不會有玫瑰。」

passages.original: “One red rose is all I want,” cried the Nightingale, “only one red rose! Is there no way by which I can get it?”
passages.vernacular: 「我只要一朵紅玫瑰,」夜鶯喊道,「只要一朵紅玫瑰!有冇乜嘢辦法可以得到佢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只要一朵紅玫瑰,」夜鶯喊道,「只要一朵紅玫瑰!有沒有什麼辦法可以得到它?」

passages.original: “There is a way,” answered the Tree; “but it is so terrible that I dare not tell it to you.”
passages.vernacular: 「有辦法,」樹回答;「但佢太可怕喇,我唔敢告訴你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有辦法,」樹回答;「但它太可怕了,我不敢告訴你。」

passages.original: “Tell it to me,” said the Nightingale, “I am not afraid.”
passages.vernacular: 「告訴我,」夜鶯講,「我不怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「告訴我,」夜鶯說,「我不怕。」

passages.original: “If you want a red rose,” said the Tree, “you must build it out of music by moonlight, and stain it with your own heart’s-blood. You must sing to me with your breast against a thorn. All night long you must sing to me, and the thorn must pierce your heart, and your life-blood must flow into my veins, and become mine.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你想要一朵紅玫瑰,」樹講,「你必須喺月光下用音樂把佢建造出嚟,並用你自己嘅心頭血染紅佢。你必須讓胸口抵住一根刺為我歌唱。整夜你都必須為我歌唱,刺必須刺穿你嘅心,你嘅生命之血必須流進我嘅血管,成為我嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你想要一朵紅玫瑰,」樹說,「你必須在月光下用音樂把它建造出來,並用你自己的心頭血染紅它。你必須讓胸口抵著一根刺為我歌唱。整夜你都必須為我歌唱,刺必須刺穿你的心,你的生命之血必須流進我的血管,成為我的。」

passages.original: “Death is a great price to pay for a red rose,” cried the Nightingale, “and Life is very dear to all. It is pleasant to sit in the green wood, and to watch the Sun in his chariot of gold, and the Moon in her chariot of pearl. Sweet is the scent of the hawthorn, and sweet are the bluebells that hide in the valley, and the heather that blows on the hill. Yet Love is better than Life, and what is the heart of a bird compared to the heart of a man?”
passages.vernacular: 「死亡係為一朵紅玫瑰付出嘅巨大代價,」夜鶯喊道,「而生命對所有人都好寶貴。坐喺綠色嘅樹林裡,睇太陽坐喺佢嘅金色馬車裡,月亮坐喺佢嘅珍珠馬車裡,係愉快嘅。山楂嘅香氣係甜美嘅,藏喺山谷裡嘅藍鈴花同山上開嘅石楠花係甜美嘅。然而愛比生命更好,鳥兒嘅心同人嘅心相比算得咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「死亡是為一朵紅玫瑰付出的巨大代價,」夜鶯喊道,「而生命對所有人都很寶貴。坐在綠色的樹林裡,看太陽坐在他的金色馬車裡,月亮坐在她的珍珠馬車裡,是愉快的。山楂的香氣是甜美的,藏在山谷裡的藍鈴花和山上開的石楠花是甜美的。然而愛比生命更好,鳥兒的心與人的心相比算得了什麼?」

passages.original: So she spread her brown wings for flight, and soared into the air. She swept over the garden like a shadow, and like a shadow she sailed through the grove.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢展開棕色嘅翅膀飛起,升入空中。佢像影子一樣掠過花園,像影子一樣穿過樹林。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是她展開棕色的翅膀飛起,升入空中。她像影子一樣掠過花園,像影子一樣穿過樹林。

passages.original: The young Student was still lying on the grass, where she had left him, and the tears were not yet dry in his beautiful eyes.
passages.vernacular: 年輕嘅學生仲躺喺佢離開佢嘅草地上,美麗嘅眼睛裡淚水仲冇乾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 年輕的學生還躺在她離開他的草地上,美麗的眼睛裡淚水還沒乾。

passages.original: “Be happy,” cried the Nightingale, “be happy; you shall have your red rose. I will build it out of music by moonlight, and stain it with my own heart’s-blood. All that I ask of you in return is that you will be a true lover, for Love is wiser than Philosophy, though she is wise, and mightier than Power, though he is mighty. Flame-coloured are his wings, and coloured like flame is his body. His lips are sweet as honey, and his breath is like frankincense.”
passages.vernacular: 「高興起嚟,」夜鶯喊道,「高興起嚟;你會得到你嘅紅玫瑰。我會喺月光下用音樂建造佢,並用我自己嘅心頭血染紅佢。作為回報,我只要求你做一個真正嘅情人,因為愛比哲學更聰明,雖然哲學都聰明,比權力更強大,雖然權力都強大。佢嘅翅膀係火焰嘅顏色,佢嘅身體像火焰嘅顏色。佢嘅嘴唇像蜜一樣甜,佢嘅呼吸像乳香。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「高興起來,」夜鶯喊道,「高興起來;你會得到你的紅玫瑰。我會在月光下用音樂建造它,並用我自己的心頭血染紅它。作為回報,我只要求你做一個真正的情人,因為愛比哲學更聰明,雖然哲學也聰明,比權力更強大,雖然權力也強大。他的翅膀是火焰的顏色,他的身體像火焰的顏色。他的嘴唇像蜜一樣甜,他的呼吸像乳香。」

passages.original: The Student looked up from the grass, and listened, but he could not understand what the Nightingale was saying to him, for he only knew the things that are written down in books.
passages.vernacular: 學生從草地上抬頭聽住,但佢聽不懂夜鶯對佢講嘅話,因為佢只知道書上寫嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 學生從草地上抬頭聽著,但他聽不懂夜鶯對他說的話,因為他只知道書上寫的東西。

passages.original: But the Oak-tree understood, and felt sad, for he was very fond of the little Nightingale who had built her nest in his branches.
passages.vernacular: 但橡樹聽懂喇,感到悲傷,因為佢好鍾意喺佢枝條上築巢嘅小夜鶯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但橡樹聽懂了,感到悲傷,因為他非常喜歡在他枝條上築巢的小夜鶯。

passages.original: “Sing me one last song,” he whispered; “I shall feel very lonely when you are gone.”
passages.vernacular: 「再為我唱最後一首歌,」佢低聲講;「你走咗我會感到好孤單。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再為我唱最後一首歌,」他低聲說;「你走了我會感到很孤單。」

passages.original: So the Nightingale sang to the Oak-tree, and her voice was like water bubbling from a silver jar.
passages.vernacular: 於是夜鶯為橡樹歌唱,佢嘅聲音像水從銀罐裡冒泡而出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是夜鶯為橡樹歌唱,她的聲音像水從銀罐裡冒泡而出。

passages.original: When she had finished her song the Student got up, and pulled a note-book and a lead-pencil out of his pocket.
passages.vernacular: 佢唱完歌,學生站起嚟,從口袋裡掏出筆記本同鉛筆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她唱完歌,學生站起來,從口袋裡掏出筆記本和鉛筆。

passages.original: “She has form,” he said to himself, as he walked away through the grove—“that cannot be denied to her; but has she got feeling? I am afraid not. In fact, she is like most artists; she is all style, without any sincerity. She would not sacrifice herself for others. She thinks merely of music, and everybody knows that the arts are selfish. Still, it must be admitted that she has some beautiful notes in her voice. What a pity it is that they do not mean anything, or do any practical good.” And he went into his room, and lay down on his little pallet-bed, and began to think of his love; and, after a time, he fell asleep.
passages.vernacular: 「佢有形式,」佢一邊穿過樹林走開,一邊對自己講——「呢個係唔能夠否認嘅;但佢有感情嗎?我恐怕冇。事實上,佢像大多數藝術家;全係風格,冇任何誠意。佢唔會為別人犧牲自己。佢只想住音樂,而人人都知道藝術係自私嘅。不過,必須承認佢嘅聲音裡有啲美麗嘅音符。可惜佢哋冇任何意義,都冇任何實際嘅好處。」佢走進自己嘅房間,躺喺佢嘅小草墊床上,開始想佢嘅愛人;過咗一會兒,佢瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她有形式,」他一邊穿過樹林走開,一邊對自己說——「這是不能否認的;但她有感情嗎?我恐怕沒有。事實上,她像大多數藝術家;全是風格,沒有任何誠意。她不會為別人犧牲自己。她只想著音樂,而人人都知道藝術是自私的。不過,必須承認她的聲音裡有一些美麗的音符。可惜它們沒有任何意義,也沒有任何實際的好處。」他走進自己的房間,躺在他的小草墊床上,開始想他的愛人;過了一會兒,他睡著了。

passages.original: And when the Moon shone in the heavens the Nightingale flew to the Rose-tree, and set her breast against the thorn. All night long she sang with her breast against the thorn, and the cold crystal Moon leaned down and listened. All night long she sang, and the thorn went deeper and deeper into her breast, and her life-blood ebbed away from her.
passages.vernacular: 月亮喺天空中照耀時,夜鶯飛到玫瑰樹上,把胸口抵住刺。整夜佢胸口抵住刺歌唱,冰冷嘅水晶月亮俯身傾聽。整夜佢歌唱,刺越嚟越深地刺進佢嘅胸口,佢嘅生命之血從佢身上流走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 月亮在天空中照耀時,夜鶯飛到玫瑰樹上,把胸口抵著刺。整夜她胸口抵著刺歌唱,冰冷的水晶月亮俯身傾聽。整夜她歌唱,刺越來越深地刺進她的胸口,她的生命之血從她身上流走。

passages.original: She sang first of the birth of love in the heart of a boy and a girl. And on the top-most spray of the Rose-tree there blossomed a marvellous rose, petal following petal, as song followed song. Pale was it, at first, as the mist that hangs over the river—pale as the feet of the morning, and silver as the wings of the dawn. As the shadow of a rose in a mirror of silver, as the shadow of a rose in a water-pool, so was the rose that blossomed on the topmost spray of the Tree.
passages.vernacular: 佢先唱嘅係愛喺一個男孩同一個女孩心中嘅誕生。玫瑰樹最頂端嘅嫩枝上,綻放出一朵奇妙嘅玫瑰,花瓣接住花瓣,如同歌曲接住歌曲。起初佢係蒼白嘅,像懸喺河上嘅霧——像晨曦嘅腳一樣蒼白,像黎明嘅翅膀一樣銀白。像銀鏡裡嘅玫瑰影子,像水池裡嘅玫瑰影子,就係綻放喺樹頂嫩枝上嘅嗰朵玫瑰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她先唱的是愛在一個男孩和一個女孩心中的誕生。玫瑰樹最頂端的嫩枝上,綻放出一朵奇妙的玫瑰,花瓣接著花瓣,如同歌曲接著歌曲。起初它是蒼白的,像懸在河上的霧——像晨曦的腳一樣蒼白,像黎明的翅膀一樣銀白。像銀鏡裡的玫瑰影子,像水池裡的玫瑰影子,就是綻放在樹頂嫩枝上的那朵玫瑰。

passages.original: But the Tree cried to the Nightingale to press closer against the thorn. “Press closer, little Nightingale,” cried the Tree, “or the Day will come before the rose is finished.”
passages.vernacular: 但樹對夜鶯喊,要佢更緊地壓向刺。「再壓緊些,小夜鶯,」樹喊道,「否則玫瑰仲冇完成白天就嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但樹對夜鶯喊,要她更緊地壓向刺。「再壓緊些,小夜鶯,」樹喊道,「否則玫瑰還沒完成白天就來了。」

passages.original: So the Nightingale pressed closer against the thorn, and louder and louder grew her song, for she sang of the birth of passion in the soul of a man and a maid.
passages.vernacular: 於是夜鶯更緊地壓向刺,佢嘅歌聲越嚟越響,因為佢唱嘅係激情喺男人同少女心中嘅誕生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是夜鶯更緊地壓向刺,她的歌聲越來越響,因為她唱的是激情在男人和少女心中的誕生。

passages.original: And a delicate flush of pink came into the leaves of the rose, like the flush in the face of the bridegroom when he kisses the lips of the bride. But the thorn had not yet reached her heart, so the rose’s heart remained white, for only a Nightingale’s heart’s-blood can crimson the heart of a rose.
passages.vernacular: 玫瑰嘅葉子上出現咗一抹淡淡嘅粉紅,像新郎吻新娘嘅嘴唇時臉上嘅紅暈。但刺仲冇到達佢嘅心,所以玫瑰嘅心仍然係白嘅,因為只有夜鶯嘅心頭血才能染紅玫瑰嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 玫瑰的葉子上出現了一抹淡淡的粉紅,像新郎吻新娘的嘴唇時臉上的紅暈。但刺還沒有到達她的心,所以玫瑰的心仍然是白的,因為只有夜鶯的心頭血才能染紅玫瑰的心。

passages.original: And the Tree cried to the Nightingale to press closer against the thorn. “Press closer, little Nightingale,” cried the Tree, “or the Day will come before the rose is finished.”
passages.vernacular: 樹又對夜鶯喊,要佢更緊地壓向刺。「再壓緊些,小夜鶯,」樹喊道,「否則玫瑰仲冇完成白天就嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樹又對夜鶯喊,要她更緊地壓向刺。「再壓緊些,小夜鶯,」樹喊道,「否則玫瑰還沒完成白天就來了。」

passages.original: So the Nightingale pressed closer against the thorn, and the thorn touched her heart, and a fierce pang of pain shot through her. Bitter, bitter was the pain, and wilder and wilder grew her song, for she sang of the Love that is perfected by Death, of the Love that dies not in the tomb.
passages.vernacular: 於是夜鶯更緊地壓向刺,刺碰到咗佢嘅心,一陣劇烈嘅痛楚穿過佢全身。痛得苦,痛得苦,佢嘅歌越嚟越狂野,因為佢唱嘅係因死亡而完美嘅愛,係喺墳墓中都不死嘅愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是夜鶯更緊地壓向刺,刺碰到了她的心,一陣劇烈的痛楚穿過她全身。痛得苦,痛得苦,她的歌越來越狂野,因為她唱的是因死亡而完美的愛,是在墳墓中也不死的愛。

passages.original: And the marvellous rose became crimson, like the rose of the eastern sky. Crimson was the girdle of petals, and crimson as a ruby was the heart.
passages.vernacular: 奇妙嘅玫瑰變成咗深紅色,像東方天空嘅玫瑰。花瓣嘅腰帶係深紅嘅,花心像紅寶石一樣深紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奇妙的玫瑰變成了深紅色,像東方天空的玫瑰。花瓣的腰帶是深紅的,花心像紅寶石一樣深紅。

passages.original: But the Nightingale’s voice grew fainter, and her little wings began to beat, and a film came over her eyes. Fainter and fainter grew her song, and she felt something choking her in her throat.
passages.vernacular: 但夜鶯嘅聲音越嚟越弱,佢嘅小翅膀開始拍打,一層薄膜蓋上咗佢嘅眼睛。佢嘅歌越嚟越微弱,佢覺得有乜嘢嘢喺佢喉嚨裡哽住咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但夜鶯的聲音越來越弱,她的小翅膀開始拍打,一層薄膜蓋上了她的眼睛。她的歌越來越微弱,她覺得有什麼東西在她喉嚨裡哽住了她。

passages.original: Then she gave one last burst of music. The white Moon heard it, and she forgot the dawn, and lingered on in the sky. The red rose heard it, and it trembled all over with ecstasy, and opened its petals to the cold morning air. Echo bore it to her purple cavern in the hills, and woke the sleeping shepherds from their dreams. It floated through the reeds of the river, and they carried its message to the sea.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢發出咗最後一陣音樂。白色嘅月亮聽到喇,佢忘咗黎明,喺天空中逗留不去。紅玫瑰聽到喇,佢全身狂喜地顫抖,向寒冷嘅晨風張開花瓣。回聲把佢帶到山裡佢嘅紫色洞穴,把沉瞓嘅牧羊人從夢中喚醒。佢飄過河裡嘅蘆葦,蘆葦把佢嘅消息帶到咗大海。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她發出了最後一陣音樂。白色的月亮聽到了,她忘了黎明,在天空中逗留不去。紅玫瑰聽到了,它全身狂喜地顫抖,向寒冷的晨風張開花瓣。回聲把它帶到山裡她的紫色洞穴,把沉睡的牧羊人從夢中喚醒。它飄過河裡的蘆葦,蘆葦把它的消息帶到了大海。

passages.original: “Look, look!” cried the Tree, “the rose is finished now”; but the Nightingale made no answer, for she was lying dead in the long grass, with the thorn in her heart.
passages.vernacular: 「睇,睇!」樹喊道,「玫瑰完成喇」;但夜鶯冇回答,因為佢躺喺長草裡死喇,刺仲喺佢嘅心裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看,看!」樹喊道,「玫瑰完成了」;但夜鶯沒有回答,因為她躺在長草裡死了,刺還在她的心裡。

passages.original: And at noon the Student opened his window and looked out.
passages.vernacular: 中午學生打開窗向外睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 中午學生打開窗向外看。

passages.original: “Why, what a wonderful piece of luck!” he cried; “here is a red rose! I have never seen any rose like it in all my life. It is so beautiful that I am sure it has a long Latin name”; and he leaned down and plucked it.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,幾咁奇妙嘅運氣!」佢喊道;「呢度有一朵紅玫瑰!我一生中從冇見過咁樣嘅玫瑰。佢咁美,我肯定佢有一個好長嘅拉丁文名字」;佢彎下身摘咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,多麼奇妙的運氣!」他喊道;「這裡有一朵紅玫瑰!我一生中從沒見過這樣的玫瑰。它那麼美,我肯定它有一個很長的拉丁文名字」;他彎下身摘了它。

passages.original: Then he put on his hat, and ran up to the Professor’s house with the rose in his hand.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢戴上帽子,手裡攞住玫瑰跑到教授家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他戴上帽子,手裡拿著玫瑰跑到教授家。

passages.original: The daughter of the Professor was sitting in the doorway winding blue silk on a reel, and her little dog was lying at her feet.
passages.vernacular: 教授嘅女兒坐喺門口,把藍色絲線繞喺線軸上,佢嘅小狗躺喺佢腳邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 教授的女兒坐在門口,把藍色絲線繞在線軸上,她的小狗躺在她腳邊。

passages.original: “You said that you would dance with me if I brought you a red rose,” cried the Student. “Here is the reddest rose in all the world. You will wear it to-night next your heart, and as we dance together it will tell you how I love you.”
passages.vernacular: 「你講過如果我畀你帶紅玫瑰,你就同我跳舞,」學生喊道。「呢度係世界上最紅嘅玫瑰。你今晚把佢戴喺心口,我哋一起跳舞時,佢會告訴你我幾咁愛你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你說過如果我給你帶紅玫瑰,你就同我跳舞,」學生喊道。「這裡是世界上最紅的玫瑰。你今晚把它戴在心口,我們一起跳舞時,它會告訴你我多麼愛你。」

passages.original: But the girl frowned.
passages.vernacular: 但女孩皺起眉頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但女孩皺起眉頭。

passages.original: “I am afraid it will not go with my dress,” she answered; “and, besides, the Chamberlain’s nephew has sent me some real jewels, and everybody knows that jewels cost far more than flowers.”
passages.vernacular: 「我恐怕佢同我嘅衣服不配,」佢回答;「而且,侍從長嘅侄子送咗我啲真正嘅珠寶,人人都知道珠寶比花貴得多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我恐怕它和我的衣服不配,」她回答;「而且,侍從長的侄子送了我一些真正的珠寶,人人都知道珠寶比花貴得多。」

passages.original: “Well, upon my word, you are very ungrateful,” said the Student angrily; and he threw the rose into the street, where it fell into the gutter, and a cart-wheel went over it.
passages.vernacular: 「哼,講真嘅,你太忘恩負義喇,」學生生氣地講;佢把玫瑰扔到街上,佢落喺水溝裡,一個車輪從佢上面碾過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼,說真的,你太忘恩負義了,」學生生氣地說;他把玫瑰扔到街上,它落在水溝裡,一個車輪從它上面碾過。

passages.original: “Ungrateful!” said the girl. “I tell you what, you are very rude; and, after all, who are you? Only a Student. Why, I don’t believe you have even got silver buckles to your shoes as the Chamberlain’s nephew has”; and she got up from her chair and went into the house.
passages.vernacular: 「忘恩負義!」女孩講。「我告訴你,你好無禮;而且,你到底係邊個?只係一個學生。哎呀,我不相信你鞋子上連侍從長嘅侄子嗰樣嘅銀扣都冇」;佢從椅子上站起嚟,走進咗屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「忘恩負義!」女孩說。「我告訴你,你很無禮;而且,你到底是誰?只是一個學生。哎呀,我不相信你鞋子上連侍從長的侄子那樣的銀扣都沒有」;她從椅子上站起來,走進了屋。

passages.original: “What a silly thing Love is,” said the Student as he walked away. “It is not half as useful as Logic, for it does not prove anything, and it is always telling one of things that are not going to happen, and making one believe things that are not true. In fact, it is quite unpractical, and, as in this age to be practical is everything, I shall go back to Philosophy and study Metaphysics.”
passages.vernacular: 「愛情係幾咁愚蠢嘅嘢,」學生走開時講。「佢連邏輯一半有用都冇,因為佢乜嘢都證明不喇,總是告訴人啲唔會發生嘅事,讓人相信啲不真實嘅事。事實上,佢好不切實際,而喺呢個時代,實際就係一切,我要回去學哲學,研究形而上學。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「愛情是多麼愚蠢的東西,」學生走開時說。「它連邏輯一半有用都沒有,因為它什麼也證明不了,總是告訴人一些不會發生的事,讓人相信一些不真實的事。事實上,它非常不切實際,而在這個時代,實際就是一切,我要回去學哲學,研究形而上學。」

passages.original: So he returned to his room and pulled out a great dusty book, and began to read.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢回到自己嘅房間,取出一本積滿灰塵嘅大書,開始讀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他回到自己的房間,取出一本積滿灰塵的大書,開始讀。

chapters.title: The Selfish Giant 自私的巨人

passages.original: EVERY afternoon, as they were coming from school, the children used to go and play in the Giant’s garden.
passages.vernacular: 每天下午,細路哋放學回嚟時,都會去巨人嘅花園裡玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每天下午,孩子們放學回來時,都會去巨人的花園裡玩。

passages.original: It was a large lovely garden, with soft green grass. Here and there over the grass stood beautiful flowers like stars, and there were twelve peach-trees that in the spring-time broke out into delicate blossoms of pink and pearl, and in the autumn bore rich fruit. The birds sat on the trees and sang so sweetly that the children used to stop their games in order to listen to them. “How happy we are here!” they cried to each other.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一座寬大可愛嘅花園,有柔軟嘅綠草。草地上呢度嗰度長住像星星一樣嘅美麗花朵,仲有十二棵桃樹,春天開出粉紅色同珍珠色嘅嬌嫩花朵,秋天結出豐盛嘅果實。鳥兒坐喺樹上唱得咁甜美,細路哋常常停下遊戲嚟聽牠哋唱歌。「我哋喺呢度幾咁快樂!」佢哋互相喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一座寬大可愛的花園,有柔軟的綠草。草地上這裡那裡長著像星星一樣的美麗花朵,還有十二棵桃樹,春天開出粉紅色和珍珠色的嬌嫩花朵,秋天結出豐盛的果實。鳥兒坐在樹上唱得那麼甜美,孩子們常常停下遊戲來聽牠們唱歌。「我們在這裡多麼快樂!」他們互相喊道。

passages.original: One day the Giant came back. He had been to visit his friend the Cornish ogre, and had stayed with him for seven years. After the seven years were over he had said all that he had to say, for his conversation was limited, and he determined to return to his own castle. When he arrived he saw the children playing in the garden.
passages.vernacular: 一天,巨人回嚟喇。佢去拜訪佢嘅朋友康沃爾食人魔,同佢住咗七年。七年過去後,佢講完咗佢要講嘅話,因為佢嘅談話有限,佢決定回佢自己嘅城堡。佢到咗嘅時候,睇到細路哋喺花園裡玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天,巨人回來了。他去拜訪他的朋友康沃爾食人魔,同他住了七年。七年過去後,他說完了他要說的話,因為他的談話有限,他決定回他自己的城堡。他到了的時候,看到孩子們在花園裡玩。

passages.original: “What are you doing here?” he cried in a very gruff voice, and the children ran away.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋喺呢度做乜嘢?」佢用好粗暴嘅聲音喊道,細路哋都跑開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們在這裡做什麼?」他用很粗暴的聲音喊道,孩子們都跑開了。

passages.original: “My own garden is my own garden,” said the Giant; “any one can understand that, and I will allow nobody to play in it but myself.” So he built a high wall all round it, and put up a notice-board.
passages.vernacular: 「我自己嘅花園就係我自己嘅花園,」巨人講;「任何人都能明白,我不允許任何人喺裡面玩,除咗我自己。」於是佢喺佢周圍築咗一堵高牆,立咗一塊告示牌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我自己的花園就是我自己的花園,」巨人說;「任何人都能明白,我不允許任何人在裡面玩,除了我自己。」於是他在它周圍築了一堵高牆,立了一塊告示牌。

passages.vernacular: 擅入者
passages.vernacularMandarin: 擅入者

passages.vernacular: 將被

passages.original: He was a very selfish Giant.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個好自私嘅巨人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個非常自私的巨人。

passages.original: The poor children had now nowhere to play. They tried to play on the road, but the road was very dusty and full of hard stones, and they did not like it. They used to wander round the high wall when their lessons were over, and talk about the beautiful garden inside. “How happy we were there,” they said to each other.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅細路哋而家冇地方玩喇。佢哋試住喺路上玩,但路上塵土飛揚,滿係硬石頭,佢哋不鍾意。佢哋下課後常常喺高牆外徘徊,談論裡面美麗嘅花園。「我哋喺嗰度多快樂,」佢哋互相講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的孩子們現在沒有地方玩了。他們試著在路上玩,但路上塵土飛揚,滿是硬石頭,他們不喜歡。他們下課後常常在高牆外徘徊,談論裡面美麗的花園。「我們在那裡多快樂,」他們互相說。

passages.original: Then the Spring came, and all over the country there were little blossoms and little birds. Only in the garden of the Selfish Giant it was still winter. The birds did not care to sing in it as there were no children, and the trees forgot to blossom. Once a beautiful flower put its head out from the grass, but when it saw the notice-board it was so sorry for the children that it slipped back into the ground again, and went off to sleep. The only people who were pleased were the Snow and the Frost. “Spring has forgotten this garden,” they cried, “so we will live here all the year round.” The Snow covered up the grass with her great white cloak, and the Frost painted all the trees silver. Then they invited the North Wind to stay with them, and he came. He was wrapped in furs, and he roared all day about the garden, and blew the chimney-pots down. “This is a delightful spot,” he said, “we must ask the Hail on a visit.” So the Hail came. Every day for three hours he rattled on the roof of the castle till he broke most of the slates, and then he ran round and round the garden as fast as he could go. He was dressed in grey, and his breath was like ice.
passages.vernacular: 然後春天嚟喇,全國到處係小小嘅花朵同小鳥。只有自私巨人嘅花園裡仍然係冬天。鳥兒唔想喺嗰度唱歌,因為冇細路,樹都忘咗開花。有一次一朵美麗嘅花從草裡探出頭,但睇到告示牌,佢為細路哋感到咁難過,又縮回地裡,瞓住喇。唯一高興嘅係雪同霜。「春天忘咗呢座花園,」佢哋喊道,「所以我哋要整年住喺呢度。」雪用佢嘅大白斗篷蓋住咗草,霜把所有嘅樹漆成銀色。然後佢哋邀請北風嚟同住,佢嚟喇。佢裹住毛皮,整天喺花園周圍咆哮,把煙囪帽吹倒。「呢個係個令人愉快嘅地方,」佢講,「我哋必須請冰雹嚟訪。」於是冰雹嚟喇。每天佢喺城堡屋頂上劈劈啪啪響三個小時,直到打破大部分石板瓦,然後佢盡可能快地繞住花園跑圈。佢穿住灰色衣服,呼吸像冰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後春天來了,全國到處是小小的花朵和小鳥。只有自私巨人的花園裡仍然是冬天。鳥兒不想在那裡唱歌,因為沒有孩子,樹也忘了開花。有一次一朵美麗的花從草裡探出頭,但看到告示牌,它為孩子們感到那麼難過,又縮回地裡,睡著了。唯一高興的是雪和霜。「春天忘了這座花園,」他們喊道,「所以我們要整年住在這裡。」雪用她的大白斗篷蓋住了草,霜把所有的樹漆成銀色。然後他們邀請北風來同住,他來了。他裹著毛皮,整天在花園周圍咆哮,把煙囪帽吹倒。「這是個令人愉快的地方,」他說,「我們必須請冰雹來訪。」於是冰雹來了。每天他在城堡屋頂上劈劈啪啪響三個小時,直到打破大部分石板瓦,然後他盡可能快地繞著花園跑圈。他穿著灰色衣服,呼吸像冰。

passages.original: “I cannot understand why the Spring is so late in coming,” said the Selfish Giant, as he sat at the window and looked out at his cold white garden; “I hope there will be a change in the weather.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不明白春天點解嚟得咁晚,」自私嘅巨人坐喺窗邊,望住佢寒冷嘅白色花園講;「我希望天氣會有變化。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不明白春天為什麼來得這麼晚,」自私的巨人坐在窗邊,望著他寒冷的白色花園說;「我希望天氣會有變化。」

passages.original: But the Spring never came, nor the Summer. The Autumn gave golden fruit to every garden, but to the Giant’s garden she gave none. “He is too selfish,” she said. So it was always Winter there, and the North Wind, and the Hail, and the Frost, and the Snow danced about through the trees.
passages.vernacular: 但春天始終冇嚟,夏天都冇。秋天畀每座花園金色嘅果實,但冇畀巨人嘅花園任何嘢。「佢太自私喇,」佢講。所以嗰度永遠係冬天,北風、冰雹、霜同雪喺樹林間跳舞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但春天始終沒有來,夏天也沒有。秋天給每座花園金色的果實,但沒給巨人的花園任何東西。「他太自私了,」她說。所以那裡永遠是冬天,北風、冰雹、霜和雪在樹林間跳舞。

passages.original: One morning the Giant was lying awake in bed when he heard some lovely music. It sounded so sweet to his ears that he thought it must be the King’s musicians passing by. It was really only a little linnet singing outside his window, but it was so long since he had heard a bird sing in his garden that it seemed to him to be the most beautiful music in the world. Then the Hail stopped dancing over his head, and the North Wind ceased roaring, and a delicious perfume came to him through the open casement. “I believe the Spring has come at last,” said the Giant; and he jumped out of bed and looked out.
passages.vernacular: 一天早晨,巨人醒住躺喺床上,聽到啲可愛嘅音樂。佢喺佢耳中聽起嚟咁甜美,佢以為一定係國王嘅樂師經過。其實只係一隻紅雀喺佢窗外歌唱,但佢已經好久冇聽到鳥喺佢花園裡唱歌喇,所以對佢來講,嗰似乎係世界上最美嘅音樂。然後冰雹唔再喺佢頭上跳舞,北風停止咗咆哮,一股美妙嘅香氣透過敞開嘅窗子飄嚟。「我相信春天終於嚟喇,」巨人講;佢跳下床,向外睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天早晨,巨人醒著躺在床上,聽到一些可愛的音樂。它在他耳中聽起來那麼甜美,他以為一定是國王的樂師經過。其實只是一隻紅雀在他窗外歌唱,但他已經很久沒聽到鳥在他花園裡唱歌了,所以對他來說,那似乎是世界上最美的音樂。然後冰雹不再在他頭上跳舞,北風停止了咆哮,一股美妙的香氣透過敞開的窗子飄來。「我相信春天終於來了,」巨人說;他跳下床,向外看。

passages.original: What did he see?
passages.vernacular: 佢睇到咗乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看到了什麼?

passages.original: He saw a most wonderful sight. Through a little hole in the wall the children had crept in, and they were sitting in the branches of the trees. In every tree that he could see there was a little child. And the trees were so glad to have the children back again that they had covered themselves with blossoms, and were waving their arms gently above the children’s heads. The birds were flying about and twittering with delight, and the flowers were looking up through the green grass and laughing. It was a lovely scene, only in one corner it was still winter. It was the farthest corner of the garden, and in it was standing a little boy. He was so small that he could not reach up to the branches of the tree, and he was wandering all round it, crying bitterly. The poor tree was still quite covered with frost and snow, and the North Wind was blowing and roaring above it. “Climb up! little boy,” said the Tree, and it bent its branches down as low as it could; but the boy was too tiny.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇到咗一幅最奇妙嘅景象。細路哋從牆上嘅一個小洞爬咗進嚟,坐喺樹枝上。喺佢能睇到嘅每棵樹上都有一個小孩。樹哋好高興細路哋回嚟喇,佢哋畀自己蓋滿咗花朵,輕輕地喺細路哋頭上揮動手臂。鳥兒到處飛翔,高興地啾啾叫,花朵從綠草中向上睇住,笑住。嗰個係一幅可愛嘅景象,只有喺一個角落裡仍然係冬天。嗰個係花園最遠嘅角落,嗰度站住一個小男孩。佢太小喇,夠唔到樹枝,佢繞住樹轉圈,傷心地哭。可憐嘅樹仍然全被霜同雪覆蓋,北風喺佢上面吹住咆哮。「爬上嚟!小男孩,」樹講,佢盡可能把樹枝彎低;但男孩太小喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看到了一幅最奇妙的景象。孩子們從牆上的一個小洞爬了進來,坐在樹枝上。在他能看到的每棵樹上都有一個小孩。樹們非常高興孩子們回來了,它們給自己蓋滿了花朵,輕輕地在孩子們頭上揮動手臂。鳥兒到處飛翔,高興地啾啾叫,花朵從綠草中向上看著,笑著。那是一幅可愛的景象,只有在一個角落裡仍然是冬天。那是花園最遠的角落,那裡站著一個小男孩。他太小了,夠不到樹枝,他繞著樹轉圈,傷心地哭。可憐的樹仍然全被霜和雪覆蓋,北風在它上面吹著咆哮。「爬上來!小男孩,」樹說,它盡可能把樹枝彎低;但男孩太小了。

passages.original: And the Giant’s heart melted as he looked out. “How selfish I have been!” he said; “now I know why the Spring would not come here. I will put that poor little boy on the top of the tree, and then I will knock down the wall, and my garden shall be the children’s playground for ever and ever.” He was really very sorry for what he had done.
passages.vernacular: 巨人向外睇時,佢嘅心融化喇。「我幾咁自私!」佢講;「而家我知道春天點解不嚟呢度喇。我要把嗰個可憐嘅小男孩放到樹頂上,然後我要把牆拆掉,我嘅花園將永遠永遠成為細路哋嘅遊樂場。」佢對佢所做嘅事真嘅好抱歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巨人向外看時,他的心融化了。「我多麼自私!」他說;「現在我知道春天為什麼不來這裡了。我要把那個可憐的小男孩放到樹頂上,然後我要把牆拆掉,我的花園將永遠永遠成為孩子們的遊樂場。」他對他所做的事真的非常抱歉。

passages.original: So he crept downstairs and opened the front door quite softly, and went out into the garden. But when the children saw him they were so frightened that they all ran away, and the garden became winter again. Only the little boy did not run, for his eyes were so full of tears that he did not see the Giant coming. And the Giant stole up behind him and took him gently in his hand, and put him up into the tree. And the tree broke at once into blossom, and the birds came and sang on it, and the little boy stretched out his two arms and flung them round the Giant’s neck, and kissed him. And the other children, when they saw that the Giant was not wicked any longer, came running back, and with them came the Spring. “It is your garden now, little children,” said the Giant, and he took a great axe and knocked down the wall. And when the people were going to market at twelve o’clock they found the Giant playing with the children in the most beautiful garden they had ever seen.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢輕輕地爬下樓,悄悄打開前門,走進花園。但細路哋睇到佢時,嚇得全跑喇,花園又變成咗冬天。只有小男孩冇跑,因為佢嘅眼睛裡滿係淚水,冇睇到巨人嚟。巨人悄悄走到佢身後,輕輕把佢托喺手裡,放到樹上。樹即刻綻放出花朵,鳥兒嚟到佢上面歌唱,小男孩伸出雙臂,摟住巨人嘅脖子,吻咗佢。其他細路睇到巨人唔再邪惡,跑咗回嚟,春天都跟住佢哋嚟喇。「而家呢個係你哋嘅花園喇,小朋友哋,」巨人講,佢攞起一把大斧頭,把牆拆倒喇。十二點人哋去趕集時,發現巨人同細路哋喺佢哋見過嘅最美麗嘅花園裡玩耍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他輕輕地爬下樓,悄悄打開前門,走進花園。但孩子們看到他時,嚇得全跑了,花園又變成了冬天。只有小男孩沒有跑,因為他的眼睛裡滿是淚水,沒有看到巨人來。巨人悄悄走到他身後,輕輕把他托在手裡,放到樹上。樹立刻綻放出花朵,鳥兒來到它上面歌唱,小男孩伸出雙臂,摟住巨人的脖子,吻了他。其他孩子看到巨人不再邪惡,跑了回來,春天也跟著他們來了。「現在這是你們的花園了,小朋友們,」巨人說,他拿起一把大斧頭,把牆拆倒了。十二點人們去趕集時,發現巨人同孩子們在他們見過的最美麗的花園裡玩耍。

passages.original: All day long they played, and in the evening they came to the Giant to bid him good-bye.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋玩咗一整天,晚上佢哋嚟向巨人道別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們玩了一整天,晚上他們來向巨人道別。

passages.original: “But where is your little companion?” he said: “the boy I put into the tree.” The Giant loved him the best because he had kissed him.
passages.vernacular: 「但你哋嘅小夥伴喺邊度?」佢講:「我放到樹上嘅嗰個男孩。」巨人最愛佢,因為佢吻咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你們的小夥伴在哪裡?」他說:「我放到樹上的那個男孩。」巨人最愛他,因為他吻了他。

passages.original: “We don’t know,” answered the children; “he has gone away.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋唔知道,」細路哋回答;「佢走喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們不知道,」孩子們回答;「他走了。」

passages.original: “You must tell him to be sure and come here to-morrow,” said the Giant. But the children said that they did not know where he lived, and had never seen him before; and the Giant felt very sad.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋一定要告訴佢聽日嚟呢度,」巨人講。但細路哋講佢哋唔知道佢住喺邊度,以前都從冇見過佢;巨人覺得好悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們一定要告訴他明天來這裡,」巨人說。但孩子們說他們不知道他住在哪裡,以前也從沒見過他;巨人覺得很悲傷。

passages.original: Every afternoon, when school was over, the children came and played with the Giant. But the little boy whom the Giant loved was never seen again. The Giant was very kind to all the children, yet he longed for his first little friend, and often spoke of him. “How I would like to see him!” he used to say.
passages.vernacular: 每天下午放學後,細路哋嚟同巨人玩。但巨人愛嘅嗰個小男孩再都冇出現過。巨人對所有細路都好好,但佢渴望佢嘅第一個小朋友,常常提起佢。「我幾咁想見佢!」佢常講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每天下午放學後,孩子們來同巨人玩。但巨人愛的那個小男孩再也沒有出現過。巨人對所有孩子都非常好,但他渴望他的第一個小朋友,常常提起他。「我多麼想見他!」他常說。

passages.original: Years went over, and the Giant grew very old and feeble. He could not play about any more, so he sat in a huge armchair, and watched the children at their games, and admired his garden. “I have many beautiful flowers,” he said; “but the children are the most beautiful flowers of all.”
passages.vernacular: 歲月流逝,巨人變得好老好虛弱。佢唔能夠再到處玩喇,所以佢坐喺一張巨大嘅扶手椅上,睇細路哋玩遊戲,欣賞佢嘅花園。「我有許多美麗嘅花,」佢講;「但細路哋係所有花中最美嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歲月流逝,巨人變得很老很虛弱。他不能再到處玩了,所以他坐在一張巨大的扶手椅上,看孩子們玩遊戲,欣賞他的花園。「我有許多美麗的花,」他說;「但孩子們是所有花中最美的。」

passages.original: One winter morning he looked out of his window as he was dressing. He did not hate the Winter now, for he knew that it was merely the Spring asleep, and that the flowers were resting.
passages.vernacular: 一個冬天嘅早晨,佢穿衣服時向窗外睇。佢而家不恨冬天喇,因為佢知道佢只係春天喺瞓覺,花朵喺休息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個冬天的早晨,他穿衣服時向窗外看。他現在不恨冬天了,因為他知道它只是春天在睡覺,花朵在休息。

passages.original: Suddenly he rubbed his eyes in wonder, and looked and looked. It certainly was a marvellous sight. In the farthest corner of the garden was a tree quite covered with lovely white blossoms. Its branches were all golden, and silver fruit hung down from them, and underneath it stood the little boy he had loved.
passages.vernacular: 突然佢驚奇地揉咗揉眼睛,睇咗又睇。嗰確實係一幅奇妙嘅景象。喺花園最遠嘅角落裡有一棵樹,全被可愛嘅白花覆蓋。佢嘅樹枝都係金色嘅,銀色嘅果實從上面垂下嚟,樹下站住佢愛嘅嗰個小男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 突然他驚奇地揉了揉眼睛,看了又看。那確實是一幅奇妙的景象。在花園最遠的角落裡有一棵樹,全被可愛的白花覆蓋。它的樹枝都是金色的,銀色的果實從上面垂下來,樹下站著他愛的那個小男孩。

passages.original: Downstairs ran the Giant in great joy, and out into the garden. He hastened across the grass, and came near to the child. And when he came quite close his face grew red with anger, and he said, “Who hath dared to wound thee?” For on the palms of the child’s hands were the prints of two nails, and the prints of two nails were on the little feet.
passages.vernacular: 巨人高興地跑下樓,跑進花園。佢匆匆穿過草地,走近細路。佢走得好近時,臉氣得發紅,佢講:「邊個敢傷害你?」因為細路手掌上有兩個釘子嘅印記,小腳上都有兩個釘子嘅印記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巨人高興地跑下樓,跑進花園。他匆匆穿過草地,走近孩子。他走得很近時,臉氣得發紅,他說:「誰敢傷害你?」因為孩子手掌上有兩個釘子的印記,小腳上也有兩個釘子的印記。

passages.original: “Who hath dared to wound thee?” cried the Giant; “tell me, that I may take my big sword and slay him.”
passages.vernacular: 「邊個敢傷害你?」巨人喊道;「告訴我,我要攞我嘅大劍殺咗佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰敢傷害你?」巨人喊道;「告訴我,我要拿我的大劍殺了他。」

passages.original: “Nay!” answered the child; “but these are the wounds of Love.”
passages.vernacular: 「不!」細路回答;「呢啲係愛嘅傷口。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不!」孩子回答;「這些是愛的傷口。」

passages.original: “Who art thou?” said the Giant, and a strange awe fell on him, and he knelt before the little child.
passages.vernacular: 「你係邊個?」巨人講,一種奇異嘅敬畏降臨喺佢身上,佢跪喺小孩面前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是誰?」巨人說,一種奇異的敬畏降臨在他身上,他跪在小孩面前。

passages.original: And the child smiled on the Giant, and said to him, “You let me play once in your garden, to-day you shall come with me to my garden, which is Paradise.”
passages.vernacular: 細路對巨人微笑,對佢講:「你曾經讓我喺你嘅花園裡玩,今日你要同我到我嘅花園去,嗰個就係天堂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子對巨人微笑,對他說:「你曾經讓我在你的花園裡玩,今天你要同我到我的花園去,那就是天堂。」

passages.original: And when the children ran in that afternoon, they found the Giant lying dead under the tree, all covered with white blossoms.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天下午細路哋跑進嚟時,發現巨人躺喺樹下死喇,身上蓋滿白花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天下午孩子們跑進來時,發現巨人躺在樹下死了,身上蓋滿白花。

chapters.title: The Devoted Friend 忠實的朋友

passages.original: ONE morning the old Water-rat put his head out of his hole. He had bright beady eyes and stiff grey whiskers and his tail was like a long bit of black india-rubber. The little ducks were swimming about in the pond, looking just like a lot of yellow canaries, and their mother, who was pure white with real red legs, was trying to teach them how to stand on their heads in the water.
passages.vernacular: 一天早晨,老水鼠把頭從洞裡探出嚟。佢有明亮嘅珠子般嘅眼睛同硬硬嘅灰鬍鬚,尾巴像一長條黑色橡膠。小鴨子哋喺池塘裡游嚟游去,睇起嚟就像一群黃色金絲雀,佢哋嘅母親,純白色,有真正嘅紅腿,正在試住教佢哋點樣喺水裡倒立。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天早晨,老水鼠把頭從洞裡探出來。他有明亮的珠子般的眼睛和硬硬的灰鬍鬚,尾巴像一長條黑色橡膠。小鴨子們在池塘裡游來游去,看起來就像一群黃色金絲雀,他們的母親,純白色,有真正的紅腿,正在試著教他們怎樣在水裡倒立。

passages.original: “You will never be in the best society unless you can stand on your heads,” she kept saying to them; and every now and then she showed them how it was done. But the little ducks paid no attention to her. They were so young that they did not know what an advantage it is to be in society at all.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋除非能倒立,否則永遠進不咗上流社會,」佢不斷地對佢哋講;不時仲示範點做。但小鴨子哋不理佢。佢哋太年輕喇,唔知道能進入社交界係多大嘅好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們除非能倒立,否則永遠進不了上流社會,」她不斷地對他們說;不時還示範怎麼做。但小鴨子們不理她。他們太年輕了,不知道能進入社交界是多大的好處。

passages.original: “What disobedient children!” cried the old Water-rat; “they really deserve to be drowned.”
passages.vernacular: 「幾咁不聽話嘅細路!」老水鼠喊道;「佢哋真該被淹死。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多麼不聽話的孩子!」老水鼠喊道;「他們真該被淹死。」

passages.original: “Nothing of the kind,” answered the Duck, “every one must make a beginning, and parents cannot be too patient.”
passages.vernacular: 「完全唔係嗰樣,」鴨子回答,「每個人都得有個開始,父母點有耐心都不為過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「完全不是那樣,」鴨子回答,「每個人都得有個開始,父母怎麼有耐心都不為過。」

passages.original: “Ah! I know nothing about the feelings of parents,” said the Water-rat; “I am not a family man. In fact, I have never been married, and I never intend to be. Love is all very well in its way, but friendship is much higher. Indeed, I know of nothing in the world that is either nobler or rarer than a devoted friendship.”
passages.vernacular: 「啊!我對父母嘅感情一無所知,」水鼠講;「我唔係個有家嘅人。事實上,我從冇結過婚,都不打算結。愛情喺佢嘅方式上好好,但友誼要高得多。確實,我知道世上冇比忠實嘅友誼更高貴或更稀有嘅嘢喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!我對父母的感情一無所知,」水鼠說;「我不是個有家的人。事實上,我從沒結過婚,也不打算結。愛情在它的方式上很好,但友誼要高得多。確實,我知道世上沒有比忠實的友誼更高貴或更稀有的東西了。」

passages.original: “And what, pray, is your idea of the duties of a devoted friend?” asked a Green Linnet, who was sitting in a willow-tree hard by, and had overheard the conversation.
passages.vernacular: 「請問,你認為忠實朋友嘅責任係乜嘢?」一隻綠紅雀問,佢坐喺附近一棵柳樹上,偷聽到咗呢番談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請問,你認為忠實朋友的責任是什麼?」一隻綠紅雀問,他坐在附近一棵柳樹上,偷聽到了這番談話。

passages.original: “Yes, that is just what I want to know,” said the Duck; and she swam away to the end of the pond, and stood upon her head, in order to give her children a good example.
passages.vernacular: 「對,呢正是我想知道嘅,」鴨子講;佢游到池塘盡頭,倒立起嚟,畀佢嘅細路哋做個好榜樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,這正是我想知道的,」鴨子說;她游到池塘盡頭,倒立起來,給她的孩子們做個好榜樣。

passages.original: “What a silly question!” cried the Water-rat. “I should expect my devoted friend to be devoted to me, of course.”
passages.vernacular: 「幾咁愚蠢嘅問題!」水鼠喊道。「我當然期望我忠實嘅朋友對我忠實。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多麼愚蠢的問題!」水鼠喊道。「我當然期望我忠實的朋友對我忠實。」

passages.original: “And what would you do in return?” said the little bird, swinging upon a silver spray, and flapping his tiny wings.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你會做乜嘢作為回報?」小鳥講,喺一根銀色嘅嫩枝上搖晃,拍住小小嘅翅膀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你會做什麼作為回報?」小鳥說,在一根銀色的嫩枝上搖晃,拍著小小的翅膀。

passages.original: “I don’t understand you,” answered the Water-rat.
passages.vernacular: 「我不明白你嘅意思,」水鼠回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不明白你的意思,」水鼠回答。

passages.original: “Let me tell you a story on the subject,” said the Linnet.
passages.vernacular: 「讓我畀你講一個關於呢個主題嘅故事,」紅雀講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我給你講一個關於這個主題的故事,」紅雀說。

passages.original: “Is the story about me?” asked the Water-rat. “If so, I will listen to it, for I am extremely fond of fiction.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢故事係關於我嘅嗎?」水鼠問。「如果係,我就聽,因為我好鍾意小講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這故事是關於我的嗎?」水鼠問。「如果是,我就聽,因為我非常喜歡小說。」

passages.original: “It is applicable to you,” answered the Linnet; and he flew down, and alighting upon the bank, he told the story of The Devoted Friend.
passages.vernacular: 「佢適用於你,」紅雀回答;佢飛下嚟,落喺岸邊,講咗〈忠實嘅朋友〉嘅故事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它適用於你,」紅雀回答;他飛下來,落在岸邊,講了〈忠實的朋友〉的故事。

passages.original: “Once upon a time,” said the Linnet, “there was an honest little fellow named Hans.”
passages.vernacular: 「從前,」紅雀講,「有一個誠實嘅小伙子叫漢斯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從前,」紅雀說,「有一個誠實的小伙子叫漢斯。」

passages.original: “Was he very distinguished?” asked the Water-rat.
passages.vernacular: 「佢好傑出嗎?」水鼠問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他很傑出嗎?」水鼠問。

passages.original: “No,” answered the Linnet, “I don’t think he was distinguished at all, except for his kind heart, and his funny round good-humoured face. He lived in a tiny cottage all by himself, and every day he worked in his garden. In all the country-side there was no garden so lovely as his. Sweet-william grew there, and Gilly-flowers, and Shepherds’-purses, and Fair-maids of France. There were damask Roses, and yellow Roses, lilac Crocuses, and gold, purple Violets and white. Columbine and Ladysmock, Marjoram and Wild Basil, the Cowslip and the Flower-de-luce, the Daffodil and the Clove-Pink bloomed or blossomed in their proper order as the months went by, one flower taking another flower’s place, so that there were always beautiful things to look at, and pleasant odours to smell.
passages.vernacular: 「不,」紅雀回答,「我想佢啲都不傑出,除咗佢善良嘅心,同佢嗰張滑稽嘅圓圓嘅好脾氣嘅臉。佢獨自住喺一間小茅屋裡,每天喺佢嘅花園裡工作。整個鄉間冇一座花園像佢嘅咁可愛。嗰度長住美國石竹、紫羅蘭、薺菜,同法蘭西美人花。有大馬士革玫瑰、黃玫瑰、淡紫色嘅番紅花同金色嘅,紫色嘅紫羅蘭同白色嘅。耬斗菜同布穀鳥花、馬郁蘭同野羅勒、黃花九輪草同鳶尾花、水仙同丁香石竹,隨住月份過去,依時序開花,一種花接替另一種花嘅位置,所以總有美麗嘅嘢可睇,有宜人嘅香氣可聞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,」紅雀回答,「我想他一點也不傑出,除了他善良的心,和他那張滑稽的圓圓的好脾氣的臉。他獨自住在一間小茅屋裡,每天在他的花園裡工作。整個鄉間沒有一座花園像他的那麼可愛。那裡長著美國石竹、紫羅蘭、薺菜,和法蘭西美人花。有大馬士革玫瑰、黃玫瑰、淡紫色的番紅花和金色的,紫色的紫羅蘭和白色的。耬斗菜和布穀鳥花、馬郁蘭和野羅勒、黃花九輪草和鳶尾花、水仙和丁香石竹,隨著月份過去,依時序開花,一種花接替另一種花的位置,所以總有美麗的東西可看,有宜人的香氣可聞。

passages.original: “Little Hans had a great many friends, but the most devoted friend of all was big Hugh the Miller.
