Indeed, so devoted was the rich Miller to little Hans, that he would never go by his garden without leaning over the wall and plucking a large nosegay, or a handful of sweet herbs, or filling his pockets with plums and cherries if it was the fruit season.
passages.vernacular: 「小漢斯有好多朋友,但最忠實嘅朋友係大個子磨坊主休。確實,富有嘅磨坊主對小漢斯咁忠實,佢經過佢嘅花園時,從唔會不靠喺牆上摘一大束花,或一把香草,如果係水果季節,仲把口袋裝滿李子同櫻桃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「小漢斯有很多朋友,但最忠實的朋友是大個子磨坊主休。確實,富有的磨坊主對小漢斯那麼忠實,他經過他的花園時,從不會不靠在牆上摘一大束花,或一把香草,如果是水果季節,還把口袋裝滿李子和櫻桃。

passages.original: “‘Real friends should have everything in common,’ the Miller used to say, and little Hans nodded and smiled, and felt very proud of having a friend with such noble ideas.
passages.vernacular: 「『真正嘅朋友應該有福同享,』磨坊主常講,小漢斯點頭微笑,為有咁樣一個有高尚思想嘅朋友感到好自豪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『真正的朋友應該有福同享,』磨坊主常說,小漢斯點頭微笑,為有這樣一個有高尚思想的朋友感到十分自豪。

passages.original: “Sometimes, indeed, the neighbours thought it strange that the rich Miller never gave little Hans anything in return, though he had a hundred sacks of flour stored away in his mill, and six milch cows, and a large flock of woolly sheep; but Hans never troubled his head about these things, and nothing gave him greater pleasure than to listen to all the wonderful things the Miller used to say about the unselfishness of true friendship.
passages.vernacular: 「有時,確實,鄰居哋覺得奇怪,富有嘅磨坊主從不回報小漢斯任何嘢,雖然佢磨坊裡貯藏住一百袋麵粉,有六頭奶牛,同一大群毛茸茸嘅羊;但漢斯從不為呢啲事操心,冇乜嘢比聽磨坊主講關於真正友誼嘅無私嘅所有奇妙話語更讓佢高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有時,確實,鄰居們覺得奇怪,富有的磨坊主從不回報小漢斯任何東西,雖然他磨坊裡貯藏著一百袋麵粉,有六頭奶牛,和一大群毛茸茸的羊;但漢斯從不為這些事操心,沒有什麼比聽磨坊主說關於真正友誼的無私的所有奇妙話語更讓他高興。

passages.original: “So little Hans worked away in his garden. During the spring, the summer, and the autumn he was very happy, but when the winter came, and he had no fruit or flowers to bring to the market, he suffered a good deal from cold and hunger, and often had to go to bed without any supper but a few dried pears or some hard nuts. In the winter, also, he was extremely lonely, as the Miller never came to see him then.
passages.vernacular: 「於是小漢斯喺佢嘅花園裡辛勤工作。春天、夏天同秋天佢好快樂,但冬天嚟喇,佢冇水果或花攞到市場上去,佢食咗好多冷同餓嘅苦,常常唔得不空住肚子上床,只有幾個乾梨子或啲硬堅果。冬天佢都極其孤獨,因為嗰時磨坊主從不嚟睇佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「於是小漢斯在他的花園裡辛勤工作。春天、夏天和秋天他很快樂,但冬天來了,他沒有水果或花拿到市場上去,他吃了很多冷和餓的苦,常常不得不空著肚子上床,只有幾個乾梨子或一些硬堅果。冬天他也極其孤獨,因為那時磨坊主從不來看他。

passages.original: “‘There is no good in my going to see little Hans as long as the snow lasts,’ the Miller used to say to his wife, ‘for when people are in trouble they should be left alone, and not be bothered by visitors. That at least is my idea about friendship, and I am sure I am right. So I shall wait till the spring comes, and then I shall pay him a visit, and he will be able to give me a large basket of primroses and that will make him so happy.’
passages.vernacular: 「『只要雪仲喺,我去睇小漢斯就冇好處,』磨坊主常對佢嘅妻子講,『因為人哋有困難時,應該讓佢哋獨自待住,不被訪客打擾。呢至少係我對友誼嘅睇法,我肯定我係對嘅。所以我要等到春天嚟喇,然後我去拜訪佢,佢能畀我一大籃櫻草花,嗰會使佢好快樂。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『只要雪還在,我去看小漢斯就沒有好處,』磨坊主常對他的妻子說,『因為人們有困難時,應該讓他們獨自待著,不被訪客打擾。這至少是我對友誼的看法,我肯定我是對的。所以我要等到春天來了,然後我去拜訪他,他能給我一大籃櫻草花,那會使他非常快樂。』

passages.original: “‘You are certainly very thoughtful about others,’ answered the Wife, as she sat in her comfortable armchair by the big pinewood fire; ‘very thoughtful indeed. It is quite a treat to hear you talk about friendship. I am sure the clergyman himself could not say such beautiful things as you do, though he does live in a three-storied house, and wear a gold ring on his little finger.’
passages.vernacular: 「『你確實好為別人著想,』妻子回答,佢坐喺大松木火旁舒適嘅扶手椅上;『真嘅好體貼。聽你談論友誼簡直係一種享受。我肯定牧師自己都講不出像你咁樣美嘅話,雖然佢住喺三層樓嘅房子裡,小指上戴住金戒指。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你確實非常為別人著想,』妻子回答,她坐在大松木火旁舒適的扶手椅上;『真的非常體貼。聽你談論友誼簡直是一種享受。我肯定牧師自己也說不出像你這樣美的話,雖然他住在三層樓的房子裡,小指上戴著金戒指。』

passages.original: “‘But could we not ask little Hans up here?’ said the Miller’s youngest son. ‘If poor Hans is in trouble I will give him half my porridge, and show him my white rabbits.’
passages.vernacular: 「『但我哋唔能夠請小漢斯上嚟嗎?』磨坊主最小嘅兒子講。『如果可憐嘅漢斯有困難,我會分佢一半我嘅粥,畀佢睇我嘅白兔子。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『但我們不能請小漢斯上來嗎?』磨坊主最小的兒子說。『如果可憐的漢斯有困難,我會分他一半我的粥,給他看我的白兔子。』

passages.original: “‘What a silly boy you are!’ cried the Miller; ‘I really don’t know what is the use of sending you to school. You seem not to learn anything. Why, if little Hans came up here, and saw our warm fire, and our good supper, and our great cask of red wine, he might get envious, and envy is a most terrible thing, and would spoil anybody’s nature. I certainly will not allow Hans’ nature to be spoiled. I am his best friend, and I will always watch over him, and see that he is not led into any temptations. Besides, if Hans came here, he might ask me to let him have some flour on credit, and that I could not do. Flour is one thing, and friendship is another, and they should not be confused. Why, the words are spelt differently, and mean quite different things. Everybody can see that.’
passages.vernacular: 「『你呢細路真蠢!』磨坊主喊道;『我真唔知道送你上學有乜嘢用。你似乎乜嘢都冇學到。哎呀,如果小漢斯上嚟,睇到我哋暖同嘅火、我哋豐盛嘅晚餐同我哋大桶嘅紅酒,佢可能會嫉妒,而嫉妒係最可怕嘅嘢,會敗壞任何人嘅天性。我絕唔會允許漢斯嘅天性被敗壞。我係佢最好嘅朋友,我會一直睇護佢,確保佢不被引入任何誘惑。而且,如果漢斯嚟呢度,佢可能要求我賒畀佢啲麵粉,嗰個係我做唔到嘅。麵粉係一回事,友誼係另一回事,佢哋不該被混淆。哎呀,呢兩個詞拼寫不同,意思都完全不同。每個人都睇得出嚟。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你這孩子真蠢!』磨坊主喊道;『我真不知道送你上學有什麼用。你似乎什麼也沒學到。哎呀,如果小漢斯上來,看到我們暖和的火、我們豐盛的晚餐和我們大桶的紅酒,他可能會嫉妒,而嫉妒是最可怕的東西,會敗壞任何人的天性。我絕不會允許漢斯的天性被敗壞。我是他最好的朋友,我會一直看護他,確保他不被引入任何誘惑。而且,如果漢斯來這裡,他可能要求我賒給他一些麵粉,那是我做不到的。麵粉是一回事,友誼是另一回事,它們不該被混淆。哎呀,這兩個詞拼寫不同,意思也完全不同。每個人都看得出來。』

passages.original: “‘How well you talk!’ said the Miller’s Wife, pouring herself out a large glass of warm ale; ‘really I feel quite drowsy. It is just like being in church.’
passages.vernacular: 「『你講得多好!』磨坊主嘅妻子講,畀自己倒咗一大杯溫啤酒;『真嘅我覺得相當睏。就像喺教堂裡一樣。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你說得多好!』磨坊主的妻子說,給自己倒了一大杯溫啤酒;『真的我覺得相當睏。就像在教堂裡一樣。』

passages.original: “‘Lots of people act well,’ answered the Miller; ‘but very few people talk well, which shows that talking is much the more difficult thing of the two, and much the finer thing also’; and he looked sternly across the table at his little son, who felt so ashamed of himself that he hung his head down, and grew quite scarlet, and began to cry into his tea. However, he was so young that you must excuse him.”
passages.vernacular: 「『好多人做得好,』磨坊主回答;『但好少人講得好,呢表明講比做難得多,都高雅得多』;佢嚴厲地隔住桌子睇佢嘅小兒子,嗰細路羞愧得垂下頭,臉變得通紅,開始哭到茶杯裡。不過,佢太年輕喇,你必須原諒佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『很多人做得好,』磨坊主回答;『但很少人說得好,這表明說比做難得多,也高雅得多』;他嚴厲地隔著桌子看他的小兒子,那孩子羞愧得垂下頭,臉變得通紅,開始哭到茶杯裡。不過,他太年輕了,你必須原諒他。」

passages.original: “Is that the end of the story?” asked the Water-rat.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係故事嘅結尾嗎?」水鼠問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是故事的結尾嗎?」水鼠問。

passages.original: “Certainly not,” answered the Linnet, “that is the beginning.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然唔係,」紅雀回答,「呢個係開頭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然不是,」紅雀回答,「這是開頭。」

passages.original: “Then you are quite behind the age,” said the Water-rat. “Every good story-teller nowadays starts with the end, and then goes on to the beginning, and concludes with the middle. That is the new method. I heard all about it the other day from a critic who was walking round the pond with a young man. He spoke of the matter at great length, and I am sure he must have been right, for he had blue spectacles and a bald head, and whenever the young man made any remark, he always answered ‘Pooh!’ But pray go on with your story. I like the Miller immensely. I have all kinds of beautiful sentiments myself, so there is a great sympathy between us.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你就落後於時代喇,」水鼠講。「而家每個好嘅講故事人都從結尾開始,然後講到開頭,以中間結束。呢個係新方法。前幾天我從一個同一個年輕人繞住池塘散步嘅評論家嗰度聽講咗呢一切。佢好詳細地談論呢件事,我肯定佢一定係對嘅,因為佢戴住藍眼鏡,頭禿喇,每當年輕人發表意見,佢總是回答『呸!』但請繼續你嘅故事。我好鍾意嗰個磨坊主。我自己都有各種各樣嘅美好情感,所以我哋之間有好大嘅共鳴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你就落後於時代了,」水鼠說。「現在每個好的說故事人都從結尾開始,然後講到開頭,以中間結束。這是新方法。前幾天我從一個同一個年輕人繞著池塘散步的評論家那裡聽說了這一切。他非常詳細地談論這件事,我肯定他一定是對的,因為他戴著藍眼鏡,頭禿了,每當年輕人發表意見,他總是回答『呸!』但請繼續你的故事。我非常喜歡那個磨坊主。我自己也有各種各樣的美好情感,所以我們之間有很大的共鳴。」

passages.original: “Well,” said the Linnet, hopping now on one leg and now on the other, “as soon as the winter was over, and the primroses began to open their pale yellow stars, the Miller said to his wife that he would go down and see little Hans.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」紅雀講,一會兒單腳跳,一會兒換另一隻腳,「冬天一過,櫻草花開始綻放佢哋淡黃色嘅星星時,磨坊主對妻子講佢要下去睇睇小漢斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」紅雀說,一會兒單腳跳,一會兒換另一隻腳,「冬天一過,櫻草花開始綻放它們淡黃色的星星時,磨坊主對妻子說他要下去看看小漢斯。

passages.original: “‘Why, what a good heart you have!’ cried his Wife; ‘you are always thinking of others. And mind you take the big basket with you for the flowers.’
passages.vernacular: 「『哎呀,你嘅心幾咁好!』佢嘅妻子喊道;『你總是想住別人。記得帶上大籃子裝花。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哎呀,你的心多麼好!』他的妻子喊道;『你總是想著別人。記得帶上大籃子裝花。』

passages.original: “So the Miller tied the sails of the windmill together with a strong iron chain, and went down the hill with the basket on his arm.
passages.vernacular: 「於是磨坊主用一條堅固嘅鐵鏈把風車嘅葉片綁喺一起,手臂上挎住籃子下山喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「於是磨坊主用一條堅固的鐵鏈把風車的葉片綁在一起,手臂上挎著籃子下山了。

passages.original: “‘Good morning, little Hans,’ said the Miller.
passages.vernacular: 「『早安,小漢斯,』磨坊主講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『早安,小漢斯,』磨坊主說。

passages.original: “‘Good morning,’ said Hans, leaning on his spade, and smiling from ear to ear.
passages.vernacular: 「『早安,』漢斯講,倚住佢嘅鏟子,笑得咧到耳根。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『早安,』漢斯說,倚著他的鏟子,笑得咧到耳根。

passages.original: “‘And how have you been all the winter?’ said the Miller.
passages.vernacular: 「『你整個冬天過得點樣?』磨坊主講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你整個冬天過得怎麼樣?』磨坊主說。

passages.original: “‘Well, really,’ cried Hans, ‘it is very good of you to ask, very good indeed. I am afraid I had rather a hard time of it, but now the spring has come, and I am quite happy, and all my flowers are doing well.’
passages.vernacular: 「『講真嘅,』漢斯喊道,『你肯問,真係太好喇,真嘅太好喇。我恐怕過得相當艱難,但而家春天嚟喇,我好快樂,我所有嘅花都長得好好。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『說真的,』漢斯喊道,『你肯問,真是太好了,真的太好了。我恐怕過得相當艱難,但現在春天來了,我很快樂,我所有的花都長得很好。』

passages.original: “‘We often talked of you during the winter, Hans,’ said the Miller, ‘and wondered how you were getting on.’
passages.vernacular: 「『冬天我哋常常談起你,漢斯,』磨坊主講,『想知道你過得點樣。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『冬天我們常常談起你,漢斯,』磨坊主說,『想知道你過得怎樣。』

passages.original: “‘That was kind of you,’ said Hans; ‘I was half afraid you had forgotten me.’
passages.vernacular: 「『你哋真好,』漢斯講;『我有一半怕你哋忘咗我。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你們真好,』漢斯說;『我有一半怕你們忘了我。』

passages.original: “‘Hans, I am surprised at you,’ said the Miller; ‘friendship never forgets. That is the wonderful thing about it, but I am afraid you don’t understand the poetry of life. How lovely your primroses are looking, by-the-bye!”
passages.vernacular: 「『漢斯,你真讓我驚訝,』磨坊主講;『友誼從唔會忘記。嗰個係佢奇妙嘅地方,但我恐怕你不懂生活嘅詩意。順便講一句,你嘅櫻草花睇起嚟幾咁可愛!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『漢斯,你真讓我驚訝,』磨坊主說;『友誼從不會忘記。那是它奇妙的地方,但我恐怕你不懂生活的詩意。順便說一句,你的櫻草花看起來多麼可愛!』

passages.original: “‘They are certainly very lovely,’ said Hans, ‘and it is a most lucky thing for me that I have so many. I am going to bring them into the market and sell them to the Burgomaster’s daughter, and buy back my wheelbarrow with the money.’
passages.vernacular: 「『佢哋確實好可愛,』漢斯講,『我有咁多,對我係極其幸運嘅事。我要把佢哋攞到市場上賣畀市長嘅女兒,用嗰筆錢把我嘅手推車買回嚟。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『它們確實很可愛,』漢斯說,『我有這麼多,對我是極其幸運的事。我要把它們拿到市場上賣給市長的女兒,用那筆錢把我的手推車買回來。』

passages.original: “‘Buy back your wheelbarrow? You don’t mean to say you have sold it? What a very stupid thing to do!’
passages.vernacular: 「『把你嘅手推車買回嚟?你唔係講你把佢賣咗吧?嗰個係幾咁愚蠢嘅事!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『把你的手推車買回來?你不是說你把它賣了吧?那是多麼愚蠢的事!』

passages.original: “‘Well, the fact is,’ said Hans, ‘that I was obliged to. You see the winter was a very bad time for me, and I really had no money at all to buy bread with. So I first sold the silver buttons off my Sunday coat, and then I sold my silver chain, and then I sold my big pipe, and at last I sold my wheelbarrow. But I am going to buy them all back again now.’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗯,事實係,』漢斯講,『我唔得不賣。你睇冬天對我係好艱難嘅時期,我真嘅啲錢都冇買麵包。所以我先賣咗我星期日外套上嘅銀鈕扣,然後賣咗我嘅銀鏈子,然後賣咗我嘅大菸斗,最後賣咗我嘅手推車。但我而家要把佢哋都買回嚟。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『嗯,事實是,』漢斯說,『我不得不賣。你看冬天對我是很艱難的時期,我真的一點錢也沒有買麵包。所以我先賣了我星期日外套上的銀鈕扣,然後賣了我的銀鏈子,然後賣了我的大菸斗,最後賣了我的手推車。但我現在要把它們都買回來。』

passages.original: “‘Hans,’ said the Miller, ‘I will give you my wheelbarrow. It is not in very good repair; indeed, one side is gone, and there is something wrong with the wheel-spokes; but in spite of that I will give it to you. I know it is very generous of me, and a great many people would think me extremely foolish for parting with it, but I am not like the rest of the world. I think that generosity is the essence of friendship, and, besides, I have got a new wheelbarrow for myself. Yes, you may set your mind at ease, I will give you my wheelbarrow.’
passages.vernacular: 「『漢斯,』磨坊主講,『我把我嘅手推車畀你。佢修得不太好;確實,一邊冇喇,輻條都有點毛病;但儘管如此我定係把佢畀你。我知道呢對我來講好慷慨,好多人會認為我把佢送出去極其愚蠢,但我不像世上其他人。我認為慷慨係友誼嘅本質,而且,我畀自己有咗一輛新手推車。係嘅,你可以放心,我把我嘅手推車畀你。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『漢斯,』磨坊主說,『我把我的手推車給你。它修得不太好;確實,一邊沒了,輻條也有點毛病;但儘管如此我還是把它給你。我知道這對我來說非常慷慨,很多人會認為我把它送出去極其愚蠢,但我不像世上其他人。我認為慷慨是友誼的本質,而且,我給自己有了一輛新手推車。是的,你可以放心,我把我的手推車給你。』

passages.original: “‘Well, really, that is generous of you,’ said little Hans, and his funny round face glowed all over with pleasure. ‘I can easily put it in repair, as I have a plank of wood in the house.’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗯,真嘅,你太慷慨喇,』小漢斯講,佢滑稽嘅圓臉上洋溢住喜悅。『我可以輕易把佢修好,因為我家裡有一塊木板。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『嗯,真的,你太慷慨了,』小漢斯說,他滑稽的圓臉上洋溢著喜悅。『我可以輕易把它修好,因為我家裡有一塊木板。』

passages.original: “‘A plank of wood!’ said the Miller; ‘why, that is just what I want for the roof of my barn. There is a very large hole in it, and the corn will all get damp if I don’t stop it up. How lucky you mentioned it! It is quite remarkable how one good action always breeds another. I have given you my wheelbarrow, and now you are going to give me your plank. Of course, the wheelbarrow is worth far more than the plank, but true, friendship never notices things like that. Pray get it at once, and I will set to work at my barn this very day.’
passages.vernacular: 「『一塊木板!』磨坊主講;『哎呀,嗰正是我需要嘅,用嚟修我穀倉嘅屋頂。上面有個好大嘅洞,如果我不把佢堵上,玉米都會受潮。你提起佢真係太巧喇!一件好事總是帶嚟另一件好事,呢真係了不起。我畀咗你我嘅手推車,而家你要畀我你嘅木板。當然,手推車比木板值錢得多,但真正嘅友誼從不注意呢類事。請即刻去攞嚟,我今日就開始修我嘅穀倉。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『一塊木板!』磨坊主說;『哎呀,那正是我需要的,用來修我穀倉的屋頂。上面有個很大的洞,如果我不把它堵上,玉米都會受潮。你提起它真是太巧了!一件好事總是帶來另一件好事,這真是了不起。我給了你我的手推車,現在你要給我你的木板。當然,手推車比木板值錢得多,但真正的友誼從不注意這類事。請馬上去拿來,我今天就開始修我的穀倉。』

passages.original: “‘Certainly,’ cried little Hans, and he ran into the shed and dragged the plank out.
passages.vernacular: 「『當然,』小漢斯喊道,佢跑進棚子,把木板拖咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『當然,』小漢斯喊道,他跑進棚子,把木板拖了出來。

passages.original: “‘It is not a very big plank,’ said the Miller, looking at it, ‘and I am afraid that after I have mended my barn-roof there won’t be any left for you to mend the wheelbarrow with; but, of course, that is not my fault. And now, as I have given you my wheelbarrow, I am sure you would like to give me some flowers in return. Here is the basket, and mind you fill it quite full.’
passages.vernacular: 「『呢唔係好大嘅木板,』磨坊主睇住佢講,『我恐怕我修完穀倉屋頂後,就唔會剩下任何畀你修手推車喇;但係,當然,呢唔係我嘅錯。而家,既然我畀咗你我嘅手推車,我肯定你想畀我啲花作為回報。籃子喺呢度,記得把佢裝得滿滿嘅。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『這不是很大的木板,』磨坊主看著它說,『我恐怕我修完穀倉屋頂後,就不會剩下任何給你修手推車了;但是,當然,這不是我的錯。現在,既然我給了你我的手推車,我肯定你想給我一些花作為回報。籃子在這裡,記得把它裝得滿滿的。』

passages.original: “‘Quite full?’ said little Hans, rather sorrowfully, for it was really a very big basket, and he knew that if he filled it he would have no flowers left for the market and he was very anxious to get his silver buttons back.
passages.vernacular: 「『裝得滿滿嘅?』小漢斯相當悲傷地講,因為嗰確實係個好大嘅籃子,佢知道如果佢裝滿喇,佢就冇花攞到市場去喇,而佢好想把佢嘅銀鈕扣買回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『裝得滿滿的?』小漢斯相當悲傷地說,因為那確實是個很大的籃子,他知道如果他裝滿了,他就沒有花拿到市場去了,而他非常想把他的銀鈕扣買回來。

passages.original: “‘Well, really,’ answered the Miller, ‘as I have given you my wheelbarrow, I don’t think that it is much to ask you for a few flowers. I may be wrong, but I should have thought that friendship, true friendship, was quite free from selfishness of any kind.’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗯,真嘅,』磨坊主回答,『既然我畀咗你我嘅手推車,我不認為向你要幾朵花算得上要求好多。我可能錯喇,但我本以為友誼,真正嘅友誼,係完全冇任何自私嘅。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『嗯,真的,』磨坊主回答,『既然我給了你我的手推車,我不認為向你要幾朵花算得上要求很多。我可能錯了,但我本以為友誼,真正的友誼,是完全沒有任何自私的。』

passages.original: “‘My dear friend, my best friend,’ cried little Hans, ‘you are welcome to all the flowers in my garden. I would much sooner have your good opinion than my silver buttons, any day’; and he ran and plucked all his pretty primroses, and filled the Miller’s basket.
passages.vernacular: 「『我親愛嘅朋友,我最好嘅朋友,』小漢斯喊道,『我花園裡所有嘅花你都歡迎攞。我寧願要你嘅好評價,都唔好我嘅銀鈕扣,任何時候都係』;佢跑去摘下所有漂亮嘅櫻草花,裝滿咗磨坊主嘅籃子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我親愛的朋友,我最好的朋友,』小漢斯喊道,『我花園裡所有的花你都歡迎拿。我寧願要你的好評價,也不要我的銀鈕扣,任何時候都是』;他跑去摘下所有漂亮的櫻草花,裝滿了磨坊主的籃子。

passages.original: “‘Good-bye, little Hans,’ said the Miller, as he went up the hill with the plank on his shoulder, and the big basket in his hand.
passages.vernacular: 「『再見,小漢斯,』磨坊主講,肩上扛住木板,手裡拎住大籃子走上山去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『再見,小漢斯,』磨坊主說,肩上扛著木板,手裡拎著大籃子走上山去。

passages.original: “‘Good-bye,’ said little Hans, and he began to dig away quite merrily, he was so pleased about the wheelbarrow.
passages.vernacular: 「『再見,』小漢斯講,佢開始相當歡快地挖地,佢為手推車嘅事咁高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『再見,』小漢斯說,他開始相當歡快地挖地,他為手推車的事那麼高興。

passages.original: “The next day he was nailing up some honeysuckle against the porch, when he heard the Miller’s voice calling to him from the road. So he jumped off the ladder, and ran down the garden, and looked over the wall.
passages.vernacular: 「第二天佢正在門廊上釘忍冬藤,聽到磨坊主嘅聲音從路上叫佢。於是佢從梯子上跳下嚟,跑下花園,從牆上往外睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「第二天他正在門廊上釘忍冬藤,聽到磨坊主的聲音從路上叫他。於是他從梯子上跳下來,跑下花園,從牆上往外看。

passages.original: “There was the Miller with a large sack of flour on his back.
passages.vernacular: 「磨坊主背住一大袋麵粉站喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「磨坊主背著一大袋麵粉站在那裡。

passages.original: “‘Dear little Hans,’ said the Miller, ‘would you mind carrying this sack of flour for me to market?’
passages.vernacular: 「『親愛嘅小漢斯,』磨坊主講,『你介意替我把呢袋麵粉背到市場去嗎?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『親愛的小漢斯,』磨坊主說,『你介意替我把這袋麵粉背到市場去嗎?』

passages.original: “‘Oh, I am so sorry,’ said Hans, ‘but I am really very busy to-day. I have got all my creepers to nail up, and all my flowers to water, and all my grass to roll.’
passages.vernacular: 「『哦,我好抱歉,』漢斯講,『但我今日真嘅好忙。我有所有嘅攀緣植物要釘,所有嘅花要澆水,所有嘅草要碾平。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦,我很抱歉,』漢斯說,『但我今天真的很忙。我有所有的攀緣植物要釘,所有的花要澆水,所有的草要碾平。』

passages.original: “‘Well, really,’ said the Miller, ‘I think that, considering that I am going to give you my wheelbarrow, it is rather unfriendly of you to refuse.’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗯,真嘅,』磨坊主講,『我想,考慮到我要畀你我嘅手推車,你拒絕係相當不友好嘅。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『嗯,真的,』磨坊主說,『我想,考慮到我要給你我的手推車,你拒絕是相當不友好的。』

passages.original: “‘Oh, don’t say that,’ cried little Hans, ‘I wouldn’t be unfriendly for the whole world’; and he ran in for his cap, and trudged off with the big sack on his shoulders.
passages.vernacular: 「『哦,別咁講,』小漢斯喊道,『我為全世界都唔願不友好』;佢跑進去攞帽子,肩上扛住大袋子艱難地走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦,別這麼說,』小漢斯喊道,『我為全世界也不願不友好』;他跑進去拿帽子,肩上扛著大袋子艱難地走了。

passages.original: “It was a very hot day, and the road was terribly dusty, and before Hans had reached the sixth milestone he was so tired that he had to sit down and rest. However, he went on bravely, and as last he reached the market. After he had waited there some time, he sold the sack of flour for a very good price, and then he returned home at once, for he was afraid that if he stopped too late he might meet some robbers on the way.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰天好熱,路上塵土飛揚,漢斯仲冇走到第六塊里程碑就累得唔得不坐下休息。不過佢勇敢地繼續走,最後到咗市場。喺嗰度等咗一會兒後,佢以好好嘅價錢賣咗嗰袋麵粉,然後即刻回家,因為佢怕如果太晚停留,可能喺路上遇到強盜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那天很熱,路上塵土飛揚,漢斯還沒走到第六塊里程碑就累得不得不坐下休息。不過他勇敢地繼續走,最後到了市場。在那裡等了一會兒後,他以很好的價錢賣了那袋麵粉,然後馬上回家,因為他怕如果太晚停留,可能在路上遇到強盜。

passages.original: “‘It has certainly been a hard day,’ said little Hans to himself as he was going to bed, ‘but I am glad I did not refuse the Miller, for he is my best friend, and, besides, he is going to give me his wheelbarrow.’
passages.vernacular: 「『呢確實係辛苦嘅一天,』小漢斯上床時對自己講,『但我好高興我冇拒絕磨坊主,因為佢係我最好嘅朋友,而且,佢要畀我佢嘅手推車。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『這確實是辛苦的一天,』小漢斯上床時對自己說,『但我很高興我沒有拒絕磨坊主,因為他是我最好的朋友,而且,他要給我他的手推車。』

passages.original: “Early the next morning the Miller came down to get the money for his sack of flour, but little Hans was so tired that he was still in bed.
passages.vernacular: 「第二天一早,磨坊主下嚟攞佢嗰袋麵粉嘅錢,但小漢斯太累喇,仲喺床上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「第二天一早,磨坊主下來拿他那袋麵粉的錢,但小漢斯太累了,還在床上。

passages.original: “‘Upon my word,’ said the Miller, ‘you are very lazy. Really, considering that I am going to give you my wheelbarrow, I think you might work harder. Idleness is a great sin, and I certainly don’t like any of my friends to be idle or sluggish. You must not mind my speaking quite plainly to you. Of course I should not dream of doing so if I were not your friend. But what is the good of friendship if one cannot say exactly what one means? Anybody can say charming things and try to please and to flatter, but a true friend always says unpleasant things, and does not mind giving pain. Indeed, if he is a really true friend he prefers it, for he knows that then he is doing good.’
passages.vernacular: 「『講真嘅,』磨坊主講,『你太懶喇。真嘅,考慮到我要畀你我嘅手推車,我想你應該更努力工作。懶惰係好大嘅罪,我當然不鍾意我嘅任何朋友懶惰或遲鈍。你唔好介意我對你講得相當直白。當然如果我唔係你嘅朋友,我做夢都唔會咁樣做。但如果唔能夠講出自己嘅真正意思,友誼有乜嘢好處?任何人都可以講迷人嘅話,試圖取悅同奉承,但真正嘅朋友總是講不愉快嘅話,不介意畀人痛苦。確實,如果佢係真正嘅朋友,佢更鍾意咁樣,因為佢知道嗰樣佢係喺做好事。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『說真的,』磨坊主說,『你太懶了。真的,考慮到我要給你我的手推車,我想你應該更努力工作。懶惰是很大的罪,我當然不喜歡我的任何朋友懶惰或遲鈍。你不要介意我對你說得相當直白。當然如果我不是你的朋友,我做夢也不會這樣做。但如果不能說出自己的真正意思,友誼有什麼好處?任何人都可以說迷人的話,試圖取悅和奉承,但真正的朋友總是說不愉快的話,不介意給人痛苦。確實,如果他是真正的朋友,他更喜歡這樣,因為他知道那樣他是在做好事。』

passages.original: “‘I am very sorry,’ said little Hans, rubbing his eyes and pulling off his night-cap, ‘but I was so tired that I thought I would lie in bed for a little time, and listen to the birds singing. Do you know that I always work better after hearing the birds sing?’
passages.vernacular: 「『我好抱歉,』小漢斯講,揉住眼睛,脫下瞓帽,『但我太累喇,我想我可以喺床上躺一小會兒,聽鳥唱歌。你知道我聽咗鳥唱歌後總是工作得更好嗎?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我很抱歉,』小漢斯說,揉著眼睛,脫下睡帽,『但我太累了,我想我可以在床上躺一小會兒,聽鳥唱歌。你知道我聽了鳥唱歌後總是工作得更好嗎?』

passages.original: “‘Well, I am glad of that,’ said the Miller, clapping little Hans on the back, ‘for I want you to come up to the mill as soon as you are dressed, and mend my barn-roof for me.’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗯,我好高興聽到呢個,』磨坊主講,拍咗拍小漢斯嘅背,『因為我要你穿好衣服就到磨坊嚟,幫我修穀倉屋頂。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『嗯,我很高興聽到這個,』磨坊主說,拍了拍小漢斯的背,『因為我要你穿好衣服就到磨坊來,幫我修穀倉屋頂。』

passages.original: “Poor little Hans was very anxious to go and work in his garden, for his flowers had not been watered for two days, but he did not like to refuse the Miller, as he was such a good friend to him.
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅小漢斯好想去佢嘅花園工作,因為佢嘅花已經兩天冇澆水喇,但佢唔願拒絕磨坊主,因為佢對佢係咁好嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的小漢斯非常想去他的花園工作,因為他的花已經兩天沒澆水了,但他不願拒絕磨坊主,因為他對他是這麼好的朋友。

passages.original: “‘Do you think it would be unfriendly of me if I said I was busy?’ he inquired in a shy and timid voice.
passages.vernacular: 「『你認為如果我講我好忙,會不友好嗎?』佢用羞怯膽小嘅聲音問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你認為如果我說我很忙,會不友好嗎?』他用羞怯膽小的聲音問。

passages.original: “‘Well, really,’ answered the Miller, ‘I do not think it is much to ask of you, considering that I am going to give you my wheelbarrow; but of course if you refuse I will go and do it myself.’
passages.vernacular: 「『嗯,真嘅,』磨坊主回答,『考慮到我要畀你我嘅手推車,我不認為呢個係好多要求;不過當然如果你拒絕,我自己去做。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『嗯,真的,』磨坊主回答,『考慮到我要給你我的手推車,我不認為這是很多要求;不過當然如果你拒絕,我自己去做。』

passages.original: “‘Oh! on no account,’ cried little Hans and he jumped out of bed, and dressed himself, and went up to the barn.
passages.vernacular: 「『哦!絕不,』小漢斯喊道,佢跳下床,穿好衣服,去咗穀倉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦!絕不,』小漢斯喊道,他跳下床,穿好衣服,去了穀倉。

passages.original: “He worked there all day long, till sunset, and at sunset the Miller came to see how he was getting on.
passages.vernacular: 「佢喺嗰度工作咗一整天,直到日落,日落時磨坊主嚟睇佢做得點樣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他在那裡工作了一整天,直到日落,日落時磨坊主來看他做得怎樣了。

passages.original: “‘Have you mended the hole in the roof yet, little Hans?’ cried the Miller in a cheery voice.
passages.vernacular: 「『你修好屋頂上嘅洞咗嗎,小漢斯?』磨坊主用愉快嘅聲音喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你修好屋頂上的洞了嗎,小漢斯?』磨坊主用愉快的聲音喊道。

passages.original: “‘It is quite mended,’ answered little Hans, coming down the ladder.
passages.vernacular: 「『完全修好喇,』小漢斯從梯子上下嚟回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『完全修好了,』小漢斯從梯子上下來回答。

passages.original: “‘Ah!’ said the Miller, ‘there is no work so delightful as the work one does for others.’
passages.vernacular: 「『啊!』磨坊主講,『冇乜嘢工作比為別人做嘅更令人愉快喇。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『啊!』磨坊主說,『沒有什麼工作比為別人做的更令人愉快了。』

passages.original: “‘It is certainly a great privilege to hear you talk,’ answered little Hans, sitting down, and wiping his forehead, ‘a very great privilege. But I am afraid I shall never have such beautiful ideas as you have.’
passages.vernacular: 「『聽你講話確實係好大嘅榮幸,』小漢斯坐下嚟,擦住額頭回答,『好大嘅榮幸。但我怕我永遠唔會有像你嗰樣美嘅想法。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『聽你說話確實是很大的榮幸,』小漢斯坐下來,擦著額頭回答,『非常大的榮幸。但我怕我永遠不會有像你那樣美的想法。』

passages.original: “‘Oh! they will come to you,’ said the Miller, ‘but you must take more pains. At present you have only the practice of friendship; some day you will have the theory also.’
passages.vernacular: 「『哦!佢哋會嚟嘅,』磨坊主講,『但你必須更努力。目前你只有友誼嘅實踐;有一天你都會有理論。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『哦!它們會來的,』磨坊主說,『但你必須更努力。目前你只有友誼的實踐;有一天你也會有理論。』

passages.original: “‘Do you really think I shall?’ asked little Hans.
passages.vernacular: 「『你真嘅認為我會嗎?』小漢斯問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你真的認為我會嗎?』小漢斯問。

passages.original: “‘I have no doubt of it,’ answered the Miller, ‘but now that you have mended the roof, you had better go home and rest, for I want you to drive my sheep to the mountain to-morrow.’
passages.vernacular: 「『我毫不懷疑,』磨坊主回答,『但而家你修好咗屋頂,你最好回家休息,因為我要你聽日把我嘅羊趕到山上去。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我毫不懷疑,』磨坊主回答,『但現在你修好了屋頂,你最好回家休息,因為我要你明天把我的羊趕到山上去。』

passages.original: “Poor little Hans was afraid to say anything to this, and early the next morning the Miller brought his sheep round to the cottage, and Hans started off with them to the mountain. It took him the whole day to get there and back; and when he returned he was so tired that he went off to sleep in his chair, and did not wake up till it was broad daylight.
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅小漢斯唔敢對此講乜嘢,第二天一早,磨坊主把羊趕到茅屋,漢斯趕住牠哋往山上去。佢嚟回花咗一整天;佢回嚟時累得喺椅子上瞓住喇,直到大白天才醒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的小漢斯不敢對此說什麼,第二天一早,磨坊主把羊趕到茅屋,漢斯趕著牠們往山上去。他來回花了一整天;他回來時累得在椅子上睡著了,直到大白天才醒。

passages.original: “‘What a delightful time I shall have in my garden,’ he said, and he went to work at once.
passages.vernacular: 「『我喺花園裡會度過幾咁愉快嘅時光,』佢講,即刻開始工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我在花園裡會度過多麼愉快的時光,』他說,馬上開始工作。

passages.original: “But somehow he was never able to look after his flowers at all, for his friend the Miller was always coming round and sending him off on long errands, or getting him to help at the mill. Little Hans was very much distressed at times, as he was afraid his flowers would think he had forgotten them, but he consoled himself by the reflection that the Miller was his best friend. ‘Besides,’ he used to say, ‘he is going to give me his wheelbarrow, and that is an act of pure generosity.’
passages.vernacular: 「但唔知怎嘅,佢始終冇能照顧自己嘅花,因為佢嘅朋友磨坊主總是過嚟,派佢去辦長途差事,或者叫佢去磨坊幫忙。小漢斯有時好苦惱,因為怕佢嘅花會以為佢忘咗佢哋,但佢通過想住磨坊主係佢最好嘅朋友嚟安慰自己。『而且,』佢常講,『佢要畀我佢嘅手推車,嗰個係純粹慷慨嘅行為。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但不知怎的,他始終沒能照顧自己的花,因為他的朋友磨坊主總是過來,派他去辦長途差事,或者叫他去磨坊幫忙。小漢斯有時非常苦惱,因為怕他的花會以為他忘了它們,但他通過想著磨坊主是他最好的朋友來安慰自己。『而且,』他常說,『他要給我他的手推車,那是純粹慷慨的行為。』

passages.original: “So little Hans worked away for the Miller, and the Miller said all kinds of beautiful things about friendship, which Hans took down in a note-book, and used to read over at night, for he was a very good scholar.
passages.vernacular: 「於是小漢斯為磨坊主辛勤工作,磨坊主講咗各種關於友誼嘅美麗話語,漢斯把佢哋記喺筆記本裡,晚上常常重讀,因為佢係個好好嘅學生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「於是小漢斯為磨坊主辛勤工作,磨坊主說了各種關於友誼的美麗話語,漢斯把它們記在筆記本裡,晚上常常重讀,因為他是個很好的學生。

passages.original: “Now it happened that one evening little Hans was sitting by his fireside when a loud rap came at the door. It was a very wild night, and the wind was blowing and roaring round the house so terribly that at first he thought it was merely the storm. But a second rap came, and then a third, louder than any of the others.
passages.vernacular: 「有一天晚上,小漢斯正坐喺火爐邊,門上傳嚟一聲大響。嗰個係個狂風大作嘅夜晚,風喺屋子周圍呼嘯咆哮,咁可怕,起初佢以為嗰只係風暴。但第二下敲門嚟喇,然後係第三下,比其他嘅都響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有一天晚上,小漢斯正坐在火爐邊,門上傳來一聲大響。那是個狂風大作的夜晚,風在屋子周圍呼嘯咆哮,那麼可怕,起初他以為那只是風暴。但第二下敲門來了,然後是第三下,比其他的都響。

passages.original: “‘It is some poor traveller,’ said little Hans to himself, and he ran to the door.
passages.vernacular: 「『係某個可憐嘅旅人,』小漢斯對自己講,佢跑到門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『是某個可憐的旅人,』小漢斯對自己說,他跑到門口。

passages.original: “There stood the Miller with a lantern in one hand and a big stick in the other.
passages.vernacular: 「磨坊主站喺嗰度,一手提住燈籠,另一手攞住大棍子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「磨坊主站在那裡,一手提著燈籠,另一手拿著大棍子。

passages.original: “‘Dear little Hans,’ cried the Miller, ‘I am in great trouble. My little boy has fallen off a ladder and hurt himself, and I am going for the Doctor. But he lives so far away, and it is such a bad night, that it has just occurred to me that it would be much better if you went instead of me. You know I am going to give you my wheelbarrow, and so, it is only fair that you should do something for me in return.’
passages.vernacular: 「『親愛嘅小漢斯,』磨坊主喊道,『我遇到大麻煩喇。我嘅小兒子從梯子上摔下嚟受傷喇,我要去找醫生。但佢住得咁遠,夜晚咁糟,我剛想到,如果你替我去,會好得多。你知道我要畀你我嘅手推車,所以,你為我做點乜嘢作為回報,係公平嘅。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『親愛的小漢斯,』磨坊主喊道,『我遇到大麻煩了。我的小兒子從梯子上摔下來受傷了,我要去找醫生。但他住得那麼遠,夜晚這麼糟,我剛想到,如果你替我去,會好得多。你知道我要給你我的手推車,所以,你為我做點什麼作為回報,是公平的。』

passages.original: “‘Certainly,’ cried little Hans, ‘I take it quite as a compliment your coming to me, and I will start off at once. But you must lend me your lantern, as the night is so dark that I am afraid I might fall into the ditch.’
passages.vernacular: 「『當然,』小漢斯喊道,『你嚟找我,我把佢當作一種恭維,我即刻就出發。但你必須把你嘅燈籠借畀我,因為夜晚咁黑,我怕會掉進溝裡。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『當然,』小漢斯喊道,『你來找我,我把它當作一種恭維,我馬上就出發。但你必須把你的燈籠借給我,因為夜晚這麼黑,我怕會掉進溝裡。』

passages.original: “‘I am very sorry,’ answered the Miller, ‘but it is my new lantern, and it would be a great loss to me if anything happened to it.’
passages.vernacular: 「『我好抱歉,』磨坊主回答,『但佢係我嘅新燈籠,如果佢出咗乜嘢事,對我係好大嘅損失。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『我很抱歉,』磨坊主回答,『但它是我的新燈籠,如果它出了什麼事,對我是很大的損失。』

passages.original: “‘Well, never mind, I will do without it,’ cried little Hans, and he took down his great fur coat, and his warm scarlet cap, and tied a muffler round his throat, and started off.
passages.vernacular: 「『好吧,冇關係,我唔使佢,』小漢斯喊道,佢取下佢嘅大皮大衣同暖同嘅猩紅色帽子,喺喉嚨上繫咗一條圍巾,出發喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『好吧,沒關係,我不用它,』小漢斯喊道,他取下他的大皮大衣和暖和的猩紅色帽子,在喉嚨上繫了一條圍巾,出發了。

passages.original: “What a dreadful storm it was! The night was so black that little Hans could hardly see, and the wind was so strong that he could scarcely stand. However, he was very courageous, and after he had been walking about three hours, he arrived at the Doctor’s house, and knocked at the door.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係幾咁可怕嘅暴風雨!夜晚咁黑,小漢斯幾乎睇唔見,風咁強,佢幾乎站不住。不過,佢好勇敢,走咗大約三個小時後,佢到咗醫生家,敲咗門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是多麼可怕的暴風雨!夜晚那麼黑,小漢斯幾乎看不見,風那麼強,他幾乎站不住。不過,他非常勇敢,走了大約三個小時後,他到了醫生家,敲了門。

passages.original: “‘Who is there?’ cried the Doctor, putting his head out of his bedroom window.
passages.vernacular: 「『邊個喺嗰度?』醫生從臥室窗口探出頭喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『誰在那裡?』醫生從臥室窗口探出頭喊道。

passages.original: “‘Little Hans, Doctor.’
passages.vernacular: 「『小漢斯,醫生。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『小漢斯,醫生。』

passages.original: “’What do you want, little Hans?’
passages.vernacular: 「『你要乜嘢,小漢斯?』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你要什麼,小漢斯?』

passages.original: “‘The Miller’s son has fallen from a ladder, and has hurt himself, and the Miller wants you to come at once.’
passages.vernacular: 「『磨坊主嘅兒子從梯子上摔下嚟受傷喇,磨坊主要你即刻去。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『磨坊主的兒子從梯子上摔下來受傷了,磨坊主要你馬上去。』

passages.original: “‘All right!’ said the Doctor; and he ordered his horse, and his big boots, and his lantern, and came downstairs, and rode off in the direction of the Miller’s house, little Hans trudging behind him.
passages.vernacular: 「『好嘅!』醫生講;佢叫人備馬,穿上大靴子,攞住燈籠,下樓,騎馬向磨坊主家嘅方向去,小漢斯艱難地跟喺佢後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『好的!』醫生說;他叫人備馬,穿上大靴子,拿著燈籠,下樓,騎馬向磨坊主家的方向去,小漢斯艱難地跟在他後面。

passages.original: “But the storm grew worse and worse, and the rain fell in torrents, and little Hans could not see where he was going, or keep up with the horse. At last he lost his way, and wandered off on the moor, which was a very dangerous place, as it was full of deep holes, and there poor little Hans was drowned. His body was found the next day by some goatherds, floating in a great pool of water, and was brought back by them to the cottage.
passages.vernacular: 「但暴風雨越嚟越大,大雨傾盆,小漢斯睇唔見往邊度走,都跟不上馬。最後佢迷咗路,漫遊到荒原上,嗰個係個好危險嘅地方,滿係深洞,可憐嘅小漢斯就淹死喺嗰度。第二天佢嘅屍體被啲牧羊人發現,漂喺一大灘水裡,佢哋把佢帶回茅屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但暴風雨越來越大,大雨傾盆,小漢斯看不見往哪裡走,也跟不上馬。最後他迷了路,漫遊到荒原上,那是個非常危險的地方,滿是深洞,可憐的小漢斯就淹死在那裡。第二天他的屍體被一些牧羊人發現,漂在一大灘水裡,他們把他帶回茅屋。

passages.original: “Everybody went to little Hans’ funeral, as he was so popular, and the Miller was the chief mourner.
passages.vernacular: 「每個人都去參加小漢斯嘅葬禮,因為佢咁受歡迎,磨坊主係主要嘅送葬者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「每個人都去參加小漢斯的葬禮,因為他那麼受歡迎,磨坊主是主要的送葬者。

passages.original: “‘As I was his best friend,’ said the Miller, ‘it is only fair that I should have the best place’; so he walked at the head of the procession in a long black cloak, and every now and then he wiped his eyes with a big pocket-handkerchief.
passages.vernacular: 「『因為我係佢最好嘅朋友,』磨坊主講,『我應該有最好嘅位置才公平』;於是佢穿住長長嘅黑斗篷走喺送葬隊伍前面,不時用大手帕擦眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『因為我是他最好的朋友,』磨坊主說,『我應該有最好的位置才公平』;於是他穿著長長的黑斗篷走在送葬隊伍前面,不時用大手帕擦眼睛。

passages.original: “‘Little Hans is certainly a great loss to every one,’ said the Blacksmith, when the funeral was over, and they were all seated comfortably in the inn, drinking spiced wine and eating sweet cakes.
passages.vernacular: 「『小漢斯對每個人都係好大嘅損失,』葬禮結束後,鐵匠講,呢陣佢哋都舒服地坐喺客棧裡,飲住香料酒,食住甜點心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『小漢斯對每個人都是很大的損失,』葬禮結束後,鐵匠說,這時他們都舒服地坐在客棧裡,喝著香料酒,吃著甜點心。

passages.original: “‘A great loss to me at any rate,’ answered the Miller; ‘why, I had as good as given him my wheelbarrow, and now I really don’t know what to do with it. It is very much in my way at home, and it is in such bad repair that I could not get anything for it if I sold it. I will certainly take care not to give away anything again. One always suffers for being generous.’”
passages.vernacular: 「『無論如何對我係好大嘅損失,』磨坊主回答;『哎呀,我差不多已經把手推車畀佢喇,而家我真嘅唔知道該點處理佢。佢喺家裡好礙事,而且修得咁差,即使賣咗都得唔到乜嘢。我一定要小心,再都不送嘢喇。慷慨總是要食虧。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『無論如何對我是很大的損失,』磨坊主回答;『哎呀,我差不多已經把手推車給他了,現在我真的不知道該怎麼處理它。它在家裡很礙事,而且修得那麼差,即使賣了也得不到什麼。我一定要小心,再也不送東西了。慷慨總是要吃虧。』」

passages.original: “Well?” said the Water-rat, after a long pause.
passages.vernacular: 「然後呢?」水鼠停頓好久後講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後呢?」水鼠停頓很久後說。

passages.original: “Well, that is the end,” said the Linnet.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,就係結尾,」紅雀講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,就是結尾,」紅雀說。

passages.original: “But what became of the Miller?” asked the Water-rat.
passages.vernacular: 「但磨坊主後來點樣喇?」水鼠問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但磨坊主後來怎樣了?」水鼠問。

passages.original: “Oh! I really don’t know,” replied the Linnet; “and I am sure that I don’t care.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦!我真嘅唔知道,」紅雀回答;「而且我肯定我不在乎。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦!我真的不知道,」紅雀回答;「而且我肯定我不在乎。」

passages.original: “It is quite evident then that you have no sympathy in your nature,” said the Water-rat.
passages.vernacular: 「咁好明顯你嘅天性裡冇同情心,」水鼠講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼很明顯你的天性裡沒有同情心,」水鼠說。

passages.original: “I am afraid you don’t quite see the moral of the story,” remarked the Linnet.
passages.vernacular: 「我恐怕你冇完全睇出呢個故事嘅寓意,」紅雀講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我恐怕你沒有完全看出這個故事的寓意,」紅雀說。

passages.original: “The what?” screamed the Water-rat.
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢?」水鼠尖叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼?」水鼠尖叫。

passages.original: “The moral.”
passages.vernacular: 「寓意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「寓意。」

passages.original: “Do you mean to say that the story has a moral?”
passages.vernacular: 「你係講呢個故事有寓意?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是說這個故事有寓意?」

passages.original: “Certainly,” said the Linnet.
passages.vernacular: 「當然,」紅雀講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,」紅雀說。

passages.original: “Well, really,” said the Water-rat, in a very angry manner, “I think you should have told me that before you began. If you had done so, I certainly would not have listened to you; in fact, I should have said ‘Pooh,’ like the critic. However, I can say it now”; so he shouted out “Pooh” at the top of his voice, gave a whisk with his tail, and went back into his hole.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,真嘅,」水鼠好生氣地講,「我想你應該喺開始之前就告訴我。如果你咁樣做,我當然唔會聽你嘅;事實上,我會像嗰個評論家一樣講『呸』。不過,我而家可以講喇」;於是佢扯開嗓子大喊「呸」,甩咗一下尾巴,回到佢嘅洞裡去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,真的,」水鼠非常生氣地說,「我想你應該在開始之前就告訴我。如果你這樣做,我當然不會聽你的;事實上,我會像那個評論家一樣說『呸』。不過,我現在可以說了」;於是他扯開嗓子大喊「呸」,甩了一下尾巴,回到他的洞裡去了。

passages.original: “And how do you like the Water-rat?” asked the Duck, who came paddling up some minutes afterwards. “He has a great many good points, but for my own part I have a mother’s feelings, and I can never look at a confirmed bachelor without the tears coming into my eyes.”
passages.vernacular: 「你覺得水鼠點樣?」鴨子問,佢幾分鐘後划水游過嚟。「佢有好多優點,但就我自己而言,我有母親嘅情感,我睇到一個頑固嘅單身漢就禁不住眼淚湧上眼睛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你覺得水鼠怎麼樣?」鴨子問,她幾分鐘後划水游過來。「他有很多優點,但就我自己而言,我有母親的情感,我看到一個頑固的單身漢就禁不住眼淚湧上眼睛。」

passages.original: “I am rather afraid that I have annoyed him,” answered the Linnet. “The fact is, that I told him a story with a moral.”
passages.vernacular: 「我恐怕我惹惱咗佢,」紅雀回答。「事實係,我畀佢講咗一個有寓意嘅故事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我恐怕我惹惱了他,」紅雀回答。「事實是,我給他講了一個有寓意的故事。」

passages.original: “Ah! that is always a very dangerous thing to do,” said the Duck.
passages.vernacular: 「啊!呢總是一件好危險嘅事,」鴨子講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!這總是一件非常危險的事,」鴨子說。

passages.original: And I quite agree with her.
passages.vernacular: 我完全同意佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我完全同意她。

chapters.title: The Remarkable Rocket 了不起的火箭

passages.original: THE King’s son was going to be married, so there were general rejoicings. He had waited a whole year for his bride, and at last she had arrived. She was a Russian Princess, and had driven all the way from Finland in a sledge drawn by six reindeer. The sledge was shaped like a great golden swan, and between the swan’s wings lay the little Princess herself. Her long ermine-cloak reached right down to her feet, on her head was a tiny cap of silver tissue, and she was as pale as the Snow Palace in which she had always lived. So pale was she that as she drove through the streets all the people wondered. “She is like a white rose!” they cried, and they threw down flowers on her from the balconies.
passages.vernacular: 國王嘅兒子要結婚喇,所以到處一片歡慶。佢等佢嘅新娘等咗整整一年,佢終於到喇。佢係一位俄羅斯公主,從芬蘭一路乘住六頭馴鹿拉嘅雪橇嚟。雪橇嘅形狀像一隻巨大嘅金天鵝,小公主自己就躺喺天鵝嘅雙翼之間。佢嘅長貂皮斗篷一直垂到腳上,頭上戴住一頂銀色薄紗嘅小帽,佢蒼白得像佢一直住嘅雪宮。佢咁蒼白,佢乘車經過街道時,所有嘅人都感到驚奇。「佢像一朵白玫瑰!」佢哋喊道,從陽台上向佢拋下花朵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王的兒子要結婚了,所以到處一片歡慶。他等他的新娘等了整整一年,她終於到了。她是一位俄羅斯公主,從芬蘭一路乘著六頭馴鹿拉的雪橇來。雪橇的形狀像一隻巨大的金天鵝,小公主自己就躺在天鵝的雙翼之間。她的長貂皮斗篷一直垂到腳上,頭上戴著一頂銀色薄紗的小帽,她蒼白得像她一直住的雪宮。她那麼蒼白,她乘車經過街道時,所有的人都感到驚奇。「她像一朵白玫瑰!」他們喊道,從陽台上向她拋下花朵。

passages.original: At the gate of the Castle the Prince was waiting to receive her. He had dreamy violet eyes, and his hair was like fine gold. When he saw her he sank upon one knee, and kissed her hand.
passages.vernacular: 城堡門口王子喺等住迎接佢。佢有夢幻般嘅紫羅蘭色眼睛,頭髮像純金。佢睇到佢,單膝跪下,吻咗佢嘅手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 城堡門口王子在等著迎接她。他有夢幻般的紫羅蘭色眼睛,頭髮像純金。他看到她,單膝跪下,吻了她的手。

passages.original: “Your picture was beautiful,” he murmured, “but you are more beautiful than your picture”; and the little Princess blushed.
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅畫像好美,」佢低聲講,「但你比你嘅畫像更美」;小公主臉紅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的畫像很美,」他低聲說,「但你比你的畫像更美」;小公主臉紅了。

passages.original: “She was like a white rose before,” said a young Page to his neighbour, “but she is like a red rose now”; and the whole Court was delighted.
passages.vernacular: 「佢之前像一朵白玫瑰,」一個年輕侍從對旁邊嘅人講,「但佢而家像一朵紅玫瑰」;整個宮廷都好高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她之前像一朵白玫瑰,」一個年輕侍從對旁邊的人說,「但她現在像一朵紅玫瑰」;整個宮廷都很高興。

passages.original: For the next three days everybody went about saying, “White rose, Red rose, Red rose, White rose”; and the King gave orders that the Page’s salary was to be doubled. As he received no salary at all this was not of much use to him, but it was considered a great honour, and was duly published in the Court Gazette.
passages.vernacular: 接下嚟嘅三天,每個人都走嚟走去講住:「白玫瑰,紅玫瑰,紅玫瑰,白玫瑰」;國王下令把嗰個侍從嘅薪水加倍。由於佢根本冇薪水,呢對佢冇乜嘢用,但呢被認為係莫大嘅榮譽,並且正式刊登喺宮廷公報上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接下來的三天,每個人都走來走去說著:「白玫瑰,紅玫瑰,紅玫瑰,白玫瑰」;國王下令把那個侍從的薪水加倍。由於他根本沒有薪水,這對他沒什麼用,但這被認為是莫大的榮譽,並且正式刊登在宮廷公報上。

passages.original: When the three days were over the marriage was celebrated. It was a magnificent ceremony, and the bride and bridegroom walked hand in hand under a canopy of purple velvet embroidered with little pearls. Then there was a State Banquet, which lasted for five hours. The Prince and Princess sat at the top of the Great Hall and drank out of a cup of clear crystal. Only true lovers could drink out of this cup, for if false lips touched it, it grew grey and dull and cloudy.
passages.vernacular: 三天過後,婚禮舉行喇。嗰個係一場壯麗嘅儀式,新娘同新郎手牽手走喺綴滿小珍珠嘅紫色天鵝絨華蓋下。然後係國宴,持續咗五個小時。王子同公主坐喺大廳嘅上首,用一個透明水晶嘅杯子飲酒。只有真正嘅情人才能用呢個杯子飲,因為如果虛假嘅嘴唇碰到佢,佢會變得灰暗、無光、混濁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三天過後,婚禮舉行了。那是一場壯麗的儀式,新娘和新郎手牽手走在綴滿小珍珠的紫色天鵝絨華蓋下。然後是國宴,持續了五個小時。王子和公主坐在大廳的上首,用一個透明水晶的杯子喝酒。只有真正的情人才能用這個杯子喝,因為如果虛假的嘴唇碰到它,它會變得灰暗、無光、混濁。

passages.original: “It’s quite clear that they love each other,” said the little Page, “as clear as crystal!” and the King doubled his salary a second time. “What an honour!” cried all the courtiers.
passages.vernacular: 「好明顯佢哋彼此相愛,」小侍從講,「像水晶一樣清楚!」國王第二次把佢嘅薪水加倍。「幾咁榮耀!」所有朝臣喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很明顯他們彼此相愛,」小侍從說,「像水晶一樣清楚!」國王第二次把他的薪水加倍。「多麼榮耀!」所有朝臣喊道。

passages.original: After the banquet there was to be a Ball. The bride and bridegroom were to dance the Rose-dance together, and the King had promised to play the flute. He played very badly, but no one had ever dared to tell him so, because he was the King. Indeed, he knew only two airs, and was never quite certain which one he was playing; but it made no matter, for, whatever he did, everybody cried out, “Charming! charming!”
passages.vernacular: 宴會後有一場舞會。新娘同新郎要一起跳玫瑰舞,國王答應吹長笛。佢吹得好糟糕,但冇人敢告訴佢,因為佢係國王。事實上,佢只會兩首曲子,從來不太確定自己喺吹邊一首;但冇關係,因為不管佢點吹,每個人都喊:「迷人!迷人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 宴會後有一場舞會。新娘和新郎要一起跳玫瑰舞,國王答應吹長笛。他吹得很糟糕,但沒有人敢告訴他,因為他是國王。事實上,他只會兩首曲子,從來不太確定自己在吹哪一首;但沒關係,因為不管他怎麼吹,每個人都喊:「迷人!迷人!」

passages.original: The last item on the programme was a grand display of fireworks, to be let off exactly at midnight. The little Princess had never seen a firework in her life, so the King had given orders that the Royal Pyrotechnist should be in attendance on the day of her marriage.
passages.vernacular: 節目單上嘅最後一項係盛大嘅煙花表演,將喺午夜整點燃放。小公主呢輩子從冇見過煙花,所以國王下令皇家煙火師要喺佢婚禮嗰天在場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 節目單上的最後一項是盛大的煙花表演,將在午夜整點燃放。小公主這輩子從沒見過煙花,所以國王下令皇家煙火師要在她婚禮那天在場。

passages.original: “What are fireworks like?” she had asked the Prince, one morning, as she was walking on the terrace.
passages.vernacular: 「煙花係乜嘢樣嘅?」一天早晨佢喺露台上散步時問王子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「煙花是什麼樣的?」一天早晨她在露台上散步時問王子。

passages.original: “They are like the Aurora Borealis,” said the King, who always answered questions that were addressed to other people, “only much more natural. I prefer them to stars myself, as you always know when they are going to appear, and they are as delightful as my own flute-playing. You must certainly see them.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋像北極光,」國王講,佢總是回答別人問嘅問題,「只係自然得多。我自己更鍾意佢哋而唔係星星,因為你總是知道佢哋乜嘢時候會出現,而且佢哋像我吹長笛一樣令人愉快。你一定要睇睇佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它們像北極光,」國王說,他總是回答別人問的問題,「只是自然得多。我自己更喜歡它們而不是星星,因為你總是知道它們什麼時候會出現,而且它們像我吹長笛一樣令人愉快。你一定要看看它們。」

passages.original: So at the end of the King’s garden a great stand had been set up, and as soon as the Royal Pyrotechnist had put everything in its proper place, the fireworks began to talk to each other.
passages.vernacular: 於是喺國王花園嘅盡頭搭起咗一個大台子,皇家煙火師把一切放喺適當嘅位置後,煙花哋就開始互相交談。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是在國王花園的盡頭搭起了一個大台子,皇家煙火師把一切放在適當的位置後,煙花們就開始互相交談。

passages.original: “The world is certainly very beautiful,” cried a little Squib. “Just look at those yellow tulips. Why! if they were real crackers they could not be lovelier. I am very glad I have travelled. Travel improves the mind wonderfully, and does away with all one’s prejudices.”
passages.vernacular: 「世界確實好美麗,」一個小炮竹喊道。「睇睇嗰啲黃鬱金香。哎呀!如果佢哋係真嘅爆竹,都唔會更可愛喇。我好高興我旅行過。旅行奇妙地改善頭腦,並去除人所有嘅偏見。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「世界確實非常美麗,」一個小炮竹喊道。「看看那些黃鬱金香。哎呀!如果它們是真的爆竹,也不會更可愛了。我很高興我旅行過。旅行奇妙地改善頭腦,並去除人所有的偏見。」

passages.original: “The King’s garden is not the world, you foolish squib,” said a big Roman Candle; “the world is an enormous place, and it would take you three days to see it thoroughly.”
passages.vernacular: 「國王嘅花園唔係世界,你呢愚蠢嘅小炮竹,」一個大羅馬焰火筒講;「世界係個巨大嘅地方,你要花三天才能徹底睇完。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「國王的花園不是世界,你這愚蠢的小炮竹,」一個大羅馬焰火筒說;「世界是個巨大的地方,你要花三天才能徹底看完。」

passages.original: “Any place you love is the world to you,” exclaimed a pensive Catherine Wheel, who had been attached to an old deal box in early life, and prided herself on her broken heart; “but love is not fashionable any more, the poets have killed it. They wrote so much about it that nobody believed them, and I am not surprised. True love suffers, and is silent. I remember myself once—But it is no matter now. Romance is a thing of the past.”
passages.vernacular: 「你愛嘅任何地方對你來講就係世界,」一個深思嘅旋轉煙花輪喊道,佢早年曾依戀一個舊木箱,並以佢破碎嘅心為榮;「但愛情唔再流行喇,詩人把佢殺死喇。佢哋寫咗咁多,冇人再相信佢哋,我並不驚訝。真正嘅愛承受痛苦,並保持沉默。我自己記得有一次——但而家冇關係喇。浪漫已成過去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你愛的任何地方對你來說就是世界,」一個深思的旋轉煙花輪喊道,她早年曾依戀一個舊木箱,並以她破碎的心為榮;「但愛情不再流行了,詩人把它殺死了。他們寫了那麼多,沒有人再相信他們,我並不驚訝。真正的愛承受痛苦,並保持沉默。我自己記得有一次——但現在沒關係了。浪漫已成過去。」

passages.original: “Nonsense!” said the Roman Candle, “Romance never dies. It is like the moon, and lives for ever. The bride and bridegroom, for instance, love each other very dearly. I heard all about them this morning from a brown-paper cartridge, who happened to be staying in the same drawer as myself, and knew the latest Court news.”
passages.vernacular: 「胡講!」羅馬焰火筒講,「浪漫永不死亡。佢像月亮,永遠活住。例如,新娘同新郎好深愛彼此。我今日早晨從一個牛皮紙筒嗰度聽到咗佢哋嘅一切,佢碰巧同我住喺同一個抽屜裡,知道最新嘅宮廷新聞。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胡說!」羅馬焰火筒說,「浪漫永不死亡。它像月亮,永遠活著。例如,新娘和新郎非常深愛彼此。我今天早晨從一個牛皮紙筒那裡聽到了他們的一切,他碰巧和我住在同一個抽屜裡,知道最新的宮廷新聞。」

passages.original: But the Catherine Wheel shook her head. “Romance is dead, Romance is dead, Romance is dead,” she murmured. She was one of those people who think that, if you say the same thing over and over a great many times, it becomes true in the end.
passages.vernacular: 但旋轉煙花輪搖咗搖頭。「浪漫死喇,浪漫死喇,浪漫死喇,」佢喃喃講。佢係嗰種人,認為如果你把同一件事講好多遍,最後佢就會成真。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但旋轉煙花輪搖了搖頭。「浪漫死了,浪漫死了,浪漫死了,」她喃喃說。她是那種人,認為如果你把同一件事說很多遍,最後它就會成真。

passages.original: Suddenly, a sharp, dry cough was heard, and they all looked round.
passages.vernacular: 突然,聽到一聲尖銳乾澀嘅咳嗽,佢哋都轉過頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 突然,聽到一聲尖銳乾澀的咳嗽,他們都轉過頭。

passages.original: It came from a tall, supercilious-looking Rocket, who was tied to the end of a long stick. He always coughed before he made any observation, so as to attract attention.
passages.vernacular: 嗰來自一枚高高嘅睇起嚟傲慢嘅火箭,佢被綁喺一根長棍嘅末端。佢喺發表任何意見之前總是咳嗽,以吸引注意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那來自一枚高高的看起來傲慢的火箭,他被綁在一根長棍的末端。他在發表任何意見之前總是咳嗽,以吸引注意。

passages.original: “Ahem! ahem!” he said, and everybody listened except the poor Catherine Wheel, who was still shaking her head, and murmuring, “Romance is dead.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯哼!嗯哼!」佢講,除咗可憐嘅旋轉煙花輪,每個人都喺聽,佢仍喺搖頭,喃喃講:「浪漫死喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯哼!嗯哼!」他說,除了可憐的旋轉煙花輪,每個人都在聽,她仍在搖頭,喃喃說:「浪漫死了。」

passages.original: “Order! order!” cried out a Cracker. He was something of a politician, and had always taken a prominent part in the local elections, so he knew the proper Parliamentary expressions to use.
passages.vernacular: 「秩序!秩序!」一個爆竹喊道。佢有點像政客,總是喺地方選舉中扮演突出角色,所以佢知道該用嘅恰當嘅議會用語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「秩序!秩序!」一個爆竹喊道。他有點像政客,總是在地方選舉中扮演突出角色,所以他知道該用的恰當的議會用語。

passages.original: “Quite dead,” whispered the Catherine Wheel, and she went off to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 「完全死喇,」旋轉煙花輪低聲講,佢瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「完全死了,」旋轉煙花輪低聲說,她睡著了。

passages.original: As soon as there was perfect silence, the Rocket coughed a third time and began. He spoke with a very slow, distinct voice, as if he was dictating his memoirs, and always looked over the shoulder of the person to whom he was talking. In fact, he had a most distinguished manner.
passages.vernacular: 一旦完全安靜,火箭第三次咳嗽,開始喇。佢講話聲音好緩慢清晰,好像喺口述回憶錄,總是越過跟佢講話嘅人嘅肩膀睇。事實上,佢有一種最傑出嘅風度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一旦完全安靜,火箭第三次咳嗽,開始了。他說話聲音非常緩慢清晰,好像在口述回憶錄,總是越過跟他說話的人的肩膀看。事實上,他有一種最傑出的風度。

passages.original: “How fortunate it is for the King’s son,” he remarked, “that he is to be married on the very day on which I am to be let off. Really, if it had been arranged beforehand, it could not have turned out better for him; but, Princes are always lucky.”
passages.vernacular: 「對國王嘅兒子來講幾咁幸運,」佢講,「佢要喺我被點燃嘅同一天結婚。真嘅,如果事先安排,都唔會對佢更好喇;但係,王子哋總是幸運嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對國王的兒子來說多麼幸運,」他說,「他要在我被點燃的同一天結婚。真的,如果事先安排,也不會對他更好了;但是,王子們總是幸運的。」

passages.original: “Dear me!” said the little Squib, “I thought it was quite the other way, and that we were to be let off in the Prince’s honour.”
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!」小炮竹講,「我以為完全相反,我哋係要為王子嘅榮耀被點燃嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!」小炮竹說,「我以為完全相反,我們是要為王子的榮耀被點燃的。」

passages.original: “It may be so with you,” he answered; “indeed, I have no doubt that it is, but with me it is different. I am a very remarkable Rocket, and come of remarkable parents. My mother was the most celebrated Catherine Wheel of her day, and was renowned for her graceful dancing. When she made her great public appearance she spun round nineteen times before she went out, and each time that she did so she threw into the air seven pink stars. She was three feet and a half in diameter, and made of the very best gunpowder. My father was a Rocket like myself, and of French extraction. He flew so high that the people were afraid that he would never come down again. He did, though, for he was of a kindly disposition, and he made a most brilliant descent in a shower of golden rain. The newspapers wrote about his performance in very flattering terms. Indeed, the Court Gazette called him a triumph of Pylotechnic art.”
passages.vernacular: 「對你來講可能如此,」佢回答;「確實,我毫不懷疑係咁樣,但對我就不同喇。我係一枚好了不起嘅火箭,出身於了不起嘅父母。我母親係佢嗰個時代最著名嘅旋轉煙花輪,以優雅嘅舞蹈聞名。佢大規模公開亮相時,喺熄滅前旋轉咗十九圈,每次旋轉都向空中拋出七顆粉紅色嘅星星。佢嘅直徑有三呎半,用最好嘅火藥做成。我父親係像我一樣嘅火箭,有法國血統。佢飛得咁高,人哋怕佢再都唔會下嚟。不過佢下嚟喇,因為佢性情善良,佢以一陣金雨作咗一次最輝煌嘅降落。報紙用好讚美嘅詞語寫佢嘅表演。確實,宮廷公報稱佢係焰火藝術嘅勝利。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對你來說可能如此,」他回答;「確實,我毫不懷疑是這樣,但對我就不同了。我是一枚非常了不起的火箭,出身於了不起的父母。我母親是她那個時代最著名的旋轉煙花輪,以優雅的舞蹈聞名。她大規模公開亮相時,在熄滅前旋轉了十九圈,每次旋轉都向空中拋出七顆粉紅色的星星。她的直徑有三呎半,用最好的火藥做成。我父親是像我一樣的火箭,有法國血統。他飛得那麼高,人們怕他再也不會下來。不過他下來了,因為他性情善良,他以一陣金雨作了一次最輝煌的降落。報紙用非常讚美的詞語寫他的表演。確實,宮廷公報稱他是焰火藝術的勝利。」

passages.original: “Pyrotechnic, Pyrotechnic, you mean,” said a Bengal Light; “I know it is Pyrotechnic, for I saw it written on my own canister.”
passages.vernacular: 「係焰火,焰火,你嘅意思係,」一個孟加拉焰火講;「我知道係焰火,因為我睇到我自己嘅罐子上咁樣寫住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是焰火,焰火,你的意思是,」一個孟加拉焰火說;「我知道是焰火,因為我看到我自己的罐子上這樣寫著。」

passages.original: “Well, I said Pylotechnic,” answered the Rocket, in a severe tone of voice, and the Bengal Light felt so crushed that he began at once to bully the little squibs, in order to show that he was still a person of some importance.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我講嘅係焰火,」火箭用嚴厲嘅聲音回答,孟加拉焰火覺得被擊垮喇,即刻開始欺負小炮竹,以顯示佢仍係個有些重要性嘅人物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我說的是焰火,」火箭用嚴厲的聲音回答,孟加拉焰火覺得被擊垮了,馬上開始欺負小炮竹,以顯示他仍是個有些重要性的人物。

passages.original: “I was saying,” continued the Rocket, “I was saying—What was I saying?”
passages.vernacular: 「我頭先講,」火箭繼續講,「我頭先講——我頭先講乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我剛才說,」火箭繼續說,「我剛才說——我剛才說什麼?」

passages.original: “You were talking about yourself,” replied the Roman Candle.
passages.vernacular: 「你喺談論你自己,」羅馬焰火筒回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你在談論你自己,」羅馬焰火筒回答。

passages.original: “Of course; I knew I was discussing some interesting subject when I was so rudely interrupted. I hate rudeness and bad manners of every kind, for I am extremely sensitive. No one in the whole world is so sensitive as I am, I am quite sure of that.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然;我知道我喺討論某個有趣嘅話題,被咁無禮地打斷。我討厭任何種類嘅無禮同壞禮貌,因為我極其敏感。全世界冇人像我咁樣敏感,我對此好確定。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然;我知道我在討論某個有趣的話題,被這麼無禮地打斷。我討厭任何種類的無禮和壞禮貌,因為我極其敏感。全世界沒有人像我這樣敏感,我對此很確定。」

passages.original: “What is a sensitive person?” said the Cracker to the Roman Candle.
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢係敏感嘅人?」爆竹問羅馬焰火筒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼是敏感的人?」爆竹問羅馬焰火筒。

passages.original: “A person who, because he has corns himself, always treads on other people’s toes,” answered the Roman Candle in a low whisper; and the Cracker nearly exploded with laughter.
passages.vernacular: 「一個因為自己有雞眼,所以總是踩別人腳趾嘅人,」羅馬焰火筒低聲回答;爆竹幾乎笑爆喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一個因為自己有雞眼,所以總是踩別人腳趾的人,」羅馬焰火筒低聲回答;爆竹幾乎笑爆了。

passages.original: “Pray, what are you laughing at?” inquired the Rocket; “I am not laughing.”
passages.vernacular: 「請問,你喺笑乜嘢?」火箭問;「我冇笑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請問,你在笑什麼?」火箭問;「我沒笑。」

passages.original: “I am laughing because I am happy,” replied the Cracker.
passages.vernacular: 「我笑係因為我快樂,」爆竹回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我笑是因為我快樂,」爆竹回答。

passages.original: “That is a very selfish reason,” said the Rocket angrily. “What right have you to be happy? You should be thinking about others. In fact, you should be thinking about me. I am always thinking about myself, and I expect everybody else to do the same. That is what is called sympathy. It is a beautiful virtue, and I possess it in a high degree. Suppose, for instance, anything happened to me to-night, what a misfortune that would be for every one! The Prince and Princess would never be happy again, their whole married life would be spoiled; and as for the King, I know he would not get over it. Really, when I begin to reflect on the importance of my position, I am almost moved to tears.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係個好自私嘅理由,」火箭生氣地講。「你有乜嘢權利快樂?你應該想住別人。事實上,你應該想住我。我總是想住我自己,我期望其他每個人都咁樣。呢就叫同情。佢係美麗嘅美德,我喺好高嘅程度上擁有佢。比如講,假如今晚我出咗乜嘢事,對每個人係多大嘅不幸!王子同公主再都唔會快樂,佢哋嘅整個婚姻生活都會被毀;至於國王,我知道佢永遠唔會恢復過嚟。真嘅,當我開始思考我嘅地位嘅重要性時,我幾乎感動得要流淚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是個非常自私的理由,」火箭生氣地說。「你有什麼權利快樂?你應該想著別人。事實上,你應該想著我。我總是想著我自己,我期望其他每個人也這樣。這就叫同情。它是美麗的美德,我在很高的程度上擁有它。比如說,假如今晚我出了什麼事,對每個人是多大的不幸!王子和公主再也不會快樂,他們的整個婚姻生活都會被毀;至於國王,我知道他永遠不會恢復過來。真的,當我開始思考我的地位的重要性時,我幾乎感動得要流淚。」

passages.original: “If you want to give pleasure to others,” cried the Roman Candle, “you had better keep yourself dry.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你想畀別人帶嚟快樂,」羅馬焰火筒喊道,「你最好保持乾燥。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你想給別人帶來快樂,」羅馬焰火筒喊道,「你最好保持乾燥。」

passages.original: “Certainly,” exclaimed the Bengal Light, who was now in better spirits; “that is only common sense.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然,」孟加拉焰火喊道,佢而家精神好些喇;「嗰只係常識。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,」孟加拉焰火喊道,他現在精神好些了;「那只是常識。」

passages.original: “Common sense, indeed!” said the Rocket indignantly; “you forget that I am very uncommon, and very remarkable. Why, anybody can have common sense, provided that they have no imagination. But I have imagination, for I never think of things as they really are; I always think of them as being quite different. As for keeping myself dry, there is evidently no one here who can at all appreciate an emotional nature. Fortunately for myself, I don’t care. The only thing that sustains one through life is the consciousness of the immense inferiority of everybody else, and this is a feeling that I have always cultivated. But none of you have any hearts. Here you are laughing and making merry just as if the Prince and Princess had not just been married.”
passages.vernacular: 「常識,真嘅!」火箭憤慨地講;「你忘咗我係好不尋常、好了不起嘅。哎呀,任何人只要冇想像力,都可以有常識。但我有想像力,因為我從不按事物嘅真實面貌去想;我總是把佢哋想成完全不同。至於保持乾燥,呢度顯然冇一個人能欣賞一種感性嘅天性。對我自己幸運嘅係,我不在乎。唯一支持一個人度過一生嘅係對其他每個人嘅極大低劣嘅意識,而呢個係我一直培養嘅感覺。但你哋邊個都冇心。你哋喺呢度笑住、取樂,好像王子同公主啱啱冇結婚似嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「常識,真的!」火箭憤慨地說;「你忘了我是非常不尋常、非常了不起的。哎呀,任何人只要沒有想像力,都可以有常識。但我有想像力,因為我從不按事物的真實面貌去想;我總是把它們想成完全不同。至於保持乾燥,這裡顯然沒有一個人能欣賞一種感性的天性。對我自己幸運的是,我不在乎。唯一支持一個人度過一生的是對其他每個人的極大低劣的意識,而這是我一直培養的感覺。但你們誰也沒有心。你們在這裡笑著、取樂,好像王子和公主剛剛沒有結婚似的。」

passages.original: “Well, really,” exclaimed a small Fire-balloon, “why not? It is a most joyful occasion, and when I soar up into the air I intend to tell the stars all about it. You will see them twinkle when I talk to them about the pretty bride.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,真嘅,」一個小火氣球喊道,「點解不?呢個係一個最歡樂嘅場合,我升到空中時,打算把呢一切告訴星星。我同佢哋談起漂亮嘅新娘時,你會睇到佢哋閃爍。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,真的,」一個小火氣球喊道,「為什麼不?這是一個最歡樂的場合,我升到空中時,打算把這一切告訴星星。我同它們談起漂亮的新娘時,你會看到它們閃爍。」

passages.original: “Ah! what a trivial view of life!” said the Rocket; “but it is only what I expected. There is nothing in you; you are hollow and empty. Why, perhaps the Prince and Princess may go to live in a country where there is a deep river, and perhaps they may have one only son, a little fair-haired boy with violet eyes like the Prince himself; and perhaps some day he may go out to walk with his nurse; and perhaps the nurse may go to sleep under a great elder-tree; and perhaps the little boy may fall into the deep river and be drowned. What a terrible misfortune! Poor people, to lose their only son! It is really too dreadful! I shall never get over it.”
passages.vernacular: 「啊!幾咁瑣碎嘅人生觀!」火箭講;「但呢只係我預料到嘅。你裡面乜嘢都冇;你係空心嘅,空空如都。哎呀,或者王子同公主可能去住喺一個有深河嘅國家,或者佢哋可能只有一個獨生子,一個金髮嘅小男孩,像王子本人一樣有紫羅蘭色嘅眼睛;或者某天佢可能同佢嘅保姆出去散步;或者保姆可能喺一棵大接骨木樹下瞓住;或者小男孩可能掉進深河淹死。幾咁可怕嘅不幸!可憐嘅人,失去佢哋唯一嘅兒子!真係太可怕喇!我永遠唔會恢復過嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!多麼瑣碎的人生觀!」火箭說;「但這只是我預料到的。你裡面什麼也沒有;你是空心的,空空如也。哎呀,也許王子和公主可能去住在一個有深河的國家,也許他們可能只有一個獨生子,一個金髮的小男孩,像王子本人一樣有紫羅蘭色的眼睛;也許某天他可能同他的保姆出去散步;也許保姆可能在一棵大接骨木樹下睡著;也許小男孩可能掉進深河淹死。多麼可怕的不幸!可憐的人,失去他們唯一的兒子!真是太可怕了!我永遠不會恢復過來。」

passages.original: “But they have not lost their only son,” said the Roman Candle; “no misfortune has happened to them at all.”
passages.vernacular: 「但佢哋冇失去佢哋唯一嘅兒子,」羅馬焰火筒講;「佢哋根本冇遇到任何不幸。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但他們沒有失去他們唯一的兒子,」羅馬焰火筒說;「他們根本沒有遇到任何不幸。」

passages.original: “I never said that they had,” replied the Rocket; “I said that they might. If they had lost their only son there would be no use in saying anything more about the matter. I hate people who cry over spilt milk. But when I think that they might lose their only son, I certainly am very much affected.”
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇講佢哋失去喇,」火箭回答;「我講嘅係佢哋可能。如果佢哋失去咗獨生子,就冇必要再多講呢件事喇。我討厭嗰啲為打翻嘅牛奶哭泣嘅人。但當我想到佢哋可能失去獨生子時,我確實好受感動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒說他們失去了,」火箭回答;「我說的是他們可能。如果他們失去了獨生子,就沒有必要再多說這件事了。我討厭那些為打翻的牛奶哭泣的人。但當我想到他們可能失去獨生子時,我確實非常受感動。」

passages.original: “You certainly are!” cried the Bengal Light. “In fact, you are the most affected person I ever met.”
passages.vernacular: 「你確實係!」孟加拉焰火喊道。「事實上,你係我見過嘅最做作嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你確實是!」孟加拉焰火喊道。「事實上,你是我見過的最做作的人。」

passages.original: “You are the rudest person I ever met,” said the Rocket, “and you cannot understand my friendship for the Prince.”
passages.vernacular: 「你係我見過最無禮嘅人,」火箭講,「你唔能夠理解我對王子嘅友誼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是我見過最無禮的人,」火箭說,「你不能理解我對王子的友誼。」

passages.original: “Why, you don’t even know him,” growled the Roman Candle.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,你連佢都不認識,」羅馬焰火筒咆哮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,你連他也不認識,」羅馬焰火筒咆哮。

passages.original: “I never said I knew him,” answered the Rocket. “I dare say that if I knew him I should not be his friend at all. It is a very dangerous thing to know one’s friends.”
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇講我認識佢,」火箭回答。「我敢講如果我認識佢,我根本唔會成為佢嘅朋友。認識自己嘅朋友係好危險嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒說我認識他,」火箭回答。「我敢說如果我認識他,我根本不會成為他的朋友。認識自己的朋友是非常危險的事。」

passages.original: “You had really better keep yourself dry,” said the Fire-balloon. “That is the important thing.”
passages.vernacular: 「你真嘅最好保持乾燥,」火氣球講。「呢個係最重要嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真的最好保持乾燥,」火氣球說。「這是最重要的。」

passages.original: “Very important for you, I have no doubt,” answered the Rocket, “but I shall weep if I choose”; and he actually burst into real tears, which flowed down his stick like rain-drops, and nearly drowned two little beetles, who were just thinking of setting up house together, and were looking for a nice dry spot to live in.
passages.vernacular: 「對你好重要,我毫不懷疑,」火箭回答,「但如果我願意我就要哭」;佢真嘅爆出咗眼淚,像雨滴一樣沿住佢嘅棍子流下,差點淹死兩隻小甲蟲,牠哋正想一起安家,正在找一個好嘅乾燥地方住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對你很重要,我毫不懷疑,」火箭回答,「但如果我願意我就要哭」;他真的爆出了眼淚,像雨滴一樣沿著他的棍子流下,差點淹死兩隻小甲蟲,牠們正想一起安家,正在找一個好的乾燥地方住。

passages.original: “He must have a truly romantic nature,” said the Catherine Wheel, “for he weeps when there is nothing at all to weep about”; and she heaved a deep sigh, and thought about the deal box.
passages.vernacular: 「佢一定有一個真正浪漫嘅天性,」旋轉煙花輪講,「因為佢喺根本冇乜嘢值得哭嘅時候哭」;佢深深歎咗口氣,想起咗嗰個木箱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他一定有一個真正浪漫的天性,」旋轉煙花輪說,「因為他在根本沒有什麼值得哭的時候哭」;她深深歎了口氣,想起了那個木箱。

passages.original: But the Roman Candle and the Bengal Light were quite indignant, and kept saying, “Humbug! humbug!” at the top of their voices. They were extremely practical, and whenever they objected to anything they called it humbug.
passages.vernacular: 但羅馬焰火筒同孟加拉焰火相當憤慨,扯開嗓子不停地喊:「騙人!騙人!」佢哋極其實際,每當佢哋反對任何事,就稱之為騙人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但羅馬焰火筒和孟加拉焰火相當憤慨,扯開嗓子不停地喊:「騙人!騙人!」他們極其實際,每當他們反對任何事,就稱之為騙人。

passages.original: Then the moon rose like a wonderful silver shield; and the stars began to shine, and a sound of music came from the palace.
passages.vernacular: 然後月亮像一面奇妙嘅銀盾升起;星星開始閃耀,宮殿裡傳嚟音樂聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後月亮像一面奇妙的銀盾升起;星星開始閃耀,宮殿裡傳來音樂聲。

passages.original: The Prince and Princess were leading the dance. They danced so beautifully that the tall white lilies peeped in at the window and watched them, and the great red poppies nodded their heads and beat time.
passages.vernacular: 王子同公主喺領舞。佢哋跳得咁美,高高嘅白百合從窗口偷睇佢哋,大紅罌粟花點住頭打拍子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 王子和公主在領舞。他們跳得那麼美,高高的白百合從窗口偷看他們,大紅罌粟花點著頭打拍子。

passages.original: Then ten o’clock struck, and then eleven, and then twelve, and at the last stroke of midnight every one came out on the terrace, and the King sent for the Royal Pyrotechnist.
passages.vernacular: 然後十點鐘響,然後十啲,然後十二點,午夜最後一響時,每個人都嚟到露台上,國王派人叫皇家煙火師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後十點鐘響,然後十一點,然後十二點,午夜最後一響時,每個人都來到露台上,國王派人叫皇家煙火師。

passages.original: “Let the fireworks begin,” said the King; and the Royal Pyrotechnist made a low bow, and marched down to the end of the garden. He had six attendants with him, each of whom carried a lighted torch at the end of a long pole.
passages.vernacular: 「讓煙花開始吧,」國王講;皇家煙火師深深鞠躬,大步走到花園盡頭。佢帶住六個隨從,每人喺長竿嘅末端攞住一支點燃嘅火把。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓煙花開始吧,」國王說;皇家煙火師深深鞠躬,大步走到花園盡頭。他帶著六個隨從,每人在長竿的末端拿著一支點燃的火把。

passages.original: It was certainly a magnificent display.
passages.vernacular: 嗰確實係壯麗嘅表演。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那確實是壯麗的表演。

passages.original: Whizz! Whizz! went the Catherine Wheel, as she spun round and round. Boom! Boom! went the Roman Candle. Then the Squibs danced all over the place, and the Bengal Lights made everything look scarlet. “Good-bye,” cried the Fire-balloon, as he soared away, dropping tiny blue sparks. Bang! Bang! answered the Crackers, who were enjoying themselves immensely. Every one was a great success except the Remarkable Rocket. He was so damp with crying that he could not go off at all. The best thing in him was the gunpowder, and that was so wet with tears that it was of no use. All his poor relations, to whom he would never speak, except with a sneer, shot up into the sky like wonderful golden flowers with blossoms of fire. Huzza! Huzza! cried the Court; and the little Princess laughed with pleasure.
passages.vernacular: 嗖!嗖!旋轉煙花輪一圈一圈地轉住。砰!砰!羅馬焰火筒響住。然後小炮竹哋喺各處跳舞,孟加拉焰火把一切變成猩紅色。「再見,」火氣球喊道,佢飛走喇,落下細小嘅藍色火花。砰!砰!爆竹哋回應,佢哋玩得好開心。每個都大獲成功,除咗了不起嘅火箭。佢哭得太濕喇,根本點不住。佢身上最好嘅嘢係火藥,而佢被眼淚弄得咁濕,毫無用處。佢所有嘅窮親戚,佢從不同佢哋講話,除非係冷笑,像奇妙嘅金色花朵一樣帶住火焰嘅花朵射上咗天空。萬歲!萬歲!宮廷喊道;小公主高興地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗖!嗖!旋轉煙花輪一圈一圈地轉著。砰!砰!羅馬焰火筒響著。然後小炮竹們在各處跳舞,孟加拉焰火把一切變成猩紅色。「再見,」火氣球喊道,他飛走了,落下細小的藍色火花。砰!砰!爆竹們回應,他們玩得非常開心。每個都大獲成功,除了了不起的火箭。他哭得太濕了,根本點不著。他身上最好的東西是火藥,而它被眼淚弄得那麼濕,毫無用處。他所有的窮親戚,他從不同他們說話,除非是冷笑,像奇妙的金色花朵一樣帶著火焰的花朵射上了天空。萬歲!萬歲!宮廷喊道;小公主高興地笑了。

passages.original: “I suppose they are reserving me for some grand occasion,” said the Rocket; “no doubt that is what it means,” and he looked more supercilious than ever.
passages.vernacular: 「我想佢哋係把我留作某個盛大嘅場合,」火箭講;「毫無疑問,嗰個就係佢嘅意思,」佢睇起嚟比以往更傲慢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想他們是把我留作某個盛大的場合,」火箭說;「毫無疑問,那就是它的意思,」他看起來比以往更傲慢。

passages.original: The next day the workmen came to put everything tidy. “This is evidently a deputation,” said the Rocket; “I will receive them with becoming dignity” so he put his nose in the air, and began to frown severely as if he were thinking about some very important subject. But they took no notice of him at all till they were just going away. Then one of them caught sight of him. “Hallo!” he cried, “what a bad rocket!” and he threw him over the wall into the ditch.
passages.vernacular: 第二天,工人哋嚟把一切收拾整齊。「呢顯然係代表團,」火箭講;「我要以適當嘅尊嚴接見佢哋」於是佢把鼻子昂向空中,開始嚴厲地皺眉,好像喺思考某個好重要嘅問題。但佢哋根本冇理睬佢,直到佢哋快要離開。然後其中一個人睇到咗佢。「喂!」佢喊道,「多糟糕嘅火箭!」佢把佢扔過牆,扔進溝裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天,工人們來把一切收拾整齊。「這顯然是代表團,」火箭說;「我要以適當的尊嚴接見他們」於是他把鼻子昂向空中,開始嚴厲地皺眉,好像在思考某個非常重要的問題。但他們根本沒有理睬他,直到他們快要離開。然後其中一個人看到了他。「喂!」他喊道,「多糟糕的火箭!」他把他扔過牆,扔進溝裡。

passages.original: “BAD Rocket? BAD Rocket?” he said, as he whirled through the air; “impossible! GRAND Rocket, that is what the man said. BAD and GRAND sound very much the same, indeed they often are the same”; and he fell into the mud.
passages.vernacular: 「糟糕嘅火箭?糟糕嘅火箭?」佢喺空中旋轉時講;「唔可能!係了不起嘅火箭,嗰人講嘅係呢個。糟糕同了不起聽起嚟好相似,確實常常係一樣嘅」;佢掉進咗泥裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「糟糕的火箭?糟糕的火箭?」他在空中旋轉時說;「不可能!是了不起的火箭,那人說的是這個。糟糕和了不起聽起來非常相似,確實常常是一樣的」;他掉進了泥裡。

passages.original: “It is not comfortable here,” he remarked, “but no doubt it is some fashionable watering-place, and they have sent me away to recruit my health. My nerves are certainly very much shattered, and I require rest.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢度不舒服,」佢講,「但毫無疑問呢個係某個時髦嘅療養勝地,佢哋把我送嚟恢復健康。我嘅神經確實被嚴重震壞喇,我需要休息。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這裡不舒服,」他說,「但毫無疑問這是某個時髦的療養勝地,他們把我送來恢復健康。我的神經確實被嚴重震壞了,我需要休息。」

passages.original: Then a little Frog, with bright jewelled eyes, and a green mottled coat, swam up to him.
passages.vernacular: 然後一隻小青蛙,有明亮嘅寶石般嘅眼睛,穿住綠色斑點外衣,游到佢身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後一隻小青蛙,有明亮的寶石般的眼睛,穿著綠色斑點外衣,游到他身邊。

passages.original: “A new arrival, I see!” said the Frog. “Well, after all there is nothing like mud. Give me rainy weather and a ditch, and I am quite happy. Do you think it will be a wet afternoon? I am sure I hope so, but the sky is quite blue and cloudless. What a pity!”
passages.vernacular: 「我睇係新嚟嘅!」青蛙講。「嗯,畢竟冇乜嘢比得上泥。畀我雨天同一條溝,我就好快樂。你認為今日下午會下雨嗎?我肯定希望會,但天空好藍,冇雲。多可惜!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看是新來的!」青蛙說。「嗯,畢竟沒有什麼比得上泥。給我雨天和一條溝,我就非常快樂。你認為今天下午會下雨嗎?我肯定希望會,但天空很藍,沒有雲。多可惜!」

passages.original: “Ahem! ahem!” said the Rocket, and he began to cough.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯哼!嗯哼!」火箭講,開始咳嗽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯哼!嗯哼!」火箭說,開始咳嗽。

passages.original: “What a delightful voice you have!” cried the Frog. “Really it is quite like a croak, and croaking is of course the most musical sound in the world. You will hear our glee-club this evening. We sit in the old duck pond close by the farmer’s house, and as soon as the moon rises we begin. It is so entrancing that everybody lies awake to listen to us. In fact, it was only yesterday that I heard the farmer’s wife say to her mother that she could not get a wink of sleep at night on account of us. It is most gratifying to find oneself so popular.”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅聲音幾咁悅耳!」青蛙喊道。「真嘅好像呱呱叫,呱呱叫當然係世界上最有音樂感嘅聲音。你今晚會聽到我哋嘅合唱團。我哋坐喺農夫房子旁邊嘅老鴨塘裡,月亮一升起我哋就開始。佢咁迷人,每個人都醒住聽我哋。事實上,就喺尋日,我聽到農夫嘅妻子對佢母親講,因為我哋,佢晚上啲都瞓不住。發現自己咁受歡迎真令人好滿意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的聲音多麼悅耳!」青蛙喊道。「真的很像呱呱叫,呱呱叫當然是世界上最有音樂感的聲音。你今晚會聽到我們的合唱團。我們坐在農夫房子旁邊的老鴨塘裡,月亮一升起我們就開始。它那麼迷人,每個人都醒著聽我們。事實上,就在昨天,我聽到農夫的妻子對她母親說,因為我們,她晚上一點也睡不著。發現自己這麼受歡迎真令人非常滿意。」

passages.original: “Ahem! ahem!” said the Rocket angrily. He was very much annoyed that he could not get a word in.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯哼!嗯哼!」火箭生氣地講。佢好惱火,因為插不上一句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯哼!嗯哼!」火箭生氣地說。他非常惱火,因為插不上一句話。

passages.original: “A delightful voice, certainly,” continued the Frog; “I hope you will come over to the duck-pond. I am off to look for my daughters. I have six beautiful daughters, and I am so afraid the Pike may meet them. He is a perfect monster, and would have no hesitation in breakfasting off them. Well, good-bye: I have enjoyed our conversation very much, I assure you.”
passages.vernacular: 「確實係悅耳嘅聲音,」青蛙繼續講;「我希望你會到鴨塘嚟。我要去找我嘅女兒哋。我有六個美麗嘅女兒,我好怕梭子魚遇到佢哋。佢係個十足嘅怪物,會毫不猶豫地把佢哋當早餐食喇。好喇,再見:我向你保證我好享受我哋嘅談話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「確實是悅耳的聲音,」青蛙繼續說;「我希望你會到鴨塘來。我要去找我的女兒們。我有六個美麗的女兒,我非常怕梭子魚遇到她們。他是個十足的怪物,會毫不猶豫地把她們當早餐吃了。好了,再見:我向你保證我非常享受我們的談話。」

passages.original: “Conversation, indeed!” said the Rocket. “You have talked the whole time yourself. That is not conversation.”
passages.vernacular: 「談話,真嘅!」火箭講。「整個時間都係你自己喺講。嗰唔係談話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「談話,真的!」火箭說。「整個時間都是你自己在說。那不是談話。」

passages.original: “Somebody must listen,” answered the Frog, “and I like to do all the talking myself. It saves time, and prevents arguments.”
passages.vernacular: 「總得有人聽,」青蛙回答,「我鍾意自己講所有嘅話。佢節省時間,防止爭論。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「總得有人聽,」青蛙回答,「我喜歡自己說所有的話。它節省時間,防止爭論。」

passages.original: “But I like arguments,” said the Rocket.
passages.vernacular: 「但我鍾意爭論,」火箭講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我喜歡爭論,」火箭說。

passages.original: “I hope not,” said the Frog complacently. “Arguments are extremely vulgar, for everybody in good society holds exactly the same opinions. Good-bye a second time; I see my daughters in the distance:” and the little Frog swam away.
passages.vernacular: 「我希望唔係,」青蛙自滿地講。「爭論極其庸俗,因為上流社會嘅每個人持嘅意見都完全一樣。再講一次再見;我睇到我嘅女兒哋喺遠處喇:」小青蛙游走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望不是,」青蛙自滿地說。「爭論極其庸俗,因為上流社會的每個人持的意見都完全一樣。再說一次再見;我看到我的女兒們在遠處了:」小青蛙游走了。

passages.original: “You are a very irritating person,” said the Rocket, “and very ill-bred. I hate people who talk about themselves, as you do, when one wants to talk about oneself, as I do. It is what I call selfishness, and selfishness is a most detestable thing, especially to any one of my temperament, for I am well known for my sympathetic nature. In fact, you should take example by me; you could not possibly have a better model. Now that you have the chance you had better avail yourself of it, for I am going back to Court almost immediately. I am a great favourite at Court; in fact, the Prince and Princess were married yesterday in my honour. Of course you know nothing of these matters, for you are a provincial.”
passages.vernacular: 「你係個好令人惱火嘅人,」火箭講,「而且教養好差。我討厭嗰啲像你一樣談論自己嘅人,而一個人想像我咁樣談論自己。呢個就係我所稱嘅自私,而自私係最可憎嘅嘢,尤其係對我呢種氣質嘅人來講,因為我以富同情心嘅天性而聞名。事實上,你應該以我為榜樣;你唔可能有更好嘅榜樣喇。而家你有機會,你最好利用佢,因為我幾乎即刻要回宮廷去。我喺宮廷係個大紅人;事實上,王子同公主尋日為了向我致敬而結婚。當然你對呢啲事一無所知,因為你係個鄉下人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是個非常令人惱火的人,」火箭說,「而且教養很差。我討厭那些像你一樣談論自己的人,而一個人想像我這樣談論自己。這就是我所稱的自私,而自私是最可憎的東西,尤其是對我這種氣質的人來說,因為我以富同情心的天性而聞名。事實上,你應該以我為榜樣;你不可能有更好的榜樣了。現在你有機會,你最好利用它,因為我幾乎馬上要回宮廷去。我在宮廷是個大紅人;事實上,王子和公主昨天為了向我致敬而結婚。當然你對這些事一無所知,因為你是個鄉下人。」

passages.original: “There is no good talking to him,” said a Dragon-fly, who was sitting on the top of a large brown bulrush; “no good at all, for he has gone away.”
passages.vernacular: 「同佢講話冇好處,」一隻蜻蜓講,牠坐喺一根大棕色蒲草嘅頂上;「啲好處都冇,因為佢已經走喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同他說話沒好處,」一隻蜻蜓說,牠坐在一根大棕色蒲草的頂上;「一點好處也沒有,因為他已經走了。」

passages.original: “Well, that is his loss, not mine,” answered the Rocket. “I am not going to stop talking to him merely because he pays no attention. I like hearing myself talk. It is one of my greatest pleasures. I often have long conversations all by myself, and I am so clever that sometimes I don’t understand a single word of what I am saying.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰個係佢嘅損失,唔係我嘅,」火箭回答。「我唔會僅僅因為佢不理睬就停止同佢講話。我鍾意聽自己講話。呢個係我最大嘅樂趣之一。我常常自己進行長篇談話,我咁聰明,有時連我自己講嘅一個字都不懂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那是他的損失,不是我的,」火箭回答。「我不會僅僅因為他不理睬就停止同他說話。我喜歡聽自己說話。這是我最大的樂趣之一。我常常自己進行長篇談話,我那麼聰明,有時連我自己說的一個字也不懂。」

passages.original: “Then you should certainly lecture on Philosophy,” said the Dragon-fly; and he spread a pair of lovely gauze wings and soared away into the sky.
passages.vernacular: 「咁你一定該講授哲學,」蜻蜓講;牠展開一雙可愛嘅薄紗翅膀,飛向天空。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼你一定該講授哲學,」蜻蜓說;牠展開一雙可愛的薄紗翅膀,飛向天空。

passages.original: “How very silly of him not to stay here!” said the Rocket. “I am sure that he has not often got such a chance of improving his mind. However, I don’t care a bit. Genius like mine is sure to be appreciated some day”; and he sank down a little deeper into the mud.
passages.vernacular: 「佢不留喺呢度真係太蠢喇!」火箭講。「我肯定佢不常有咁樣改善頭腦嘅機會。不過,我啲都不在乎。像我咁樣嘅天才總有一天一定會得到賞識」;佢往泥裡沉得更深咗啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他不留在這裡真是太蠢了!」火箭說。「我肯定他不常有這樣改善頭腦的機會。不過,我一點也不在乎。像我這樣的天才總有一天一定會得到賞識」;他往泥裡沉得更深了一點。

passages.original: After some time a large White Duck swam up to him. She had yellow legs, and webbed feet, and was considered a great beauty on account of her waddle.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒,一隻大白鴨游到佢身邊。佢有黃色嘅腿同蹼足,因為佢搖搖擺擺嘅走路,被認為係大美人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒,一隻大白鴨游到他身邊。她有黃色的腿和蹼足,因為她搖搖擺擺的走路,被認為是大美人。

passages.original: “Quack, quack, quack,” she said. “What a curious shape you are! May I ask were you born like that, or is it the result of an accident?”
passages.vernacular: 「呱,呱,呱,」佢講。「你嘅形狀幾咁奇特!請問你生來就係咁樣,定係意外嘅結果?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「呱,呱,呱,」她說。「你的形狀多麼奇特!請問你生來就是這樣,還是意外的結果?」

passages.original: “It is quite evident that you have always lived in the country,” answered the Rocket, “otherwise you would know who I am. However, I excuse your ignorance. It would be unfair to expect other people to be as remarkable as oneself. You will no doubt be surprised to hear that I can fly up into the sky, and come down in a shower of golden rain.”
passages.vernacular: 「好明顯你一直住喺鄉下,」火箭回答,「否則你會知道我係邊個。不過,我原諒你嘅無知。期望別人像自己一樣了不起係不公平嘅。你聽到我能飛向天空,以一陣金雨降落,無疑會感到驚訝。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很明顯你一直住在鄉下,」火箭回答,「否則你會知道我是誰。不過,我原諒你的無知。期望別人像自己一樣了不起是不公平的。你聽到我能飛向天空,以一陣金雨降落,無疑會感到驚訝。」

passages.original: “I don’t think much of that,” said the Duck, “as I cannot see what use it is to any one. Now, if you could plough the fields like the ox, or draw a cart like the horse, or look after the sheep like the collie-dog, that would be something.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不覺得嗰有乜嘢了不起,」鴨子講,「因為我睇不出佢對任何人有乜嘢用。而家,如果你能像牛一樣犁田,或像馬一樣拉車,或像牧羊犬一樣照睇羊,嗰才算點乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不覺得那有什麼了不起,」鴨子說,「因為我看不出它對任何人有什麼用。現在,如果你能像牛一樣犁田,或像馬一樣拉車,或像牧羊犬一樣照看羊,那才算點什麼。」

passages.original: “My good creature,” cried the Rocket in a very haughty tone of voice, “I see that you belong to the lower orders. A person of my position is never useful. We have certain accomplishments, and that is more than sufficient. I have no sympathy myself with industry of any kind, least of all with such industries as you seem to recommend. Indeed, I have always been of opinion that hard work is simply the refuge of people who have nothing whatever to do.”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅好傢伙,」火箭用好傲慢嘅聲音喊道,「我睇出你屬於下等階層。像我呢種地位嘅人從不有用。我哋有某些才藝,嗰就綽綽有餘喇。我自己對任何種類嘅勤勞都冇同情,對你似乎推薦嘅嗰種勤勞更係如此。確實,我一直認為努力工作只係無事可做嘅人嘅避難所。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的好傢伙,」火箭用非常傲慢的聲音喊道,「我看出你屬於下等階層。像我這種地位的人從不有用。我們有某些才藝,那就綽綽有餘了。我自己對任何種類的勤勞都沒有同情,對你似乎推薦的那種勤勞更是如此。確實,我一直認為努力工作只是無事可做的人的避難所。」

passages.original: “Well, well,” said the Duck, who was of a very peaceable disposition, and never quarrelled with any one, “everybody has different tastes. I hope, at any rate, that you are going to take up your residence here.”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,好吧,」鴨子講,佢性情好平和,從不同任何人爭吵,「每個人品味不同。我希望,無論如何,你打算喺呢度定居。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,好吧,」鴨子說,她性情非常平和,從不同任何人爭吵,「每個人品味不同。我希望,無論如何,你打算在這裡定居。」

passages.original: “Oh! dear no,” cried the Rocket. “I am merely a visitor, a distinguished visitor. The fact is that I find this place rather tedious. There is neither society here, nor solitude. In fact, it is essentially suburban. I shall probably go back to Court, for I know that I am destined to make a sensation in the world.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦!當然不,」火箭喊道。「我只係個訪客,一個傑出嘅訪客。事實係我覺得呢個地方相當乏味。呢度既冇社交,都冇孤獨。事實上,佢本質上係郊區。我大概會回宮廷去,因為我知道我註定要在世界上引起轟動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦!當然不,」火箭喊道。「我只是個訪客,一個傑出的訪客。事實是我覺得這個地方相當乏味。這裡既沒有社交,也沒有孤獨。事實上,它本質上是郊區。我大概會回宮廷去,因為我知道我註定要在世界上引起轟動。」

passages.original: “I had thoughts of entering public life once myself,” remarked the Duck; “there are so many things that need reforming. Indeed, I took the chair at a meeting some time ago, and we passed resolutions condemning everything that we did not like. However, they did not seem to have much effect. Now I go in for domesticity, and look after my family.”
passages.vernacular: 「我自己曾經都想過進入公共生活,」鴨子講;「有咁多事需要改革。確實,不久前我主持過一次會議,我哋通過咗決議,譴責所有我哋不鍾意嘅事。不過,佢哋似乎冇乜嘢效果。而家我專心於家庭生活,照顧我嘅家人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我自己曾經也想過進入公共生活,」鴨子說;「有那麼多事需要改革。確實,不久前我主持過一次會議,我們通過了決議,譴責所有我們不喜歡的事。不過,它們似乎沒什麼效果。現在我專心於家庭生活,照顧我的家人。」

passages.original: “I am made for public life,” said the Rocket, “and so are all my relations, even the humblest of them. Whenever we appear we excite great attention. I have not actually appeared myself, but when I do so it will be a magnificent sight. As for domesticity, it ages one rapidly, and distracts one’s mind from higher things.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係為公共生活而生嘅,」火箭講,「我所有嘅親戚都係,連最卑微嘅都係。我哋無論喺邊度出現,都會引起極大嘅注意。我自己仲冇真正出現過,但我出現時會係壯麗嘅景象。至於家庭生活,佢使人迅速變老,並使人嘅心思從更高嘅事物上分散。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是為公共生活而生的,」火箭說,「我所有的親戚也是,連最卑微的也是。我們無論在哪裡出現,都會引起極大的注意。我自己還沒有真正出現過,但我出現時會是壯麗的景象。至於家庭生活,它使人迅速變老,並使人的心思從更高的事物上分散。」

passages.original: “Ah! the higher things of life, how fine they are!” said the Duck; “and that reminds me how hungry I feel”: and she swam away down the stream, saying, “Quack, quack, quack.”
passages.vernacular: 「啊!生活中更高嘅事物,幾咁美好!」鴨子講;「呢使我想起我覺得多餓」:佢沿住溪流游走,講住:「呱,呱,呱。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊!生活中更高的事物,多麼美好!」鴨子說;「這使我想起我覺得多餓」:她沿著溪流游走,說著:「呱,呱,呱。」

passages.original: “Come back! come back!” screamed the Rocket, “I have a great deal to say to you”; but the Duck paid no attention to him. “I am glad that she has gone,” he said to himself, “she has a decidedly middle-class mind”; and he sank a little deeper still into the mud, and began to think about the loneliness of genius, when suddenly two little boys in white smocks came running down the bank, with a kettle and some faggots.
passages.vernacular: 「回嚟!回嚟!」火箭尖叫,「我有好多話要對你講」;但鴨子不理佢。「我好高興佢走喇,」佢對自己講,「佢明顯有中產階級嘅頭腦」;佢又往泥裡沉得更深啲,開始思考天才嘅孤獨,呢陣突然兩個穿白罩衫嘅小男孩帶住水壺同啲柴捆跑下河岸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「回來!回來!」火箭尖叫,「我有很多話要對你說」;但鴨子不理他。「我很高興她走了,」他對自己說,「她明顯有中產階級的頭腦」;他又往泥裡沉得更深一點,開始思考天才的孤獨,這時突然兩個穿白罩衫的小男孩帶著水壺和一些柴捆跑下河岸。

passages.original: “This must be the deputation,” said the Rocket, and he tried to look very dignified.
passages.vernacular: 「呢一定係代表團,」火箭講,佢試圖顯得好有尊嚴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這一定是代表團,」火箭說,他試圖顯得很有尊嚴。

passages.original: “Hallo!” cried one of the boys, “look at this old stick! I wonder how it came here”; and he picked the rocket out of the ditch.
passages.vernacular: 「喂!」一個男孩喊道,「睇呢根舊棍子!我想知道佢點到呢度嘅」;佢把火箭從溝裡撿起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂!」一個男孩喊道,「看這根舊棍子!我想知道它怎麼到這裡的」;他把火箭從溝裡撿起來。

passages.original: “OLD Stick!” said the Rocket, “impossible! GOLD Stick, that is what he said. Gold Stick is very complimentary. In fact, he mistakes me for one of the Court dignitaries!”
passages.vernacular: 「舊棍子!」火箭講,「唔可能!係金棍,佢講嘅係呢個。金棍係好恭維嘅。事實上,佢把我誤認為宮廷顯貴之一喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「舊棍子!」火箭說,「不可能!是金棍,他說的是這個。金棍是很恭維的。事實上,他把我誤認為宮廷顯貴之一了!」

passages.original: “Let us put it into the fire!” said the other boy, “it will help to boil the kettle.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋把佢放進火裡!」另一個男孩講,「佢能幫助把水壺燒開。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們把它放進火裡!」另一個男孩說,「它能幫助把水壺燒開。」

passages.original: So they piled the faggots together, and put the Rocket on top, and lit the fire.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋把柴捆堆喺一起,把火箭放喺上面,點住咗火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們把柴捆堆在一起,把火箭放在上面,點著了火。

passages.original: “This is magnificent,” cried the Rocket, “they are going to let me off in broad day-light, so that every one can see me.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢太壯麗喇,」火箭喊道,「佢哋要喺大白天點燃我,咁樣每個人都能睇到我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這太壯麗了,」火箭喊道,「他們要在大白天點燃我,這樣每個人都能看到我。」

passages.original: “We will go to sleep now,” they said, “and when we wake up the kettle will be boiled”; and they lay down on the grass, and shut their eyes.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋而家去瞓覺,」佢哋講,「等我哋醒嚟水壺就燒開喇」;佢哋躺喺草地上,閉上咗眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們現在去睡覺,」他們說,「等我們醒來水壺就燒開了」;他們躺在草地上,閉上了眼睛。

passages.original: The Rocket was very damp, so he took a long time to burn. At last, however, the fire caught him.
passages.vernacular: 火箭好潮濕,所以佢花咗好長時間才燒起嚟。不過最後火點住咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 火箭很潮濕,所以他花了很長時間才燒起來。不過最後火點著了他。

passages.original: “Now I am going off!” he cried, and he made himself very stiff and straight. “I know I shall go much higher than the stars, much higher than the moon, much higher than the sun. In fact, I shall go so high that—”
passages.vernacular: 「而家我要發射喇!」佢喊道,把自己弄得好僵硬好直。「我知道我會飛得比星星高得多,比月亮高得多,比太陽高得多。事實上,我會飛得咁高,以致——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在我要發射了!」他喊道,把自己弄得很僵硬很直。「我知道我會飛得比星星高得多,比月亮高得多,比太陽高得多。事實上,我會飛得那麼高,以致——」

passages.original: Fizz! Fizz! Fizz! and he went straight up into the air.
passages.vernacular: 嘶嘶!嘶嘶!嘶嘶!佢直直地衝上咗空中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嘶嘶!嘶嘶!嘶嘶!他直直地衝上了空中。

passages.original: “Delightful!” he cried, “I shall go on like this for ever. What a success I am!”
passages.vernacular: 「太美妙喇!」佢喊道,「我會永遠咁樣飛下去。我係幾咁成功!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太美妙了!」他喊道,「我會永遠這樣飛下去。我是多麼成功!」

passages.original: But nobody saw him.
passages.vernacular: 但冇人睇見佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但沒有人看見他。

passages.original: Then he began to feel a curious tingling sensation all over him.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢開始感到全身有一種奇怪嘅刺痛感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他開始感到全身有一種奇怪的刺痛感。

passages.original: “Now I am going to explode,” he cried. “I shall set the whole world on fire, and make such a noise that nobody will talk about anything else for a whole year.” And he certainly did explode. Bang! Bang! Bang! went the gunpowder. There was no doubt about it.
passages.vernacular: 「而家我要爆炸喇,」佢喊道。「我會讓整個世界住火,發出咁大嘅聲響,整整一年冇人會談論別嘅事。」佢確實爆炸喇。砰!砰!砰!火藥響喇。呢毫無疑問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在我要爆炸了,」他喊道。「我會讓整個世界著火,發出那麼大的聲響,整整一年沒有人會談論別的事。」他確實爆炸了。砰!砰!砰!火藥響了。這毫無疑問。

passages.original: But nobody heard him, not even the two little boys, for they were sound asleep.
passages.vernacular: 但冇人聽見佢,連兩個小男孩都冇,因為佢哋瞓得好沉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但沒有人聽見他,連兩個小男孩也沒有,因為他們睡得很沉。

passages.original: Then all that was left of him was the stick, and this fell down on the back of a Goose who was taking a walk by the side of the ditch.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢剩下嘅只有嗰根棍子,佢掉喺一隻正在溝邊散步嘅鵝嘅背上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他剩下的只有那根棍子,它掉在一隻正在溝邊散步的鵝的背上。

passages.original: “Good heavens!” cried the Goose. “It is going to rain sticks”; and she rushed into the water.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!」鵝喊道。「要下棍子雨喇」;佢衝進咗水裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!」鵝喊道。「要下棍子雨了」;她衝進了水裡。

passages.original: “I knew I should create a great sensation,” gasped the Rocket, and he went out.
passages.vernacular: 「我就知道我會引起大轟動,」火箭喘住氣講,然後佢熄滅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就知道我會引起大轟動,」火箭喘著氣說,然後他熄滅了。
